OPEN — `0x00600720`'s own deep internals, per above.]**

### 9.20 `inv_weapon_disable_all_slots` (`0x00a51450`)

**Arguments:** 1 mandatory boolean, read unconditionally with no presence/nil check — an
enable/disable-all state. + 1 optional numeric/flag value, default `3` (the SAME recurring
default literal §9.2/§1.1-of-this-document's-own-§1-cluster already document).

**Return:** none (`return 0;`).

**Body:** both values are handed to a single dispatch (`0x007f4890`) that splits on two
individual bits of the flag byte, structurally parallel to `effect_stop`'s own dispatch
(§9.2, `0x005cfe00`): bit `0x2` opens the record-and-replicate idiom, opcode `0x40` (**not
unique to this function — the identical literal opcode `0x40` is independently used by
`waypoint_remove`, §6.17/§6.22, for a completely unrelated record; both individual claims are
confirmed by decompile, this is not a contradiction, just a cross-reference the running opcode
census should carry**), recording the raw bool and
a literal record-type tag of `0x1a` (26); bit `0x1` instead builds a small local lookup — the
input bool byte is broadcast (via a multiply-by-`0x1010101` idiom) across three consecutive
32-bit words, i.e. 12 identical byte-sized entries, all holding the SAME input bool value rather
than any real per-category data — and indexes it by the current local-player character's own
currently-equipped-weapon category byte (read off the SAME `+0x54`-offset category field
`inv_item_equip`'s own weapon-category derivation reads, §9.19, reached via the SAME "get
local-player object" zero-argument getter `camera_restrict_set_active`
(`spec-lua-api-behaviour.md` §8.12) also consults, `0x009da4e0`). Since the lookup is a
uniform broadcast rather than a genuine table, the
net effect is simply: "if the disable/enable-all bool is true (or false) AND the local player
currently has an equipped weapon, re-run the SAME generic active-item apply routine
`inv_item_equip`'s own no-item-given path enters" (`0x00600720`, literal selector `0`, §9.19) —
i.e. force a re-evaluation of the currently-equipped weapon under the new all-slots state.

**Side effects / subsystem:** network-replicates the raw enable/disable-all bool and flag value
(opcode `0x40`) when flag bit `0x2` is set, and — when flag bit `0x1` is set and the local player
currently has an equipped weapon — forces that weapon through the SAME generic active-item
apply routine `inv_item_equip` (§9.19) uses. Subsystem: inventory/weapon-selection. **[CONFIRMED
— disassembly for both flag-bit branches, the broadcast-fill arithmetic (confirmed to reduce to
a uniform value, not a real per-category table), and the shared category-field/apply-routine
identity with `inv_item_equip`; OPEN — the flag value's remaining bits and the exact real-world
meaning of record tag `0x1a`.]**

### 9.21 Cross-function observations

**The type-gated resolver family's underlying descriptor table is far more heavily reused than
§4.13's own five bit/offset sightings suggested.** This cluster alone adds ~~at least seven~~ four new
further confirmed bit/offset combinations (plus a further sighting of bit `0x8`@`+0xb`) read off the SAME per-object-type descriptor table
(indexed by an object's own type-id byte, address `0x02cc9900`) that §4.13's resolver family
already uses at offsets `+0xa`/`+0xb`: bit `0x1` at offset `+7` (`effect_stop`'s local-apply
gate, §9.2); bit `0x4` at offset `+10` (`vehicle_chase`'s per-occupant notify gate, §9.4); bit
`0x8` at offset `+0xb` (`vehicle_exists`'s own resolver, §9.9 — the SAME bit/offset pair §4.13
already lists for `release_to_world`/`vehicle_is_destroyed`/`on_vehicle_enter`, now confirmed a
sixth time through an entirely independent lookup mechanism); bit `0x20` at offset `+6`
(`mesh_mover_hide`/`mesh_mover_show`'s own secondary-object notify gate, §9.16/§9.17); and bit
`0x8` at offset `+6` (`helicopter_set_path_orientation`'s waypoint-association gate, §9.18).
**[CONFIRMED — disassembly, identical table address and indexing shape read directly at every
site above.]** Per `WALLS.md`'s own standing caution, none of these bit/offset pairs is claimed
to have a specific plain-English category meaning beyond what each function's own body already
supports — they are recorded here purely as a census of how heavily this one table is consulted,
not as a resolved bitfield dictionary.

**The record-and-replicate idiom (§4.13) has TWO sibling commit-call variants, not one.**
§4.13 documented a single three-call sequence (`0x0086f5f0`→`0x0086f110`→`0x0086eb20`) across
four call sites. This cluster's own eleven observed record-and-replicate call sites split
cleanly into two groups sharing the same begin (`0x0086f5f0`, taking the opcode argument) and end
(`0x0086eb20`) calls but differing in the MIDDLE commit call: a 4-visible-argument variant
(`0x0086f110`, the address §4.13 already named) used by `helicopter_set_path_orientation`'s
setter (§9.18), `set_unjackable_flag`'s setter (§9.13), `vehicle_infinite_mass`'s setter (§9.8),
and `vehicle_chase`'s "already chasing" position-update path (§9.4); and a 3-visible-argument
sibling (`0x0086f1b0`) used by `effect_stop`'s dispatch (§9.2), `door_lock`'s setter (§9.15),
both `mesh_mover_hide`/`mesh_mover_show`'s setters (§9.16/§9.17), and
`camera_restrict_set_active` (`spec-lua-api-behaviour.md` §8.12, independently confirmed —
that entry's own text already cites this same `0x0086f1b0`→`0x0086eb20` pair). **[CONFIRMED —
disassembly, both commit-call addresses read directly at every site listed; this
corrects/extends §4.13's own text, which named only the 4-argument variant.]**

**Correction after independent review, 2026-09-29: the "4-arg vs. 3-arg" framing above describes
the visible call SHAPE accurately but understates a real mechanism difference between the two
commit calls' own bodies.** `0x0086f110` is a plain single-target dispatcher. `0x0086f1b0`
itself takes a callback/predicate function pointer as its third parameter and, when that
pointer is non-null, walks a DIFFERENT linked list (head at the callee-object's own `+0x54`
field, next-pointer at `+0xb28c`), filtering each entry through the callback before dispatching
to it — a genuine "broadcast to matching entries" shape, not merely the same call with one fewer
visible argument. Every call site checked (across §6/§7/§8/§9) passes a literal `0` for that
callback argument, so in practice all currently-observed uses collapse to the same
single-target behavior as `0x0086f110` — but the underlying mechanism is real and distinct, and
a future caller passing a non-null callback would exercise a genuinely different broadcast path.

**One small independent cross-check on `camera_restrict_set_active` (`spec-lua-api-behaviour.md`
§8.12), not a correction, offered for a peer to re-check:** this pass's own independent decompile
of `0x00a445e0` (before the duplication with §8.12 was noticed) traced the same control flow
§8.12 describes, with one possible refinement — in the "no target argument given" case
specifically, the local boolean-guard variable that gates whether the function returns
immediately after the local toggle call reads as unchanged from its initial `true` value (it is
only ever set to `false` on the OTHER branch, when the target argument resolves to the local
player), which would mean the "argument absent" case falls through into the record-and-replicate
block afterward in addition to running the local toggle, rather than the two being strictly
exclusive. §8.12's own text describes only "arg 2 absent OR resolves to current player" as one
combined case triggering "the local setters." This is flagged here as a possible small
refinement worth a peer re-check against the raw instruction stream, not asserted over §8.12's
own published reading. **[Resolved: adopted by §8.12's 2026-09-29 correction, which now separates the "arg 2 absent" case.]** Separately, and consistently across every one of these eleven sites, the
fields staged between the begin and commit calls are appended to a growing local byte buffer via
one shared low-level append primitive (`0x00881110` for 8-byte fields, `0x00881040` for other
sizes) — a real, confirmed mechanical detail of HOW the record is built, common to every
record-and-replicate call site examined in this document so far, not previously spelled out in
§4.13's own text.

**New record-and-replicate opcodes confirmed this pass, extending §4.13's own roster
(`0x17`/`0x41`/`0x46`):** `0x3a` (`door_lock`, §9.15), `0x40` (`inv_weapon_disable_all_slots`,
§9.20), `0x42` (`helicopter_set_path_orientation`'s setter AND `vehicle_chase`'s
"already-chasing" position update, §9.18/§9.4 — the same opcode independently reached by two
different functions in this cluster), `0x43` (`door_close`/~~`door_lock`/~~`mesh_mover_show`/
`mesh_mover_hide`/`camera_restrict_set_active`, §9.14/~~§9.15/~~§9.16/§9.17/`spec-lua-api-behaviour.md`
§8.12 — ~~five~~ four functions sharing one opcode; `door_lock` is `0x3a`), and `0x45` (`effect_stop`, §9.2). Opcode `0x46`
(already documented,
§4.13) recurs twice more here (`set_unjackable_flag`/`vehicle_infinite_mass`, §9.13/§9.8).
**[CONFIRMED — disassembly, every opcode read directly as a literal argument to `0x0086f5f0` at
its own call site.]**

**Two resolver families recur with a real, confirmed difference in how their callers gate
liveness.** Every one of this cluster's `0x00a281e0`-resolved functions (vehicle-instance
resolver, §4.5) — `vehicle_chase`, `vehicle_speed_override`, `vehicle_max_speed`,
`vehicle_detonate`, `vehicle_infinite_mass`, `set_unjackable_flag`,
`helicopter_set_path_orientation`, `vehicle_pathfind_check_done`, and `teleport_vehicle`'s own
fallback branch — calls NO separate liveness check after resolving, consistent with §4.9's own
reading that `0x00a281e0` already performs equivalent internal validity gating. By contrast,
every one of this cluster's `0x006434a0`-resolved functions (the by-name resolver §1.10 already
documents for `door_open`) — `mesh_mover_hide`, `mesh_mover_show`, `mesh_mover_reset`,
`door_close`, and `door_lock` — explicitly calls the shared liveness check (`0x00853b10`)
immediately after resolving. **[CONFIRMED — disassembly, a real structural difference between
the two resolver families, not an inconsistency.]**

**`0x006434a0` is confirmed as a generic named-placed-object resolver, not door-specific.**
Five functions across two documented clusters now resolve through it: `door_open` (§1.10),
`door_close`/`door_lock` (§9.14/§9.15, this cluster), and `mesh_mover_hide`/`mesh_mover_show`/
`mesh_mover_reset` (§9.16/§9.17/§9.12, this cluster) — doors and mesh-movers share one by-name
registry rather than each having their own.

**Debug-label strings independently confirm two vehicle flag bits' real-world identity.**
`set_unjackable_flag`'s setter (§9.13) and `vehicle_infinite_mass`'s setter (§9.8) attach the
literal strings `"m_force_flagsunenterable"` and
`"m_force_flagsinfinite_vehicle_collision_mass"` respectively (both read directly from `.rdata`)
to their own record-and-replicate blocks — the same kind of independent corroboration §4.6
already established for its own debug-label strings, and a strong confirmation that these two
Lua function names describe their real engine effect precisely, not just a plausible-sounding
label.

**Recommendation for a future pass (not attempted here, out of this task's static-only
scope):** a behavioural oracle would settle several of this section's remaining OPEN items
fastest — `vehicle_chase`'s packed flag byte (which of four boolean arguments maps to which
bit); `0x00600720`'s own switch arms beyond the two this cluster's own call sites reach (would
resolve most of `inv_item_equip`/`inv_weapon_disable_all_slots`'s remaining internals); and
whether `vehicle_max_speed`'s dedicated setter (`0x00a7ded0`) or `vehicle_detonate`'s dispatch
(`0x00a9f4f0`) themselves open a record-and-replicate block that this pass's static trace did
not follow far enough to see. This is a recommendation only; building or running such an oracle
is out of scope for this task.

frequency, not the static registration-order or shipped-script-text-join metrics every other
tranche in this document (§1/§3/§4/§6/§7/§8/§9) used. This is a genuinely different selection
axis, which is exactly why none of these 9 names surfaced in any earlier tranche despite two of

### 10.2 `Completion_is_client` (`0x007bfbc0`) — 589 runtime calls

**Arguments:** none (same unused-`lua_gettop` shape as §10.1).

**Return:** 1 Lua value — a genuine boolean, via `lua_pushboolean` (`0x00dfe590`) then `return 1;`.

**Body:** queries the same co-op/session-context singleton `coop_is_active` (§3.1) and
`game_get_is_host` (§8.27) both already read via `0x0087ba20`; if the singleton is null, pushes
`false` directly. Otherwise it re-reads the singleton and pushes `true` exactly when its own `+0x5c`
field does **NOT** equal its own `+0x58` field — the literal logical negation of `game_get_is_host`
(§8.27)'s own confirmed test, which pushes `true` exactly when those same two fields **ARE** equal.

**Side effects/subsystem:** none — pure query. Subsystem: networking/co-op session state.
**[CONFIRMED — disassembly, full body read; cross-checked directly against §8.27's own already-
decompiled body of a different registered name reading the identical two fields — the two functions
are confirmed exact logical opposites of each other on a live session (this one additionally
returns `false`, not `true`, when no session object exists at all, which is not `game_get_is_host`'s
literal complement in the no-session case but is the only sensible reading of "am I a client" when
there is no session to be a client of).]** This is a clean, direct confirmation that
`Completion_is_client` means exactly what its name says: "is there an active co-op session AND is
this machine NOT the host."

**Review status (2026-10-01): re-derived from the executable (job `20261001T020213-team-a-dksj`): CONFIRMED — the body as described (the accessor is called twice); no session → false; true iff a session exists and `+0x5c` ≠ `+0x58`. Note "active" in the sentence above means "a session object exists" — it does not require `coop_is_active` (§3.1) to be true. With no session at startup this returns false (§26.28).**

### 10.5 `minimap_icon_add_do` (`0x00a53f90`) — 42 runtime calls

**Arguments:** 5. Arg 1 (string, mandatory) — an object name, later resolved to a handle. Arg 2
(string, mandatory) — an icon-type name. Arg 3 (string, optional, standard nil-gated idiom, default
a fixed empty-string constant at `0x0129a0e3`) — a secondary/group name. Arg 4 (number, optional,
standard nil-gated idiom, default `0.0`). Arg 5 (number/flag, optional, standard nil-gated idiom
using the shared flags/number-extractor pair, default `3`).

**Return:** none — every path returns `0` with no `lua_push*` call anywhere in the body.

**Body:** arg 1 is resolved to a live handle through a by-name resolver, `0x00734e90` — **a
genuinely new resolver address, not one of the object-name-resolution family this document's §3/§4
method sections already catalogue** (`0x00a280c0`/`0x005e4dd0`/`0x0062a190`/`0x006434a0`/
`0x004584e0`) — gated by the same shared handle-liveness check (`0x00853b10`) used throughout this
document; failure at either step is treated as "no object," not an error. Arg 2 and (the possibly-
defaulted) arg 3 are each converted from name string to a numeric id via the same hash/lookup helper,
`0x00802f60`. The resolved handle is then passed through `0x00807930`, which reads the SAME shared
per-object-type descriptor table (`0x02cc9900`) the type-gated resolver family (§4.13) already uses
— here testing bit `0x2` at row offset `+7`, a new bit/offset pairing for that table (distinct from
both §4.13's own `+0xa`/`+0xb` sightings and §9.21's own `+7` sighting, which tested a *different*
bit, `0x1`, at the same offset `+7`). If that check passes, the add is issued through one dedicated
call (`0x0093d3a0`) carrying a leading literal `5`; otherwise it is dispatched through a fixed
function-pointer array at `0x0130c9a8`, indexed directly by the (possibly-defaulted) arg-5 flag
value, and called with the resolved handle's own `+8`/`+0xc` fields plus the two resolved ids and
the float parameter. `0x0093d3a0`'s own body reaches the record-and-replicate idiom's begin call
(`0x0086f5f0`, tagged opcode `0x40`) and end call (`0x0086eb20`); the middle "commit" step reaches
the `0x0086f1b0` sibling commit call §9.21 already distinguishes from `0x0086f110` (a genuinely
different, "broadcast to matching entries" mechanism collapsing to single-target behaviour whenever
its own callback argument is `0`, per §9.21). **Correction (adversarial review, same day): this
specific call site does NOT pass `0` for that callback, and the surrounding text above was wrong to
hedge that it might.** `0x0093d3a0` passes the resolved handle and the literal address `0x00884650`
as its own first two arguments to the co-op/session-context singleton accessor, `0x0087ba20`
(§3.1/§8.27) — but that accessor takes **zero** arguments, so neither value is actually consumed by
it; both remain on the stack and become the 2nd/3rd explicit arguments of the immediately following
call into `0x0086f1b0` instead. `0x0086f1b0`'s real 4-argument signature places the callback in
that 3rd argument slot, so the callback `0x0086f1b0` receives here is `0x00884650` itself —
confirmed to be real, live code (a genuine predicate that reads two fields off its own argument and
calls a further comparison helper), not a null/zero value. **So `minimap_icon_add_do` genuinely
exercises the "walk the filtered list, dispatch to every match" mechanism §9.21 flagged as never
yet observed with a non-null callback — it does not collapse to single-target.** Further, the
branch reaching this call is gated on bit `0x2` of arg 5, whose own documented default (`3` =
binary `011`) already has that bit set — **meaning this broadcast path fires under the DEFAULT
argument, not only some rare explicit case.**

**Side effects/subsystem:** adds a minimap icon tied to a named, resolved object, with its type and
an optional group tag resolved from name strings via a shared hash lookup; the exact add call taken
depends on a per-object-type descriptor bit; under default arguments the add genuinely broadcasts
through the filtered-list-walk mechanism rather than targeting a single icon (see the correction
above). Subsystem: minimap/HUD icon management. **[CONFIRMED —
disassembly for argument extraction, the resolver/lookup/gate chain, the two-way dispatch, and the
non-null callback at `0x0093d3a0`→`0x0086f1b0` (independently re-derived by the adversarial review
directly from raw disassembly, not from either census file); OPEN — `0x00807930`'s exact
real-world category (beyond "a bit of the shared type-descriptor table"), the literal `5` tag's
meaning, and the function-pointer array's individual entries.]**

### 10.7 `on_qte_animation_trigger` (`0x00a572e0`) — 24 runtime calls

**Arguments:** 1 mandatory string — a callback name, read unconditionally with no nil/absence gate.

**Return:** none (`return 0;`).

**Body:** unconditionally calls the SAME generic hook-slot-clear helper, `0x005e4520`, that this
pass independently decompiled while tracing `on_revived` (§10.8) below — but reached here directly
rather than through `0x005e4660`, and anchored at a **fixed global base**, `0x026e9528`, rather than
a per-object offset: the raw instruction stream loads that literal address into the helper's implicit
`this`-style argument and passes slot index `0xd` (13) explicitly, which the helper's own body (see
§10.8) resolves to `0x026e9528 + 0xd*4 = 0x026e955c`. This clears any existing value at that fixed
slot (releasing it first, through the same internal `0x00a1fc60` cleanup call, only when this
machine is the network host — see §10.8's decompilation of the shared helper). If the callback-name
argument is a non-empty string, it is then converted to an internal hook reference via `0x00a1fcc0`
(the same name→hook-reference primitive §3.2 already established) and written into that same fixed
slot, `0x026e955c`, overwriting the just-written clear value. Finally, the shared bookkeeping/notify
call `0x00a29920` (§3.2) is invoked with a leading literal `2` (~~a QTE-specific kind tag~~ the global-hook-array kind tag, also used by §13.13/§17.7, distinct
from `0x005e4660`'s own internal leading literal `0` for the character-hook family — see §10.8),
two further fixed globals (`0x026e9568`/`0x026e956c`, read at many other call sites across this
document's own hook/objective functions), the same slot index `0xd`, and a boolean reflecting
whether the slot now holds a real hook reference.

**Side effects/subsystem:** registers (or, given an empty-string argument, clears) a single GLOBAL
QTE-animation-trigger callback slot — the same generic "array of named hook slots, one per event
kind" idiom §3/§7 already document for characters/vehicles/a third object kind, but here rooted at a
fixed global base rather than inside a resolved object. Subsystem: QTE (quick-time-event)
animation-trigger callback registration. **[CONFIRMED — disassembly for the fixed-base slot
arithmetic, the shared-primitive reuse, and the leading-literal-`2` tag; the single-global (rather
than per-object) anchor is a genuinely new shape for this family, plausibly explained by QTEs being
an inherently singleton subsystem — not independently confirmed from a consumer, flagged rather than
asserted.]**

### 10.8 `on_revived` (`0x00a58430`) — 24 runtime calls

**Arguments:** 2 mandatory strings, both read unconditionally with no nil/absence gate. Arg 1 — a
callback name. Arg 2 — a character name.

**Return:** none (`return 0;`).

**Body:** unlike `on_death`/`on_vehicle_destroyed` (§3.2/§3.3), arg 2 is resolved **directly** through
the plain character resolver (`0x005e4dd0`), never trying the generic/`"#PLAYER#"` chain
(`0x00a280c0`) first — a genuine, checked difference in resolution order from its two nearest
siblings in this document. On success and a passing liveness check (`0x00853b10`), the callback is
registered via `0x005e4660` — the SAME character hook-slot registration helper `on_death` (§3.2)/
`on_vehicle_destroyed` (§3.3)/`on_attack_performed` (§3.12)/`on_take_damage` (§3.13) all reach — at
numeric slot `2`, a new entry with no collision against this document's existing per-character
slot catalogue (`0`=`on_death`, `4`/`6`=`on_take_damage`'s two character-kind paths, `8`/`13`=
`on_attack_performed`'s two paths, `0x12`(18)=`on_vehicle_destroyed`'s generic-path fallback).

**Two precise corrections/refinements to this document's own prior description of `0x005e4660`,
found by decompiling that helper's own body directly this pass** (§3.3 had already cited two of its
internal field offsets, `+0x68`/`+0x6c`, implying some prior look inside it, but not these two
findings, which required reading its control flow rather than just those two offsets):

1. **`0x005e4660` itself performs the callback-name→hook-reference conversion (via `0x00a1fcc0`)
   internally** — it is not, as §3.2's phrasing could be read to imply, performed by each calling
   `on_*` function's own body before the call. `0x005e4660`'s own body: it first calls the generic
   slot-clear helper `0x005e4520` (releasing any existing hook at that slot, through `0x00a1fc60`,
   but only when this machine is the network host — the identical `0x0087ba20`/`+0x5c`==`+0x58`
   host-check §8.27 established, reused here); then, only if the supplied callback name is a
   non-empty string, converts it via `0x00a1fcc0` and writes the result into the slot — **meaning a
   registration call with an empty-string callback name clears that slot instead of setting it, a
   real behaviour this document had not previously recorded for this mechanism.** Finally it calls
   the shared bookkeeping/notify function `0x00a29920` with a leading literal `0` (the character-hook
   family's own kind tag, distinct from `on_qte_animation_trigger`'s leading literal `2`, §10.7).
   **[CONFIRMED — disassembly, `0x005e4660`'s full body read directly.]**
2. **The array base passed into `0x005e4660` is not a single fixed absolute character-object
   offset.** Fresh disassembly of `on_death` (§3.2) this pass (not merely its existing decompiled
   summary) shows its generic/`"#PLAYER#"`-path call passes the resolved handle's own `+0x1f00`
   sub-object as that base, while its plain-character-resolver FALLBACK path — and this function,
   `on_revived`, which always takes that same fallback-shaped route — instead passes `+0xf8`. Both
   are real, confirmed, and different; §3.2's own "`+0x68`/`+0x6c`" citation is accurate relative to
   EITHER base, it just was not previously known to differ by resolution path. **[CONFIRMED —
   disassembly, both `on_death`'s and `on_revived`'s raw instruction streams read directly and
   compared.]**

**Side effects/subsystem:** registers (or, given an empty callback name, clears) the target
character's own hook slot `2`. Subsystem: character scripting event-hooks — the "revived" slot, part
of the same named-hook family §3/§7 document. **[CONFIRMED — disassembly for the resolution order,
slot number, and the two refinements above.]**

### 10.9 `game_get_coop_join_type` (`0x008444b0`) — 1 runtime call

**Arguments:** none (same unused-`lua_gettop` shape as §10.1-§10.3).

**Return:** 1 Lua value — a number (`lua_pushnumber`, `0x00dfe3a0`) then `return 1;`.

**Body:** reads a single global (`0x012f44fc`, via a 1-line wrapper, `0x007029b0`) holding a code
`0`, `1`, or `2`, and pushes that same code back out as a Lua number after a switch that also calls
one of three trivial helper functions per branch (`0x0101ba60`/`0x00d48e50`/`0x00d48db0`) whose
return values are discarded. **All three of those helpers decompile to the exact same 1-instruction
"return `1`" stub body**, each with many unrelated callers scattered across completely different
subsystems (16-17 callers apiece) — the same shared-trivial-stub pattern `spec-lua-bindings.md`
§13.6 already documents for `script_profiler_*`'s shared `0x007c9f50` stub. **These three calls are
therefore inert in this context, not real per-branch side effects** — a deliberate check against
over-attributing distinct behaviour to superficially distinct call targets, per `WALLS.md`'s own
standing caution on this exact failure mode.

**The global's sole writer was traced and is a genuine, host-authoritative, network-replicated
value, not a per-machine computation:** `0x012f44fc` has exactly one writer, `0x00703210`, called
from exactly three literal-value sites (values `0`, `1`, `2`) inside one containing function,
`0x00844440` (not part of this tranche, not independently traced further). The writer gates on the
identical host-check singleton (`0x0087ba20`, `+0x5c`==`+0x58`, §8.27) already established
elsewhere in this document — it only commits the new value when running as host (or with no
session at all) and the value is actually changing. **Correction (adversarial review, same day):
the broadcast via `0x0087e0e0` does NOT also fire in the no-session case, contrary to how the
sentence above originally read.** `0x00703210`'s own body writes the global unconditionally under
the gate above, but the broadcast call is only reached inside the sub-branch where a session
object actually exists (the session-object pointer is non-null); in the no-session branch the function writes the global then
returns immediately, never reaching the switch/`0x0087e0e0`. Practically inert either way (nothing
to broadcast to with no session), but the write and the broadcast are gated differently, not
identically. **[CONFIRMED — disassembly, the writer's full body and both gates read directly.]**

**Side effects/subsystem:** none from this function itself — pure query of a host-set, replicated
global. Subsystem: coop/session join-type classification. The real runtime count of exactly 1 is
consistent with this being queried once, most plausibly right after a coop join/session-join
sequence completes, rather than polled.

### 10.10 Cross-function observations

**The shared per-character/vehicle hook-slot registration helper (`0x005e4660`) has now been fully
decompiled, not merely inferred from call shape — see §10.8's two numbered corrections above.** In
summary: it performs the callback-name→hook-reference conversion (`0x00a1fcc0`) itself, clears any
prior slot value through a newly-identified generic slot-clear helper (`0x005e4520`, only releasing
the old value via `0x00a1fc60` when running as host) before writing, and the array base it receives
varies by which resolver found the target (`+0x1f00` for the generic/`"#PLAYER#"` path, `+0xf8` for
the plain-character-resolver path) rather than being one fixed offset. This refines, and does not
contradict, §3.2/§3.3/§3.12/§3.13's own existing descriptions of the same mechanism.

**`0x005e4520` (the generic hook-slot-clear helper) is reused at a ~~THIRD~~ fourth anchor shape.** §3/§7
already catalogue this family's hook-slot arrays anchored at a per-character offset, a per-vehicle
offset, and a per-third-unidentified-kind offset (§3.18; the placed-object/mover kind, identified §14.6); `on_qte_animation_trigger` (§10.7) reaches
the identical clear-then-convert-and-store idiom anchored instead at a fixed GLOBAL address
(`0x026e9528`), not inside any resolved object at all. This is a fourth anchor shape for the same
underlying idiom, not a different mechanism — plausibly explained by QTEs being an inherently
singleton subsystem (only one can be active at a time), which is not independently confirmed from a
consumer but is consistent with everything observed.

**A genuinely new object-name resolver, `0x00734e90`, is confirmed shared by two functions in this
tranche** (`minimap_icon_add_do` §10.5, `object_indicator_add_do` §10.6) and appears nowhere else in
this document — distinct from every member of the by-name resolver family §3's and §4.13's own
method sections already catalogue (`0x00a280c0`/`0x005e4dd0`/`0x0062a190`/`0x006434a0`/
`0x004584e0`). Which broader object kind(s) it can resolve was not independently re-derived; flagged
OPEN rather than assumed generic.

**The shared per-object-type descriptor table (`0x02cc9900`) gains one more confirmed bit/offset
reading from this tranche**, extending §4.13's original ~~two~~ five sightings and §9.21's later ~~seven~~ four:
`minimap_icon_add_do` (§10.5) tests bit `0x2` at row offset `+7` — a DIFFERENT bit than §9.21's own
bit `0x1` at that same offset `+7` (`effect_stop`'s local-apply gate). Both are real and independently
confirmed by direct decompilation at their own sites; recorded here purely as a census entry, per
`WALLS.md`'s own standing caution against assigning this table's bits a plain-English meaning from
offset/position alone.

**Two more confirmed sightings of the `0x0086f1b0` record-and-replicate commit sibling §9.21 first
distinguished from `0x0086f110`:** `minimap_icon_add_do` (§10.5, via `0x0093d3a0`) and

day): the two call sites' own callback arguments have now been independently re-derived directly

**Three of this tranche's four `ui`-tagged functions are pure zero-argument state queries**

**Flag for §1.1's own owner, not a §10 error:** the adversarial review decompiled the shared
handle-liveness gate `0x00853b10` (§1.1, reused throughout §10.5/§10.6/§10.8 above) directly and
found its polarity is the OPPOSITE of what the name "liveness gate" suggests — it returns `1`

means reject, false means usable.** Every call site checked (here and elsewhere) branches
`if (result=='\0') proceed`, so every existing usage in this document is already consistent with
this polarity — nothing built on top of it is wrong — but §1.1's own text does not currently state
the polarity explicitly, which invites exactly the misreading `WALLS.md` warns about for
offset/bit meanings named from their surrounding use rather than their own body. Worth a one-line
addition to §1.1 next time that section is touched; not fixed here since it's outside this
tranche's own scope. **[Resolved: §1.1 already states it — `0x00853b10` "returns non-zero for a dead/invalid handle".]**

## 11. Ranks 151-250 tranche, part D — 12 UI-cluster functions (2026-09-30)

First of four parallel parts covering the next call-count tranche (ranks 151-250 by a peer team's
own real-call-count TSV, `tools/lua_reconciliation_called_and_registered_1181.tsv` on Team B's
side) — this part covers the 12 names tagged `ui` cluster; the 87 `gameplay`-cluster names are
split across three further parts landing as later sections. One name from the raw 100-row slice
(`on_qte_animation_trigger`) was excluded as already documented (§10.7).

**Method:** 9 of these 12 names are real hits in the existing 311-entry UI-wrapper table dump
(`tools/lua_ui_full_dump.txt`, fed by `0x008430f0`) — but that dump's own generating script only
recorded the name half of each `{namePtr,funcPtr}` pair, not the paired function pointer, so this
pass re-walked the 5 containing wrapper functions in full to recover it. The other 3 names were
already fully paired in the existing 113-entry loop-registrar dump (`tools/lua_game845aa0_full.txt`,
`0x00845aa0`) — direct lookup, no new derivation. `vint_options_remap_set_key_binding` was checked
against the 55-name `vint_*`-only registrar (`0x00e1dfb0`, `spec-lua-bindings.md` §13.7) first, as
its name suggests it might belong there — it does not; verified absent from that registrar's own
55-name list, and instead resolved from the UI-wrapper table. None of the 12 came from the 5-name
`0x00e0ef80` registrar (§13.6) either — checked directly. 5 of the 12 target addresses were not
yet Ghidra function starts and were force-disassembled with a manually-defined boundary before
decompiling: `0x007cd3d0`, `0x00831020`, `0x007e0430`, `0x00843ac0`, `0x00844730`.

Every function below opens with this document's already-established shared `lua_CFunction`
prologue (Method section, above) — not re-derived here.

**A ~~new~~ shared helper (already cited in §3's front matter, §8.12, §9.20 and §10.3) whose body this pass decompiles:** `0x009da4e0` — a true zero-argument accessor
returning one fixed global pointer (several call sites show 1-2 visible arguments in the
decompilation; this is the same hidden-calling-convention artifact §1.1 already flags, not a real
parameter — its own disassembled body takes none). The returned object exposes a 3-float position
at `+0x40/+0x44/+0x48` (read by §11.10's camera-math helper) and a morph-value-set handle at `+0x2088`
(read by §11.3/§11.4/§11.5). **HIGH CONFIDENCE — inferred:** this is "the current player/customization-
target character object" singleton, reused across the character-creator (PCR/PCU) functions and the
store camera-framing function — parallel in role to, but a distinct address and subsystem from, the
already-documented co-op/session-context singleton `0x0087ba20`.

### 11.3 `pcr_apply_morph_value` (`0x00834fe0`) — 311-entry UI-wrapper table, wrapper `0x008377d0`

**Arguments:** 3, all read positionally and unconditionally (not this document's usual nil-gated
optional idiom). Arg 1 (string, mandatory) — a named character-creator context/session identifier,
resolved via a case-insensitive linear scan of a small named table (`0x00831650`, 12-byte stride).
Arg 2 — **type-polymorphic**: `lua_type`-tested; a number reads as an index, anything else
(including absent, with no defensive presence check) reads as a string category name. Arg 3
(number, mandatory) — the morph blend value. **Correction (adversarial review, same day): "floor-clamped to `0.0001`" overstated when the clamp fires.** The value clamped *to* is genuinely ≈0.0001 (confirmed byte-for-byte), but the threshold that *triggers* the clamp is not a small-value floor — it's a raw sentinel bit-pattern reinterpreted as a float, evaluating to roughly −3.69×10^19 (independently confirmed byte-for-byte; the decompiler itself needs an explicit float-cast to use it, consistent with a raw sentinel rather than a designed constant). No realistic Lua-supplied value comes anywhere near that threshold, so this branch is dead for normal input — it is at most a guard against one specific extreme/corrupt value, not a small-value floor/deadzone. Do not read this as "small positive blend values get bumped up to 0.0001."

**Return:** none.

**Body:** resolves arg 1 to a session row via `0x00831650`. If found, resolves the target
morph-slot descriptor either by numeric index (bounds-checked against a row count field) or by a
linear scan of a per-row array (`{descriptorPtr, ...}`, 8-byte stride) that calls the engine's
already-documented general-purpose string hash (`0x00d9e8b0`) on both the category argument and the
literal string `"body gender"` — neither call's result is visibly stored in the decompilation, most
likely a real store hidden by the same decompiler void-typing artifact seen elsewhere in this
document, not a dead computation. **[OPEN — the hash results' actual destination was not
independently confirmed; the surrounding comparison logic only makes sense if the category value is
being hash-compared against each row's own stored hash field.]** Once a descriptor is resolved,
calls the shared "current customization-target" singleton (`0x009da4e0`, above) and forwards its
result plus the descriptor and clamped value into a setter (`0x00834860`).

`0x00834860` itself: writes the raw value into the live morph-value array (`0x009f59b0`, on the
singleton's own `+0x2088` field — the same field §11.4/§11.5 read), then enqueues onto a global
dedup'd linked pending-work list (`0x00831e90` — splice-to-front-with-membership-check, i.e.
"queue this, no-op if already queued"). **Correction (adversarial review, same day): the value
enqueued is the customization-target singleton/context object itself (the setter's own first
argument), not the resolved morph descriptor (its second argument) as originally stated here** —
confirmed via raw disassembly of which register is pushed immediately before the call. The
practical effect is closer to "mark this character as having a pending morph recompute" than
"queue this specific morph target." Then calls `0x00d9e140(4000)`. **This call was
independently decompiled this pass and turns out to be a deadline/timestamp computation (adds its
argument to a fixed global base, wraps the sum into a fixed ±1,800,000,000 range, writes the result
through a hidden pointer), not a generic notify/flush call — see the correction now applied to §1.2,
which cited the same function.** It then checks whether the resolved descriptor's own name is
literally `"body gender"`; if so, and the value crossed above `0.5`, runs a further chain
(`0x00821740`/`0x00822a00`/`0x008214c0`/`0x00821630`/`0x009dd4a0`) gated by a separate pending-flag
byte — consistent with triggering an actual body/mesh gender-swap reload (not just a blend-weight
write) once this one specific slider crosses its midpoint; below `0.5` it instead calls
`0x00827f90` and, on a positive result, sets the pending-flag byte and returns early.

**Side effects/subsystem:** writes a morph blend value into the live character-creator preview
object; for the `"body gender"` slot specifically, additionally drives a body-mesh swap pipeline
past the midpoint. Subsystem: character creator/customization (PCR). **[CONFIRMED — disassembly for
argument shape, the resolver chain, and the setter's outer control flow; HIGH CONFIDENCE — inferred
for "body gender" triggering a real mesh/body reload (the literal-string match and 0.5 threshold are
directly observed; the deeper asset-reload chain's own bodies were not opened this pass); OPEN — the
two hash calls' destination, and the exact meaning of the pending-flag byte's two branches.]**

### 11.8 `get_localized_crc_for_tag` (`0x00844730`, force-disassembled) — 113-entry loop registrar `0x00845aa0`

**Arguments:** 1 mandatory string. **Return:** 1 Lua value (a number, via the same unsigned-32-to-
double sign correction already established elsewhere in this document).

**Body — correction, adversarial review, same day: the mechanism below sits one call deeper than
originally stated.** `0x00844730` itself makes exactly one call, to `0x00849fa0` — the SAME
"string → interned id, or `0` if unresolved" helper already cited elsewhere in this document
(§13.1/§13.13). It is `0x00849fa0`'s own body, not `0x00844730`'s, that hashes the tag string via
`0x00d9e740` — a table-driven, lowercase-folding byte loop (`hash = hash>>8 XOR
table[(lower(byte) XOR hash) & 0xff]`, seeded with the caller's second argument, called here with
seed `0`) — then checks the hashed value against a real existence table (`0x00849950`: a 14-shard
hash-bucket structure, each shard gated by a live/dead byte), returning `0` instead of the raw
hash if the tag isn't genuinely registered. The net behavioral conclusion (resolve tag → id or `0`)
is unchanged; only the attribution of which function does the hashing/lookup moves one level down
the call chain. **The hash-identity question this section originally left open is now CONFIRMED,
not just HIGH CONFIDENCE, but the "core/wrapper split" framing was wrong:** independently
decompiling `0x00d9e8b0` shows it does NOT call `0x00d9e740` as a subroutine — both independently
inline the identical per-byte formula against the identical lookup table (`0x01320da0`). They are
two parallel, duplicate compiled instances of the same routine, not a caller/callee pair.

**Side effects/subsystem:** none — pure query. Resolves a localization tag name to its CRC
identifier, returning `0` for any unregistered tag. Subsystem: localization/UI text. **[CONFIRMED —
disassembly for the full chain; HIGH CONFIDENCE for the hash-identity relationship to `0x00d9e8b0`,
flagged OPEN to independently settle.]** **[Stale label: the correction in this section's body already records the hash-identity question as settled (two inlined copies of one formula, not caller/callee).]**

### 11.10 `store_set_camera_pos` (`0x00830670`) — 311-entry UI-wrapper table, wrapper `0x008377d0`

**Arguments:** 1 mandatory string, read unconditionally — a named camera-preset/view identifier

self-contained camera-math routine (`0x0080c500`). That routine: optionally runs a preliminary prep

dispatcher (`0x00568de0`) along with a per-row float, a computed "is the name literally `body`"
boolean, and a flag derived from the row's own data. The trailing `0` argument selects between two
row-relative offset components partway through this computation (always the same branch from this
particular Lua entry point, since the literal is always `0`).

**Side effects/subsystem:** moves/aims the store/character-creator preview camera to a named preset
framing around the live character-creator target. Subsystem: store/character-preview UI camera.

## 12. Ranks 151-250 tranche, part A -- 29 gameplay-cluster functions (2026-09-30)

Second part of the four-way split covering ranks 151-250 (see §11's own header for the
split rationale and TSV source). This part covers 29 names tagged `gameplay` cluster, ranks
roughly 151-180 by real call count.

**Method:** all 29 names confirmed present in the 1,014-entry gameplay registrar
(`0x00a20840`) by direct read of the existing raw-pairs walk
(`tools/scratchpad/lua_gameplay_1014_raw_pairs.txt`) -- no new array walk needed.
**[CONFIRMED -- disassembly, all 29 pairs read directly, not sampled.]** 12 of the 29
targets had not previously been marked as a Ghidra function start and were
force-disassembled and given a function boundary before decompiling, via the project's
existing `tools/scripts/AiDecForce.java`. The other 17 were already-defined functions.

Every function below opens with this document's already-established shared `lua_CFunction`
prologue (Method section, above) -- not re-derived here.

**Two ~~new~~ push primitives found this pass, added to the front-matter primitive list** (not new: `0x00dfe420` is already CONFIRMED `lua_pushstring` from its body in §2's method note/§8 intro, and `0x00dfe380` already identified as `lua_pushnil` in §2's method note)**:**
- **`0x00dfe420(L, constCharPtr)`** -- exactly 2 arguments, used everywhere a name/string
  result is returned. Matches the real public `lua_pushstring(L, s)` signature exactly (the
  only 2-argument push-family call taking a plain C-string pointer). **[HIGH CONFIDENCE --
  inferred from call shape; not independently distinguished from `lua_pushlstring` with an
  inlined `strlen`, since this address's own body was not decompiled this pass.]**
- **`0x00dfe380(L)`** -- exactly 1 argument, used once (a "no result" path). Matches the real
  public `lua_pushnil(L)` signature exactly (the only 1-argument push-family call).
  **[HIGH CONFIDENCE -- inferred from call shape.]**

Both addresses sit inside the already-known push-family address range (`0x00dfe380` <
`lua_pushnumber` `0x00dfe3a0` < `0x00dfe420` < `lua_pushcclosure` `0x00dfe4f0` <
`lua_pushboolean` `0x00dfe590`), consistent with the real Lua 5.1 `lapi.c` declaration order
(`pushnil`, `pushnumber`, `pushlstring`/`pushstring`, `pushcclosure`, `pushboolean`, ...).

### 12.1 `hud_critical_timer_stop` (`0x00a4ed00`) — 28 calls

**Arguments:** none consumed (the shared `lua_gettop` prologue call is made but its result is never used to extract anything — the same genuine zero-argument shape §3.1/§8.27 already established).

**Return:** none (`return 0;`).

**Body:** an internal, zero-explicit-argument helper (`0x006d0dc0`) runs unconditionally first — most plausibly reading state off a single FIXED global "the critical timer" widget slot, since (unlike `hud_timer_set`/`hud_timer_stop`, §8.19/§8.20) no numeric slot-id argument is ever read, meaning there can only be one such widget at a time. The shared local queue-context/stale-handle-clear helper (`0x005e4520`, `spec-lua-api-behaviour.md` §8.19/§8.20) is then called with a literal tag value `0xc` (12) — the same "clear a stale handle by tag" idiom §8.19/§8.20 already established, extending its known tag set (previously `9`/`10` at one call site, §7's own citation) with a new value.

**Side effects/subsystem:** stops/clears the HUD's single "critical countdown timer" widget. Subsystem: HUD, sharing its stale-handle-clear mechanism with the timer/bar-widget family (§8.14-§8.20). **[CONFIRMED — disassembly for the call structure and tag value; OPEN — `0x006d0dc0`'s own internal behaviour.]**

### 12.2 `audio_play_for_mission_cellphone` (`0x00a3daa0`) — 28 calls

**Arguments:** up to 6. Arg 1 (string, mandatory) — a cellphone-call/audio identifier. Arg 2 (boolean, optional, standard nil-gated idiom, default `false`). Arg 3 (boolean, optional, standard nil-gated idiom, default `true`). Arg 4 (string, optional, standard nil-gated idiom, default `""`) — a callback name. Arg 5 (string, optional, standard nil-gated idiom, default `""`) — a second callback name. Arg 6 (number/flag, optional, standard nil-gated idiom using the shared flags/number extractor, default `0`).

**Return:** none (`return 0;`).

**Body:** arg 1 plus both booleans (args 2/3) and the flag (arg 6) are handed to `0x00a38f30`, which allocates/creates a mission-cellphone-audio record and returns a handle. Args 4 and 5, if non-empty, are each independently converted to an internal hook reference via `0x00a1fcc0` — the SAME callback-name→hook-reference conversion helper this document already confirms inside the character hook-slot registration helper `0x005e4660` (§3.2/§10.8) — and written into the record's own two hook-slot fields (`+8` for arg 4, `+0xc` for arg 5). Each write is followed by its own call to the shared bookkeeping/notify function `0x00a29920` (§3.2/§10.8), with a leading literal `1` (a NEW kind tag for that shared family, distinct from the character-hook family's `0` and `on_qte_animation_trigger`'s `2`, §10.7/§10.8) and a sub-index (`0` for arg 4's slot, `1` for arg 5's), plus a boolean of whether that slot's own name resolution succeeded. Between the two slot writes, `0x005e4520` (§8.19/§8.20) is called with tags `0` and `1` respectively, presumably clearing any stale prior handle for each slot before it is (re)written.

### 12.23 `camera_restrict_target_object` (`0x00a45860`) — 22 calls

**Arguments:** up to 6, all optional (standard nil-gated idiom throughout). Arg 1 (string, default absent/`NULL`) — the object to restrict the camera toward. Arg 2 (number, default `0.0`) — a radius. Arg 3 (string, default absent/`NULL`) — a "does this apply to the local viewer" check, see below. Args 4-6 (numbers, default `0.0` each).

**Return:** none (`return 0;`).

**Body — genuinely subtle two-part gating logic, described precisely rather than summarized:** arg 3, if given, resolves through the generic `"#PLAYER#"` resolver (`0x00a280c0`) and is compared against the local-player global (`0x009da4e0`, the SAME global this document's §3 front matter already establishes `"#PLAYER#"` resolves to). By DEFAULT (arg 3 absent), the restriction is BOTH applied locally AND queued for network replication. If arg 3 IS given and resolves to exactly the local player, replication is suppressed (the restriction still applies locally only). If arg 3 is given and resolves to something else, the LOCAL application is suppressed instead (only replication happens) — read as "restrict the camera for every viewer except the one this name identifies," not independently confirmed beyond the local-player comparison. Separately, arg 1 (the actual restriction target) is resolved through TWO resolvers in parallel: `0x00734e90` (the SAME "genuinely new" by-name resolver `minimap_icon_add_do` (§10.5) already establishes) and, regardless of the first result, `0x00a3de90` — if the SECOND resolver's own handle is alive and passes a class-descriptor capability check (vtable offset `+0x68`), its own further vtable method (`+0x70`) supplies the final position-context object, overriding the first resolver's result. If arg 1 does not resolve via either path, a fixed global default position pair (`0x0117f8b8`/`0x0117f8bc`, 0.0/0.0 per §22.31) is used instead — **the SAME "shared global default position-pair" convention `mission_end_failure`/`teleport`/`mission_end_success` (§1.5/§4.3/§6.12) already establish** (same convention, but a different address from §6.12's `0x0117f9e0`/`0x0117f9e4`). The restriction itself is applied locally (when the arg-3 gate above permits) via one of three calls selected by whether a position was found and whether arg 2 (radius) is set: `0x0057a950` (no target), `0x0057ab80` (position only), or `0x0057aca0` (position + radius). When replication is permitted, the SAME record-and-replicate idiom (§4.13/§9.21) opens with opcode `0x43` — **the SAME opcode `door_close`/~~`door_lock`/~~`mesh_mover_show`/`mesh_mover_hide`/`camera_restrict_set_active` (§9.14/~~§9.15/~~§9.16/§9.17/§8.12) already share**, via the broadcast-capable commit variant (`0x0086f1b0`, §9.21) rather than the single-target one.

**Side effects/subsystem:** restricts the active camera toward a named object (with radius), applied locally and/or network-replicated depending on an optional "except for this viewer" name check. Subsystem: camera/UI, directly extending `camera_restrict_set_active`'s (§8.12) own opcode-`0x43` family with a target-object variant. **[CONFIRMED — disassembly for the full two-resolver/gate/dispatch structure and the shared opcode identity; HIGH CONFIDENCE — inferred "except for this viewer" reading of arg 3, from the local-player comparison alone; OPEN — `0x0057a950`/`0x0057ab80`/`0x0057aca0`/`0x00a3de90`'s vtable methods' own internal behaviour, and whether `0x0087ba20` being called here with two literal-zero arguments it cannot consume (it takes zero per §8.27) is the same decompiler-hidden-argument artifact §10.5's own adversarial review already caught for a different function — flagged, not independently re-verified via raw disassembly this pass.]**

### 12.24 `waypoint_add` (`0x00a68cf0`) — 20 calls

**Arguments:** up to 2. Arg 1 (string, mandatory) — a waypoint target name. Arg 2 (number/flag, optional, standard nil-gated idiom, default `3`).

**Return:** 1 Lua value (number) via `lua_pushnumber`, defaulting to the SAME `-1.0` sentinel (`0x012a3038`) `effect_play` (§9.1)/the two `effect_play_on_*` functions (§12.10/§12.12) use, though here at least one success path overwrites it with a plain `0.0` rather than a meaningful id — **OPEN whether this return value is ever a real "waypoint id," or only ever a fixed status code.**

**Body:** arg 1 is tried, in order, against the vehicle resolver (`0x0062a190`), the plain character resolver (`0x005e4dd0`), and the ~~unidentified 4th-kind~~ named-placed-object (door/mesh-mover, §9.21/§14.6) resolver (`0x006434a0` — `spec-lua-api-behaviour.md` §3's front matter) — each gated by the shared liveness check AND a further per-kind capability check at vtable offset `+0x68`. If NONE of the three qualify, arg 1 is instead tried against the trigger/generic-object resolver (`0x005e4e30`, §1.1) or, failing that, `0x005982e0` (§12.10's own resolver family), and on success a direct dispatch (`0x007dd420`) runs with the resolved position pair plus arg 2, yielding `0.0`. If one of the first three DOES qualify, its own vtable method at `+0x70` supplies a further context object, whose position pair (plus a literal `1`, arg 2, and a trailing `0`) is handed to `0x007d70e0`, and that call's own integer return value is reinterpreted directly as the double-precision return.

**Side effects/subsystem:** adds/sets a waypoint pointing at a resolved target, tried across several object kinds in a fixed priority order, with NO record-and-replicate block anywhere in this function's own body — **a confirmed, genuine asymmetry against its documented counterpart `waypoint_remove` (§6.17), which IS network-replicated (opcode `0x40`) on certain mode-value bits.** Subsystem: waypoint/HUD-navigation state. **[CONFIRMED — disassembly for the full resolver-priority chain and the confirmed absence of replication; OPEN — the real-world meaning of the numeric return value, and `0x007dd420`/`0x007d70e0`'s own internal behaviour.]**

### 12.25 `get_current_hit_points` (`0x00a4bb00`) — 20 calls

**Arguments:** 1 mandatory string, no nil-gate — a name.

**Return:** 1 Lua value (number) via `lua_pushnumber`, defaulting to `0.0` if nothing resolves.

**Body — a genuinely different data source per resolution path, not a single shared field read:** the name is tried first against the generic/`"#PLAYER#"` chain (`0x00a280c0`); on success, a float field at the resolved record's own `+0x1cb8` is returned directly. If that fails, the `"#FOLLOWER#"` sentinel chain (`0x00a26010`/`0x00a26110`, §3's front matter) is tried; on success, the SAME `+0x1cb8` field is read off ITS OWN resolved handle. If BOTH fail and a name was given, the plain character resolver (`0x005e4dd0`) is tried: if alive, its own vtable method at `+0x70` is called TWICE in sequence, and only if BOTH succeed is the `+0x1cb8` field read off the SECOND call's OWN return value rather than off the original character handle — HIGH CONFIDENCE that this vtable method resolves "the vehicle/rideable the character currently occupies" (paralleling `character_is_in_vehicle`-style precedent elsewhere in this document), not independently confirmed by decompiling that vtable slot's own target. If the character resolver fails, the vehicle resolver (`0x0062a190`) is tried instead: on success, its own vtable `+0x70` method is checked once, and if it succeeds the "hit points" value comes from an ENTIRELY DIFFERENT source — a zero-argument global context accessor, `0x00a77e10`, with a signed/unsigned correction applied to its result (adding a fixed constant `0x0113e6c8` when the raw value reads negative — the standard "reinterpret a raw unsigned 32-bit value as a large float" idiom). Finally, the ~~unidentified 4th-kind~~ named-placed-object (door/mesh-mover, §9.21/§14.6) resolver (`0x006434a0`) is tried, reading one of two int fields (`+0xdc`, or `+0x138` off a further `+0xc0` sub-object) depending on which is populated, with the same signed-correction applied.

**Side effects/subsystem:** none (pure query). Returns a "hit points" value whose real data source depends entirely on which of five resolution paths succeeded — a direct field for generic/follower/character-fallback-to-mount targets, and a completely different global/field-based source for vehicles and the unidentified 4th kind. Subsystem: character/vehicle health-state query. **[CONFIRMED — disassembly for all five branches and their distinct data sources; OPEN — the character-resolver path's own vtable`+0x70` target (HIGH CONFIDENCE "current mount," not confirmed), and `0x00a77e10`'s own real-world meaning for the vehicle path.]**

- **Two ~~new~~ push primitives identified and recommended for the front matter** (both already in §2's method note; `0x00dfe420` already CONFIRMED there and in §8's intro)**:** `0x00dfe420` (HIGH CONFIDENCE `lua_pushstring`) and `0x00dfe380` (HIGH CONFIDENCE `lua_pushnil`) — see this report's header addendum above for full reasoning.

- **Opcode `0x43` (record-and-replicate, §4.13/§9.21) is confirmed to recur ~~three more times~~ twice in this tranche alone** (`camera_restrict_target_object` §12.23, via the broadcast commit variant; `player_parachute_wear_backpack` §12.28, via the single-target commit variant) — now the single most-reused opcode value in this document's own running census, and the first case where BOTH commit variants are independently confirmed under the exact same opcode.
- **A real, unresolved tension in this document's own existing text, flagged rather than silently resolved:** `0x005e4660` is described by `on_vehicle_enter` (§4.12) and, per this pass, `on_vehicle_exit` (§12.15) as "an event-post primitive" taking a plain name string and a small literal event code — but by `on_death`/`on_revived` (§3.2/§10.8) as "the character hook-slot registration helper" taking a callback name and an array-base pointer. Both framings are independently well-evidenced at their own call sites; whether this is one overloaded/polymorphic primitive or a documentation conflation of two different addresses was NOT resolved this pass and should be checked by decompiling `0x005e4660`'s own body against both calling shapes.
- **The character's cached-vehicle-association field pair (`+0x16c0`/`+0x16c4`) is confirmed read by two independent functions in this tranche** (`get_char_vehicle_name` §12.9, via `0x00458230`; `radio_block` §12.20, via a different helper `0x004dcf00`) — real, confirmed evidence the field is a general "this character's associated vehicle" cache consulted by multiple unrelated Lua entry points, not something private to one function.
- **A ~~new~~ bit/offset combination on the shared class-descriptor table (`0x02cc9900`) — bit `0x8` at row offset `+6`, already recorded for `helicopter_set_path_orientation` (§9.18/§9.21) — is confirmed used for two UNRELATED purposes within this tranche alone:** gating `character_hide`'s (§12.5) linked-list "hide attached items" walk, and gating `effect_play_on_script_object`'s (§12.10) "can an effect attach to this object kind" check. Per this project's own standing caution (`WALLS.md`) against over-attributing a single plain-English meaning to a shared bit/offset pair from one use alone, this is reported as a confirmed dual-use fact, not a claim about what the bit "really means."
- **`vehicle_set_invulnerable` (§12.21) is confirmed to reach the exact same setter (`0x00a7a830`) `turn_invulnerable`'s (§3.7) own vehicle branch already uses** — a direct, dedicated Lua entry point for a primitive an earlier tranche only reached via a generic dispatcher's own internal branching.

### 13.1 `object_indicator_add_objective_text` (`0x00a576a0`)

**Arguments:** 3 mandatory strings, no nil-gates (unconditional positional reads). Arg 1 — a target object name. Arg 2, Arg 3 — two further strings (see body).

**Return:** none (`return 0;`).

**Body:** arg 1 resolves through `0x00734e90` — the by-name resolver `spec-lua-api-behaviour.md` §10.5 already catalogues for `minimap_icon_add_do` (a genuinely different resolver from the §3/§4 object-name-resolution family) — gated by the shared liveness check `0x00853b10`. On success, the resolved object's position pair (`+8`/`+0xc`, the established convention) plus args 2 and 3 are passed to `0x008f7d90`, which: resolves/creates an indicator slot anchored at that position via `0x008f4ef0`; converts arg 2 and arg 3 each from a raw string into a resolved localization/name id via `0x00849fa0` (a "string → interned id, or `0` if unresolved" helper, confirmed simple body) and stores the two ids at the new slot's own `+0x3c`/`+0x40`; then, gated on two further zero-argument predicates (`0x00d9e4c0`/`0x00d9e1e0`, not decompiled this pass), calls the generic expiry-timestamp setter `0x00d9e140` (see finding below) with the literal `20000`; finally, if a bit (`0x2`) is set on the slot's own `+0x2c` flags byte, calls a further zero-argument helper `0x008f76e0` (not decompiled — plausibly "flush/refresh the indicator display list").

**Side effects/subsystem:** creates or updates a world-anchored HUD objective-text indicator, with arg 2/arg 3 as two separate localization-key strings (icon key + text key, most plausibly, from the registered name — not independently distinguished). **Body:** resolves via `0x0062a190` (the established vehicle resolver), liveness-gated. Queries a virtual method at the resolved vehicle's own vtable `+0x70` with no arguments (an existence predicate — the SAME heavily-overloaded slot this document already notes is reused for different roles per object kind/context, e.g. §7.12); if truthy, calls the SAME vtable slot again with the actual value to perform an internal write, then separately calls `0x00a80710(value, 0)`. That function (independently decompiled, `__thiscall`, liveness-gated): when not already-authoritative, opens a record (opcode `0x46`, tags `"vehicle"` + `"min_hit_points"`, both literal-confirmed), position pair via `0x0050f790`, payload the 4-byte value, committed via `0x0086f110`; when authoritative, writes the value directly into the vehicle's own `+0x1560` field (min hit points) and — a real, confirmed cross-field consistency guarantee — also raises the vehicle's own `+0x1564` field (current/max hit points, see cross-cutting finding #7) up to match if the new minimum exceeds it.

**Side effects/subsystem:** sets a vehicle's minimum-hit-points floor, apparently maintained in TWO parallel representations (a vtable-dispatched internal one and the literal `+0x1560`/`+0x1564` field pair `0x00a80710` also maintains) kept in sync. Subsystem: vehicle damage-state. **[CONFIRMED — disassembly for the vtable dispatch shape and `0x00a80710`'s full body; OPEN — what the vtable-side representation actually is, not traced past the dispatch itself.]**

### 13.20 `set_max_hit_points` (`0x00a5f340`)

**Arguments:** 1 mandatory string (name — resolved through the FULL 4/5-way chain: generic/`#PLAYER#` `0x00a280c0`, `#FOLLOWER#` `0x00a26010`/`0x00a26110`, character `0x005e4dd0`, vehicle `0x0062a190`). 1 mandatory number, rounded, no nil-gate. 1 optional boolean, standard nil-gated idiom, default `false`.

**Return:** none (`return 0;`).

**Body — the richest function in this batch, extending §7.12's own established `+0x1cac` field cross-check with two new fields.** On a generic/`#PLAYER#`-or-`#FOLLOWER#` success: reads the SAME field §7.12 established (`+0x1cac`, current max cap) and a NEWLY-confirmed sibling `+0x1cb8` (current hit points, as a float) to compute a health RATIO (`current/max`); calls `0x0094d1f0` (see below) to apply the new max; if the trailing boolean argument is `false` (default), scales the (now-updated) current HP by the SAME ratio to preserve the health *percentage* across the cap change (passing the ratio times the new value to `0x0094cfc0`); if `true`, instead sets current HP to the raw new max field value directly (passing the `+0x1cac` value to `0x0094cfc0`). On a plain-character-resolve success that FAILS the vtable `+0x68`/`+0x70` double-gate §7.12 also notes: instead writes the raw value directly into a completely different field, `+0xb4` — a third, genuinely distinct code path with no health-ratio logic and no vtable dispatch at all. On a vehicle-resolve success: queries vtable `+0x70` as an existence check, then (mirroring the character ratio logic exactly, independently confirmed at the field level) calls `0x00a80510` — which rescales the vehicle's own current-HP field (`+0x1564`) proportionally to the max-field change (`+0x155c`), and additionally propagates the new max to attached sub-component records (an array at `+0x68c`, count at `+0x688`, gated on a flag at `+0xbd0`) via `0x00a88cd0`; if the boolean argument is `true`, ALSO calls `0x00a80220` to set the current-HP field to the raw new value directly (mirroring the character path's `true` branch).

`0x0094d1f0`/`0x0094cfc0` (character helpers, independently decompiled): the double-gate/record shape for `0x0094d1f0` (tags `"human"`+`"max_hit_points"`, both literal-confirmed) sets `+0x1cac` to the ~~`+0x1cb0` base value~~ **`+0x1cb0` value** plus the argument — **the Lua argument is added as a delta onto ~~a base~~ this field, not an absolute replacement** (see cross-cutting finding #7) — **CORRECTED (2026-10-02, character spawn-state investigation): `+0x1cb0` is the max-HP **bonus** field, not a "base" — its own setter is `0x0094d380` and its record tag is `"max_hit_point_bonus"` (both literal-confirmed); the arithmetic described here is unchanged, only the field's label was wrong.** — and separately clamps current HP (`+0x1cb8`) down if it now exceeds the raw argument value. `0x0094cfc0` clamps the requested current-HP value into `[0, currentMax]`; when authoritative, writes it to `+0x1cb8`, triggers a state-notify `0x0096f5e0` if a field at `+0x1584` differs from a fixed constant, and — if the new HP is `<= 0` AND two further exclusion predicates (`0x00973d40`/`0x0096f540`) are both false — calls `0x0096f8c0` (very plausibly the death-trigger path, given the same field conventions §3.5/§3.15 already establish for character death); when not authoritative, opens a record (tags `"human"`+`"hit_points"`, literal-confirmed) carrying a compressed 16-bit encoding of the max field (via `0x008add70`/`0x00bc5610`) plus the raw 4-byte requested value.

`0x00a80510`/`0x00a80220` (vehicle helpers) mirror the same authoritative-direct-write-vs.-record-and-replicate shape, tags `"vehicle"`+`"max_hit_points"`/`"vehicle"`+`"hit_points"` respectively (both literal-confirmed).

**Side effects/subsystem:** sets a character or vehicle's max hit points (as a base+delta, not an absolute value, for characters), with the trailing boolean choosing between "preserve health percentage" (default) and "reset current HP to the new max" semantics, mirrored identically for vehicles including propagation to sub-components. **[CONFIRMED — disassembly for the entire multi-path structure, all field offsets, and the ratio/delta arithmetic; HIGH CONFIDENCE — inferred that `0x0096f8c0` is the death-trigger path, from field/state-machine consistency with §3.5/§3.15, not independently re-confirmed by decompiling it directly this pass; OPEN — the `+0xb4` third-path field's real meaning and why that path skips the ratio logic entirely.]**

### 13.21 `inv_item_in_slot` (`0x00a50930`)

**Arguments:** 2 mandatory strings (character name, slot name).

**Return:** 1 string, always (via the established `lua_pushstring`, `0x00dfe420`) — the held item's own name, or a fixed fallback.

**Body:** resolves char via `0x00a281a0`. Resolves the slot name via `0x00a25f80`: tries a fixed enumeration table first (`0x008dc6b0`, not decompiled — codes `0`-`0xb`, most plausibly the numbered weapon/item slots); on failure, falls back to 5 hardcoded case-insensitive literal compares: `"best"`→`0xd`, `"best-firearm"`→`0xe`, `"best-melee"`→`0xf`, `"best-non-lethal"`→`0x10`, `"best-non-explosive"`→`0x11` (confirmed via the branchless arithmetic), else `0xff` (no match). If both resolves succeed AND the slot code `!= 0xff`: dispatches by code — `< 0xb` → `0x005fec20` (a further switch: codes `9`/`0xff`→none; `0xa`→a different field pair at `+0x60`/`+0x64`; `0xc`→substitutes the character's own "currently selected slot" byte at `+0xa8`; default → an array-of-8-byte-entries lookup at `char + slot*8`); `0xd`/`0xe`/`0xf` → three separate dedicated helpers (`0x005ff7a0`/`0x005ff220`/`0x005ff680`). On a resolved item record, pushes a doubly-indirected name string field (the name string at `+0x5c` of the object reached by double indirection through the item record's `+0x19c`); otherwise (including any unresolved/unhandled slot code) pushes the fixed literal string `"none"` (confirmed via direct string dump at `0x0129b26c`).

**A real, confirmed functional gap:** the slot-NAME resolver can produce codes `0xc`, `0x10`, and `0x11`, but `inv_item_in_slot`'s own dispatch switch only explicitly handles `< 0xb`, `0xd`, `0xe`, `0xf` — codes `0xc`/`0x10`/`0x11` all fall straight to the `"none"` fallback here, even though `0xc` ("currently selected slot") IS handled inside `0x005fec20`'s own switch when reached from OTHER callers (22 total callers of `0x005fec20`, most not through this Lua function). So `inv_item_in_slot(char, "best-non-lethal")` and `inv_item_in_slot(char, "best-non-explosive")` always return `"none"` regardless of the character's actual inventory, despite the name resolving successfully.

**Side effects/subsystem:** none — pure query. Subsystem: inventory/weapon-slot lookup. **[CONFIRMED — disassembly for the full resolve/dispatch chain and the confirmed dead slot-code gap; OPEN — the fixed slot-name enumeration table `0x008dc6b0`'s own contents beyond the 5 special-cased literals.]**

### 13.22 `hud_achievement_show_progress` (`0x00a4ea90`)

**Arguments:** 5. Arg 1 (string, mandatory) — an achievement name. Arg 2, Arg 3 (numbers, mandatory, no nil-gate) — current/total progress values. Arg 4 (number, optional, standard nil-gated idiom, default `3` — the established dual-bit flags convention). Arg 5 (boolean, optional, standard nil-gated idiom, default `true`).

**Return:** none.

**Body:** arg 1 is hashed via the general CRC-32 hash `0x00d9e8b0`, then looked up in a small fixed achievement-definition roster via `0x00711060` (linear scan, count `0x0151af34`, stride `0x16` dwords, matching against the hash — a data-table key lookup, not a live object resolve). On a match, if arg 5 (default `true`): if arg 4's bit `0x2` is set (true by default), opens a network record, opcode `0x1b` (new for this family), carrying the progress values via the established payload writers, committed via the single-target-shaped `0x0086f1b0` path; if arg 4's bit `0x1` is set (also true by default), calls `0x007fbfd0(matchedRecord, currentProgress)` — independently decompiled: allocates (via `0x007fb990`) and populates a UI notification-queue entry from the matched record's own fields plus the two passed progress values, then dispatches it via `0x007fa750` — a real, confirmed "queue an achievement-progress toast" mechanism, directly matching the function's own registered name. Separately, regardless of arg 5: if `current == total` (progress complete), calls one and/or both of two further, unidentified completion-handler routines (`0x007108a0`/`0x00711b60`) depending on two more bits of arg 4 — plausibly a completion popup and/or fanfare sound, not independently confirmed.

**Side effects/subsystem:** looks up a named achievement in a fixed data-table roster and, by default, both replicates and displays a progress-toast notification for it; separately fires one or two additional (unidentified) completion handlers when progress equals total. Subsystem: achievements/HUD notification UI. **[CONFIRMED — disassembly for the hash-based lookup, the toast-queue mechanism, and the completion-equality check; OPEN — `0x007108a0`/`0x00711b60`'s own bodies, and the exact bit-to-behavior mapping of arg 4 beyond the two already-established default-active bits.]**

### 13.25 `character_ragdoll_set_last_valid_position` (`0x00a45f50`)

**Arguments:** 1 mandatory string (character name). 1 mandatory string (a second, destination/reference name — resolved through `0x005982e0`, the "5th resolver" §7.5/§6.21 already catalogue). 1 optional boolean, standard nil-gated idiom, default `false`.

**Return:** none (`return 0;`).

**Body:** resolves arg 1 via `0x00a281a0`, arg 2 via `0x005982e0` (liveness-gated). On both succeeding, calls `0x00a26ec0(character, target+0x40/+0x44 [an 8-byte value], target+0x48 [a 4-byte value], boolean, literal 0)`. That function (independently decompiled): the trailing literal `0` (always passed by this Lua entry point) selects the branch that ALWAYS opens a network record — opcode `0x43`, tag `0x29` (41), carrying the 8-byte position value (via a dedicated writer `0x004d2d40`) and the boolean, committed via `0x0086f1b0` — **with no double-gate skip**, structurally the same "no gate, always both" shape §7.17 (`set_script_animation_state`) already catalogues as category 4 of the record-and-replicate idiom family (§7's own front matter). Separately (gated only on the boolean argument, independent of the record branch): if `false` (default), advances a 10-slot rolling RING BUFFER index (`+0xdbc`, wraps at 10) and writes the position+tag pair into the next slot (base `+0xdc0`, stride `0xc`); if `true`, instead OVERWRITES ALL 10 SLOTS with the same value in one pass.

**Side effects/subsystem:** maintains a per-character 10-entry rolling history of "last valid (pre-ragdoll) positions." The boolean argument's real role is now clear from the field-level behavior: `false` (default) appends one new history entry (normal tracking); `true` resets the ENTIRE history to a single spot (most plausibly used right after a teleport, to prevent the ragdoll-recovery system from ever reverting to a stale pre-teleport location) — always replicated over the network regardless. **[CONFIRMED — disassembly for the resolve chain, the always-both record shape, and the full ring-buffer read/overwrite logic; OPEN — the exact real-world meaning of the 8-byte value copied from the resolved destination's own `+0x40`/`+0x44` fields.]**

### 13.26 `character_collision_enable` (`0x00a41120`)

**Arguments:** 1 mandatory string (character name). 1 mandatory boolean, no nil-gate.

**Body:** resolves via `0x00a281a0`, delegates to `0x0094f450(character, boolean, 1)` — a large REASON-CODE dispatcher, not a simple bit flag. Depending on the boolean and a cascade of predicate checks — a co-op/session gate (`0x00722000`/`0x007220c0`), the ALREADY-ESTABLISHED `is_dead` predicate (`0x0096f4f0`, §3.5), two bitfields (`+0xe0`/`+0xe8`), two further predicates (`0x009b9160`/`0x009b9230`), and a bit test on the ESTABLISHED shared per-object-kind class-descriptor table (`0x02cc9900`, row offset `+0xa`, bit `0x2`) — it dispatches to ONE of several outcomes: `0x00759d80(char, reasonCode, 1)` with a reason code from the set `{0xc0005, 0x12, 0x80007, 0x40017, 0x30010, 0xd, 0x13}`, or (when the class-descriptor bit is set) an alternate `0x009dd8b0`/`0x009dd870`/`0x009dd890(descriptorSlot, 1)` variant.

**Side effects/subsystem:** `character_collision_enable`'s Lua binding is really just ONE fixed caller of the engine's own generalized, reason-coded collision-state-change system — it does not toggle a simple bit directly. Subsystem: character physics/collision. **[CONFIRMED — disassembly for the full dispatch cascade and the reuse of the established `is_dead` predicate and class-descriptor table; OPEN — the individual reason codes' real-world meanings, and `0x00759d80`'s/the `0x009dd8*0` family's own bodies, none decompiled this pass.]**
