### 13.29 Cross-function observations

1. **Confirmed (raw disassembly, 2 sites) — a real, third-hand instance of the "hidden
   `this`-pointer" decompiler gap already on record (§6.10).** For
   `character_set_no_explosive_panic` and `set_team`, the outer wrapper's decompiled view shows
   its delegate call with only the boolean/pointer argument visible, making it look like a global
   write. Raw disassembly of both call sites shows the resolved object handle is moved into the
   delegate's implicit-`this` register immediately before the call — the delegate is genuinely a
   per-object method, not a global setter. Decompiling the delegates themselves independently
   confirms this (both declared as taking a hidden object-pointer argument by Ghidra once looked
   up directly). The same pattern, not individually re-confirmed by raw disassembly but supported
   by the delegate's own confirmed signature, recurs for `vehicle_ignore_repulsors`,
   `ai_set_personality`, and `vehicle_suppress_flipping`. **Recommend citing this as a second
   confirmed instance of the §6.10 class of gap, generalizable: any call in this cluster showing
   only 1 visible argument to a delegate whose own decompiled signature takes a hidden object
   pointer almost certainly passes the resolver's handle as that hidden argument.**
2. **`0x00d9e8b0` is the project's own already-established general-purpose case-insensitive CRC-32 name hash** (confirmed elsewhere in this project per an inline source comment recovered in its own decompiled body, citing ~835 call sites, `spec-extensionless-types.md` §4) — used here by `customization_outfit_wear`, `refraction_situation_set`, and (via `0x00507e60`) `ai_set_personality`. This means these three functions' name arguments are resolved by **hash into a table/index**, not through the object-name-resolver family (§3/§4/§10.5's front matter) — a real, useful distinction: they name *data records* (outfit/refraction presets, personality profiles), not live game objects.
3. **`0x00734e90`** (used by `object_indicator_add_objective_text`) is the resolver §10.5 already catalogued for `minimap_icon_add_do` — cited, not re-derived. **`0x005982e0`** (used by `character_ragdoll_set_last_valid_position`) is the "5th resolver" §7.5/§6.21 already catalogue. **`0x00a281e0`** (used by `vehicle_ignore_repulsors`, `helicopter_set_max_bank_angle`, `vehicle_suppress_flipping`) is the dedicated object-to-vehicle-instance resolver §4.5 already documents.
4. **New record-and-replicate opcodes confirmed this pass** (extending, not contradicting, the existing census): `0x41` (`character_ragdoll_clear_last_resort_position`'s global-clear path — a further site of an existing opcode, §4.10), `0x42` (`helicopter_set_max_bank_angle`, via `0x00b37d00` — a further site of an existing opcode, §9.21), `0x44` (the only genuinely new one) (`customization_outfit_wear`'s apply delegate `0x00619110`), and further confirmed real instances of `0x43` (`customization_outfit_wear`'s other branch, `refraction_situation_set`, `camera_shake_play`, `camera_end_look_through`, `character_ragdoll_set_last_valid_position`) and `0x46` (all the simple per-object bit-flag setters in this batch, same double-gate-variant-1 shape as §3.7/§7's own family).
5. **A new record-payload helper, `0x0086f530`** (a per-object method taking the open record
   buffer as its implicit target and a C-string as its one explicit argument): writes a
   length-prefixed-by-truncation string field (computes `strlen`, writes the bytes via the established `0x00881040`, then a null terminator if space allows) into the currently-open record buffer — a string-valued sibling of the already-established fixed-size field writers `0x00881040`/`0x00881110`. Used by `camera_shake_play` to carry the shake-profile name string into its replicated record.
6. **Vehicle identity-pair convention differs by subsystem.** Character/NPC-kind setters in this batch consistently read their record-and-replicate identity pair from object `+8`/`+0xc` (the standard convention). The one vehicle-kind bit-flag setter that shows its own identity pair explicitly (`vehicle_ignore_repulsors`'s delegate `0x00b22bf0`) instead reads `+0x4e0`/`+0x4e4` — a real, confirmed, different offset pair for at least this one vehicle sub-record, not an error.
7. **Character/vehicle hit-point field models, now cross-checked end to end (extends §7.12's own `+0x1cac` finding).** Character: `+0x1cac` = current max cap (int), `+0x1cb0` = a *base* max value, `+0x1cb8` = current HP (float) — `set_max_hit_points`'s Lua argument is added as a **delta onto the base**, not an absolute replacement (`+0x1cac = +0x1cb0 + arg`), confirmed directly in `0x0094d1f0`. Vehicle: `+0x1560` = min, `+0x155c` = max, `+0x1564` = current (int) — cross-confirmed identically from both `set_min_hit_points`'s delegate (`0x00a80710`) and `set_max_hit_points`'s vehicle branch (`0x00a80510`/`0x00a80220`). Both character and vehicle max-change paths preserve the **current/max ratio** across a cap change when the Lua caller's boolean flag is left at its default (`false`), confirmed identically in both `0x0094cfc0`'s caller (character) and `0x00a80510`'s own ratio computation (vehicle) — a genuine, independently-corroborated cross-object-kind design pattern, not a coincidence.
8. **`0x009da4e0` and `0x009df3d0` are genuinely zero-argument accessors** (`0x009da4e0` returns a single global, `0x0262edfc`, directly — plausibly "the local/active player handle," ~2,239 callers project-wide; `0x009df3d0` scans a small runtime list for a match against that same global and returns it or `0`). Both are shown with 1-3 *visible* arguments at several call sites in this batch's own decompiles (`0x00a36e60`, `0x00619110`, `customization_outfit_wear`'s own body) — a real, confirmed decompiler-rendering inconsistency (not resolved by raw disassembly this pass, flagged rather than asserted). **Recommend flagging this as a WALLS.md-style caution**: when a function's own independently-decompiled signature takes 0 args but a caller's decompile shows it invoked with visible arguments, the visible arguments are very likely leftover/reused stack values from a neighboring call, not real parameters — don't attribute meaning to them without a raw-disassembly check.

## 14. Ranks 151-250 tranche, part B -- 30 gameplay-cluster functions (2026-09-30)

Fourth part of the four-way split covering ranks 151-250 (see §11's own header for the split
rationale and TSV source). This part covers 30 names tagged `gameplay` cluster, ranks roughly
181-211 by real call count.

**Method:** all 30 `{name,funcPtr}` pairs read directly from the existing raw-pairs walk
(`tools/scratchpad/lua_gameplay_1014_raw_pairs.txt`) -- no new array walk needed. 12 of the 30
targets had not previously been marked as a Ghidra function start and were force-disassembled
and given a function boundary before decompiling. The other 18 were already-defined functions.
Every function below opens with the shared `lua_CFunction` prologue already established in this
document's own front matter (`lua_gettop`=`0x00dfde50`, `lua_type`=`0x00dfe040`,
`lua_toboolean`=`0x00dfe1e0`, `lua_tolstring`=`0x00dfe210`, `lua_tonumber`+round=`0x00dfe160`+
`0x00ea2596`, `lua_pushnumber`=`0x00dfe3a0`, `lua_pushboolean`=`0x00dfe590`) -- cited, not
re-derived.

### 14.15 `vehicle_hide` (`0x00a64250`) — 17 calls

**Arguments:** 1 mandatory string (vehicle name, resolved via `0x00a281e0`). 1 optional boolean, standard nil-gated idiom, default **`false`** — a real, confirmed asymmetry against most other optional booleans in this batch, which default `true`.

Only if arg 2 is true, a second call additionally hides up to a per-vehicle count (default `8`, or a per-vehicle field at `+0x824` when a flag at `+0xbd0` is set) of attached sub-objects/occupants in an array at the vehicle's own `+0x1358` (stride `0x30`), via the same underlying hide primitive (`0x008ccb90`) each entry resolves to (`0x004d7f30`).

**Side effects/subsystem:** always hides the named vehicle's own body (and any chained/attached object); optionally (arg 2) also hides its individual attached sub-objects (doors, turrets, occupants). ### 15.2 `vehicle_anim_start` (`0x00a64850`) — 11 calls

**Arguments:** 4. Arg 1 (string, mandatory) — vehicle name, resolved via the established vehicle-reference resolver `0x00a281e0`. Arg 2 and arg 3 (strings, both mandatory) — each independently converted from a name string to a numeric id via `0x004bf810` (a distinct name→id lookup, not part of the object-handle-resolution family). Arg 4 (number, optional, default a shared global float constant `0x01117a4c`) — a blend/speed value.

**Return:** none.

**Body:** once the vehicle resolves, arg 2's id and arg 3's id are computed. If arg 2's id is the sentinel `-1` (not found): if arg 3's id is also a specific sentinel bit-pattern, a stop/cancel dispatcher (`0x00a76d70`) runs; otherwise a "play by literal id" dispatcher (`0x00a75f00`) runs, passing two fixed literal flag/duration values (`0x1d4c`, `0x200000`) plus the blend value. If arg 2's id IS valid: the stop/cancel dispatcher always runs first, then a "set target track" dispatcher (`0x00a75ea0`) runs with arg 2's id and either arg 3's id or the sentinel `-1`. All three tail dispatchers (`0x00a75f00`/`0x00a76d70`/`0x00a75ea0`) share the same entry gate on the vehicle handle: they no-op unless a byte flag at handle offset `+0xbd0` is set AND a sub-object pointer at `+0xa78` (an anim-controller object) is non-null; when gated in, they forward into `0x004b1b90`/`0x004b21a0` respectively. After the dispatch, the function unconditionally opens a record-and-replicate block (begin `0x0086f5f0`, tagged opcode `0x43`, sub-id `0x21`), serializes a per-vehicle "actor" byte obtained via `0x008add70`, then the two resolved ids and the blend value, and commits via the **local-dispatch** sibling `0x0086f1b0` (not the genuinely-networked `0x0086f110`) then `0x0086eb20`.

**Side effects/subsystem:** starts, changes, or stops a named vehicle animation track, gated on the vehicle having an active anim-controller sub-object; always emits a local (non-network) replicate record afterward. Vehicle animation. **[CONFIRMED — disassembly for the full branch structure, the resolver, the shared gate on the three tail dispatchers, and the record-and-replicate shape; OPEN — the concrete real-world meaning of the two literal flag constants `0x1d4c`/`0x200000`.]**

### 15.11 `message` (`0x00a52860`) — 11 calls

**Arguments:** 4. Arg 1 (string, mandatory) — a text key or literal message text. Arg 2 (number, optional, default a global float constant `0x01187ebc`; separately, if the resolved value is `<= 0.0`, it is replaced by a second floor constant `0x01117a50`) — a display duration. **Return:** 1 Lua number. **Raw disassembly confirms the pushed value's count is really 1** despite the decompiler rendering the function as `void`: the tail loads the literal `1` into the return register right after the `lua_pushnumber` call, in both this function and the structurally-similar `hud_display_create_state` (§15.24) — the real C source is the ordinary `lua_pushnumber(L, id); return 1;` shape.

**Body:** builds a small fixed parameter block (duration, two zeroed floats, a further fixed constant `0x0126d2cc`, and several fixed integer fields, none Lua-sourced) then dispatches on arg 3: if true, the raw text pointer (already treated as a possible localization key) is passed together with the parameter block to `0x007ff8a0`, which resolves it via `0x00849fa0` and forwards to `0x007ff680`; if false, the text is first run through the same `sprintf`-shaped formatter this document's §1.3 already cites (`0x00db06e0`) into a local buffer, then dispatched via `0x007ff3e0`→`0x007ff2d0`. Both paths return an integer message/popup-instance id (visible via the caller capturing a return value from `0x007ff8a0` even though that callee's own decompiled signature shows `void` — a decompiler signature-inference gap, not evidence of no return value), converted to `double` (with the standard negative-int32-as-unsigned wrap correction this project uses elsewhere) and pushed. **This is a separate message-slot mechanism from the `hud_display_*` trio's own slot-queue (§15.12/§15.24/§15.25) — no shared state was found between them.**

**Side effects/subsystem:** creates a HUD/console text message/popup and returns its instance id. HUD/UI messaging. **[CONFIRMED — disassembly for the argument shape, both dispatch paths, and the return-count via raw disassembly; OPEN — the exact created-object's later lifecycle/removal path was not found in this batch.]**

### 15.17 `teleport_check_done` (`0x00a61d90`) — 10 calls

**Arguments:** 1 mandatory string — an object/character name, resolved via `0x00a281a0`.

**Return:** 1 boolean, always.

**Body:** ~~the resolved handle and a literal `4` are passed to `0x006f6380`, but **that callee's own decompiled signature takes no parameters at all** and its body references only global state (a zero-argument getter for the single active-teleport singleton, `0x006f6260`). This is a genuine, confirmed finding: the resolved name argument is completely unused/discarded — the check is global, not per-object. The callee itself returns `0` (no active teleport tracked), `1` (an active teleport found AND already flagged done — clearing the flag via `0x006f6040` as a side effect), or `2` (an active teleport found but not yet done); the caller collapses all of this to a single boolean via `!= 0`. **A further real finding: this collapses the "done" (1) and "still pending" (2) cases together — the pushed boolean is true whenever ANY teleport is being tracked, not specifically "done."**~~

**CORRECTED (2026-10-02, `teleport_coop` investigation, re-read against the raw instruction stream, not just the decompile): the resolved handle and the literal `4` (the scripted-request "kind," §35.2) ARE used — the decompiler's zero-parameter signature for `0x006f6380` hid them; raw disassembly shows the object arriving in ECX and the kind in EDI, forwarded to the register-argument finder `0x006f6260`, which matches on BOTH the object's own 8-byte handle and the requested kind — this is a genuinely per-object check, not global. The status codes are also the other way around from the original reading: **`2`** = no matching kind-4 request exists for this object (never issued, already consumed, superseded, reaped, or the name didn't resolve); **`1`** = a request exists and is done (its record is released back to the free list as a side effect, via `0x006f6040`); **`0`** = a request exists and is still pending. The pushed boolean is `status != 0`, so it is **true for "done" (1) or "no request" (2), and false only while a request is genuinely pending (0)** — not "true whenever any teleport is tracked." §9.10 `vehicle_pathfind_check_done` already reads this same callee correctly (0=pending, 1=done-and-consumed, 2=none) and is the reference reading this entry should have matched all along.

**Side effects/subsystem:** queries, and on a "done" read releases, a per-object scripted-request record from the shared 200-slot request pool (`0x014f4be0`/`0x014f4be4`, kind 4 = teleport; see §35.2 for the pool's full shape, shared with `turn_to_check_done`/`move_to_check_done`/`vehicle_pathfind_check_done`). The name argument genuinely selects which object's request is examined. Teleport state. **[CONFIRMED — disassembly, re-derived 2026-10-02 from the raw instruction stream after the original decompile-based reading above was found wrong on three counts.]**

### 15.22 `npc_leash_to_object` (`0x00a56460`) — 10 calls

**Arguments:** 4. Arg 1 (string, mandatory) — an NPC/character name, resolved via `0x00a28150`. Arg 3 (number, mandatory, unconditional read) — a leash radius/distance. Arg 4 (boolean, optional, default `false`, standard nil-gated idiom).

**Return:** none — an early-return path exists if the radius is negative, dispatching to a single zero-argument call (`0x004e3bf0`, read as "clear leash") instead of the normal path.

**Body:** arg 2 is tried, in priority order, against: (1) `0x00a3de90` — if it resolves AND passes the shared liveness check `0x00853b10`, a virtual method at that object's own vtable `+0x70` is queried with no visible arguments (a further, independently-observed sighting of this document's recurring vtable-`+0x70` pattern, on a base-object class distinct from — and not claimed identical to — the vehicle-resolver sighting at §15.16); its result is then tested against the same shared type-descriptor table `0x02cc9900`, but bit `0x2` at offset `+6` — a genuinely new bit at an offset this document already uses for a different bit (`0x004584e0`'s bit `0x1` at the same offset `+6`, per §3.11) — extending the type-descriptor-table census with a ~~second~~ further bit meaning at that offset (offset `+6` already carries bits `0x1`, `0x8`, `0x20` and `0x80`). If instead only the third-resolver handle is live, a bit test at that handle's `+0x8d` gates an initialization call (`0x008cfc70`) before the same position-apply primitive runs on a converted (2-float→4-float, via `0x00da38e0`) vector.

### 15.23 `mission_end_silently` (`0x00a52490`) — 10 calls

**Arguments:** 1 optional boolean, default `false` (standard nil-gated idiom).

**Return:** none.

**Body:** the boolean is passed to `0x006da7b0`, which unconditionally sets bit `0x4` of a global mission-flags word (`0x014c848c`) and sets/clears bit `0x10` of the same word to mirror the argument. If a "can end mission now" gate (`0x006cf930`) passes: fetches the current active mission (`0x009da4e0`) and, if it is flagged restartable, runs cleanup (`0x009da840`/`0x009dcf10`). **A genuinely different polarity from every other coop-host check in this cluster:** the code then checks the coop-session singleton with `+0x5c` != `+0x58` (the opposite of this document's own established "is host" test, `==`) — when a session exists AND this machine is specifically a non-host client, it opens a network-replicate record (opcode `0x44`, via the true multi-target sibling `0x0086f110`, using a distinct 3-zero-argument sync-id resolver `0x008684d0`) and skips the local finalize call; otherwise (no session at all, or a session where this machine IS host) it runs a local-only finalize (`0x006d9f70`) instead. Read plainly: this looks like a client→host request shape ("tell the host to end the mission silently"), the reverse of the host→clients broadcast pattern the rest of this batch's opcode-`0x46` functions use.

**Side effects/subsystem:** ends the current active mission "silently," either via a client-to-host network request (opcode `0x44`) or a local finalize when running as host/offline. Mission state. **[CONFIRMED — disassembly for the full body and the inverted-polarity check; OPEN — the exact meaning of the two global mission-flags bits (`0x4` unconditional, `0x10` argument-mirrored) beyond "a mission-end-mode word."]**

### 15.26 `game_choice_set_state` (`0x00a4ac60`) — 10 calls

**Arguments:** 2 mandatory, both read unconditionally with no nil guard. Arg 1 (number, via the flag/number-extractor pair) — a small choice index, kept as a byte. Arg 2 (boolean) — the choice's state.

**Return:** none.

**Body:** calls `0x00a20070` with the index byte, the state boolean and a fixed literal `1`. That helper, only if hosting a coop session (`0x0087ba20`, `==` polarity), opens a record-and-replicate block (opcode `0x45`, sub-id `0x28`), serializes the index byte plus both char parameters, and commits via the local-dispatch sibling `0x0086f1b0`/`0x0086eb20`; then, unconditionally, sets or clears bit `(1 << index)` of a persistent global bitmask (`0x026e7e60`) — the real storage for the game-choice state. Separately, if the always-true third parameter is set AND `index == 0` specifically, fires a distinct notify (`0x00710910`, code `4` or `5` by state) — a hardcoded special case tied to choice index `0`. Back in `game_choice_set_state`'s own body, a second, independent special case fires only when `index == 1`: a gated call to `0x00bd83c0` (proceeding only if three separate global enable-flags — `0x013123d1`/`0x029897a5`/`0x029897a6` — are all set) with a code of `15` (state true) or `16` (state false), building a small struct and dispatching through `0x00423cf0` — read as an achievement/stat-tracking event, cross-referenced by this same tranche's own `dlc_achievement_counter_set` (§15.27) touching the same subsystem area.

**Side effects/subsystem:** sets/clears bit `index` of the persistent global game-choice bitmask, replicating over the network when hosting (opcode `0x45`), and fires hardcoded stat/achievement side-events for two specific choice indices (`0` and `1`). Game-choice/dialogue-decision tracking + achievement/stat hooks. **[CONFIRMED — disassembly for the full chain, both special-cased indices, and the three-gate check on `0x00bd83c0`; OPEN — the real narrative identity of choice indices `0`/`1` was not independently corroborated (mechanism only, not meaning).]**

### 15.27 `dlc_achievement_counter_set` (`0x00a475c0`) — 10 calls

**Arguments:** 2 mandatory numbers, both read unconditionally via the flag/number-extractor pair. Arg 1 — a counter index. Arg 2 — a counter value.

**Body:** if arg 1 is `< 3`, writes arg 2 directly into a global array of exactly 3 dword slots (`0x027043bc`, indexed by arg 1). No bounds error, no replication, no read-back in this function.

**Side effects/subsystem:** sets one of exactly 3 global DLC-achievement-progress counters to an arbitrary value. DLC achievement/stat tracking. **[CONFIRMED — disassembly, full body; the array's own reader/consumer was not located in this batch — flagged as a real, narrow OPEN item.]** **[Resolved: the reader is `dlc_achievement_counter_get`, §20.25.]**

### 15.28 `character_parachute_detach` (`0x00a41cc0`) — 10 calls

**Arguments:** 1 mandatory string — a character name, resolved via `0x00a281a0`.

**Return:** none.

**Body:** on resolve success, calls `0x00995620(handle, 0, 1, 0)` — a plain 4-argument call, no hidden-`this` ambiguity here. That helper, if not already in a no-op state (checked via `0x008addb0`) and the fixed "force" parameter is false (as it always is from this call site), opens a genuine network-replicate record (opcode `0x41`, sub-id `0x1e`, via the true multi-target commit sibling `0x0086f110`), serializes the handle's position (`0x0050f790`) plus the two fixed byte parameters; otherwise it applies locally — clearing bit `0x04000000` at handle `+0xe8` and, if a linked object at handle `+0x1c` passes a type-descriptor-table check (bit `0x40` at offset `+9`, matched against a bit `0x1` at that object's own `+0xdc`), walking that object's own linked list to find the match and scheduling a delayed re-check via the already-established deadline/timestamp helper this document's §1.2 decompiles (`0x00d9e140`), reused here for a genuinely different purpose (computing a `1000`-or-`0` unit deadline depending on the third parameter). Regardless of outcome, `character_parachute_detach`'s own body then unconditionally calls `0x00d21f80`, a 1-instruction stub that always returns `1` — the same shared inert trivial-stub pattern this document's §10.9 already documents; its return value is discarded and it has no real side effect here.

**Side effects/subsystem:** forces a parachute detach on the named character, network-replicated (opcode `0x41`) when not already detached, or applied locally with a possible delayed re-check scheduled via the already-established deadline helper. Character/parachute state. **[CONFIRMED — disassembly, full body, including the reused deadline-helper cross-reference and the inert trivial-stub identification; OPEN — the linked object's own identity at handle `+0x1c`.]**

## 16. Ranks 251-350 tranche, part D — 15 UI-cluster functions (2026-09-30)

Fourth part of the four-way split covering ranks 251-350 (peer TSV: `D:\Project Crreish\TEAM B\tools\lua_reconciliation_called_and_registered_1181.tsv`, `cluster` column). Covers 15 `ui`-cluster names — rows 1-23 of the UI-cluster slice (ranks ~659-14 calls) are already specced (§2/§8/§11); the next 15 (rows 24-38 of that slice, ~13 down to 8 calls each) are this part's target set. 3 of the 15 (`game_get_language`, `game_award_respect`, `tutorial_set_hud_help_closing`) are in the 113-entry loop registrar (`0x00845aa0`); the other 12 are in the 311-entry UI-wrapper family anchored at `0x008430f0`, spread across 7 of its ~~48~~ 42 per-screen wrapper functions. Every function below opens with this document's already-established shared `lua_CFunction` prologue idiom (`lua_gettop`/`lua_type`/`lua_toboolean`/`lua_tolstring`/`lua_tonumber`+round-cast/`lua_pushboolean`/`lua_pushnumber`/`lua_pushstring`) — cited, not re-derived.

### 16.1 `game_get_language` (`0x00841c20`) — 113-name loop registrar, 12 calls/11 scripts

**Arguments:** none (only the boilerplate `lua_gettop` call, whose result is discarded — the wrapper prologue idiom running with nothing to extract).

**Return:** 1 string, pushed via `lua_pushstring` (`0x00dfe420`).

**Body:** calls a one-line helper (`0x00849920`) that indexes a small string table of ISO-style language codes at `0x0116409c` by a global current-language index (`0x01301a90`); if that index is negative, returns a fixed fallback string, ~~the literal `"null"`~~ the shared empty-string constant (`""`, byte-confirmed §8.25/§22.3), from `0x0129a0e3` instead. At least 12 real entries were read directly off the table: `US`, `ES`, `IT`, `JP`, `DE`, `FR`, `NL`, `SE`, `DK`, `CZ`, `PL`, `SK` (table not walked past entry 12, so this is a floor, not necessarily the full list). **[CONFIRMED — disassembly, both the outer wrapper and `0x00849920`'s own body read directly; table contents read as literal `.rdata` strings, not inferred.]**

**Side effects / subsystem:** none (pure read). Subsystem: localization/UI.

### 16.2 `game_award_respect` (`0x00843bf0`) — 113-name loop registrar, 13 calls/8 scripts

**Arguments:** 1 mandatory number (a quantity/count) + 3 optional trailing (two numbers, default `-1`, then one boolean, default `false`), all via this document's standard optional-countdown idiom.

**Return:** 1 number, pushed via `lua_pushnumber` (`0x00dfe3a0`) — the actual respect amount applied (see body).

**Body:** the mandatory arg (count) is multiplied by a global float constant read from `0x012fd1b0` (via a one-line accessor, `0x007bdb70`), rounded to an integer (`0x00dad900`), then passed through two further calls — `0x009da4e0` then `0x009e2440` — whose result is the actual applied amount. That amount is then routed either to a specific target (if the 2nd optional numeric arg is present: an opcode-tagged record opened via `0x00710cb0` using that arg's value as the target/opcode id) or broadcast via a fixed opcode `0xa1` record (same `0x00710cb0`, used elsewhere in this section family for "open an opcode-tagged record" — same idiom already documented for the record-and-replicate paths in §4.13's cross-function notes, just a different opcode literal here). If the 4th optional arg (boolean) is true, `0x006ced90` is additionally called — its own body (independently decompiled) checks two further globals and, if either is non-null, calls a further one-line function on each — consistent with an optional "show a respect-gained UI popup" notification, though that terminal call itself was not decompiled this pass.

**Two real disassembly-confirmed anomalies, deliberately flagged rather than silently resolved:**
1. **`0x007bdb70` is called with a genuine explicit stack argument here** (a small selector value, computed branchlessly as `6` if the 3rd optional numeric arg is absent, `3` if present — **corrected after adversarial review: the original write-up had this backwards**) **— but `0x007bdb70`'s own decompiled body takes zero parameters and only ever reads the global `0x012fd1b0`.** The pushed selector is never consumed inside the callee. **[CONFIRMED — disassembly for both the call site's explicit push and the callee's own parameterless body; OPEN — why the caller computes and passes an argument the callee ignores. Not necessarily a bug: possibly a shared calling convention with another, unlocated call site that DOES read it.]** (A second, superficially similar push at this same call site turned out on tracing to be an unrelated stack-slot reservation for a subsequent FPU store, not a second hidden argument — checked and ruled out, not assumed.)
2. **`0x009da4e0` is called here with one explicit argument (the rounded amount) and its result fed into `0x009e2440` (also called with only one explicit argument).** This is a real, disassembly-confirmed departure from `0x009da4e0`'s characterization everywhere else in this document (**corrected citation after adversarial review — §4.13 never actually mentions this address; the real citations are §3's front matter, first mention, and §11's front matter, where the address's own body is independently decompiled and confirmed as a true zero-argument accessor**): "a one-line accessor" resolving to **the current player object, called with zero arguments**. Likewise, `0x009e2440`'s own independently-decompiled body (elsewhere in this same helper chain) has 3 formal parameters, of which only 1 is actually supplied here. **[CONFIRMED — disassembly, both call sites' single explicit push, cross-checked against `0x009da4e0`'s well-established zero-argument shape elsewhere.] [OPEN — flagging for cross-check against §3/§11's own citations (not §4.13, which doesn't mention this address at all — see correction above) rather than asserting a resolution: either `0x009da4e0` is genuinely context/argument-sensitive (a different real behavior when called with 1 arg vs. 0), or this is evidence worth a future pass reconciling against the existing "current player, zero args" characterization. Not re-derived independently this pass, since doing so would mean re-opening §11's own finding rather than this section's own target.]**

**Side effects / subsystem:** grants respect (a scored/currency-like stat), opcode-tagged network-record-worthy (per the two `0x00710cb0` call shapes above, matching the same record-opening idiom this document already treats as network-replicate-relevant elsewhere), with an optional UI notification gate. Subsystem: player progression / notification.

**Note on a cosmetic-only decompiler quirk, checked and ruled out as a real anomaly:** this function's very first call (`lua_gettop`) decompiles as taking zero visible arguments (`0x00dfde50()`), unlike every other function in this document where it's rendered with the `L` parameter. Raw disassembly at the real prologue (a push of the register already holding `L`, immediately followed by the call to `0x00dfde50`) confirms `L` genuinely is pushed — this is purely a decompiler display artifact for this one call site, not a real missing/hidden argument. **[CONFIRMED — disassembly.]** The identical cosmetic quirk was independently observed and ruled out the same way at `pause_menu_control_scheme_init`'s own `lua_gettop` call (§16.11 below).

### 16.4 `completion_load_lut` (`0x007bdbd0`) — 311-entry UI-wrapper table, wrapper `0x007c04b0`, 10 calls/5 scripts

**Arguments:** 1 mandatory string (a LUT — color-lookup-table — name, or the literal `"none"`).

**Return:** none (`return 0;`).

**Body:** the argument is compared, case-insensitively, against the literal 4-character prefix `"none"` via the recognized C-runtime symbol `_strnicmp` (at `0x00ea632c`) — note this means any string starting with those 4 characters, not only an exact `"none"` match, satisfies the check. If it matches: a one-line setter (`0x00b9d2c0`, taking its target purely through a hidden/implicit ECX-register "this"-style pointer rather than a visible stack argument — a genuine hidden-argument decompiler artifact, confirmed by disassembly: `ECX` is loaded with the constant address `0x02282284` immediately before the call, on both branches) resets that global to `-1`; then a fixed slot index `2` is written with value `-1` and intensity `0.0` via two small parallel-array setters (`0x005deb30`, writes into a 4-slot array at `0x0149ab80`, bounds-checked `<4`; `0x005deb70`, writes into a second 4-slot array at `0x0149ab70`, unchecked). If the argument does NOT match `"none"`: a hashing/resolver helper (`0x00b9d740`) resolves the given LUT name to an id (also written into the SAME `0x02282284` global, through the same hidden-ECX-pointer convention, then further resolved through two more calls, `0x00dcecc0`/`0x00dced00`, ending in a write to a separate global `0x0290fa04` not otherwise used here), and slot `2` of the same two parallel arrays is set to that resolved id and intensity `1.0`.

**Side effects / subsystem:** writes into a small, fixed-size (4-slot) color-grading LUT-selection + intensity array — always slot `2` — either clearing it (LUT off) or pointing it at a resolved, named color-grading LUT with full intensity. Subsystem: post-process/color-grading, gated on the completion/cutscene-screen context by name (`completion_*`). **[CONFIRMED — disassembly for the whole control-flow and both hidden-ECX-pointer call sites; HIGH CONFIDENCE for the semantic role of slot `2` and the two parallel arrays as "LUT id" / "intensity", inferred from the literal values written (`-1`/`0.0` vs. resolved-id/`1.0`), not independently cross-checked against a consumer.]**

### 16.7 `pcr_change_composite` (`0x00835760`) — same wrapper, 12 calls/4 scripts

**Arguments:** 3 mandatory (string, number, number) + 2 optional trailing numbers (defaults `1.0` and `0`, each individually nil/type-gated per this document's standard optional idiom).

**Return:** none (`return 0;`).

**Body — the largest and most branchy of the 15, summarized rather than exhaustively enumerated, matching this document's own house style for switch/branch-heavy dispatchers:** the mandatory string (arg1) is looked up case-insensitively against a 34-entry category-name table at `0x0130b7f0` (real literal strings read directly: `lips`, `eyes`, `tattoo upper/lower/entire arm left/right`, `tattoo upper/lower/entire chest`, `tattoo upper/lower/entire back`, `tattoo head`/`neck`/`leg left`/`leg right`/`hand left`/`hand right`, `body mask`, `shaderball`, `fingernails`, `fingernails_alt`, `body diffuse`, `makeup eyeliner`/`eyeshadow`/`cheeks`/`entire face`, `eyebrows`, `facial hair`, `body hair`, `face features`, `face items`) via the recognized C-runtime symbol `_stricmp`, yielding a category index (`-1` if unmatched). Otherwise, depending on the resolved category and the optional args, the function either (a) resolves and applies a `"Standard_2"`-named composite/material variant with an RGB tint computed from a per-item color-list entry (each channel individually run through a shared inverse-gamma helper, see the anomaly below), writing the tint into the item via `0x009f1f40`, or (b) walks the SAME 63-slot ("up to `0x3f`") per-character customization-item list `pcr_change_hair`'s own shared helper (`0x00836b10`) uses (`0x026533ac`/`0x026533b0` = per-item category+id array, `0x0265430c`/`0x02654304` = a parallel per-category-definition table, `0x026534b0` = per-item RGB tint storage, `0x02653384` = a per-character "list changed" dirty flag, `0x02654320`/`0x02654328` = a per-category flags/style-count table) to add, update, or clear one item in that list via `0x009f98e0` (remove/compact) and `0x009f9f60` (set/clear an item's tint), with a special-cased extra call for category id `0x16` (`22`, most plausibly the `fingernails` entry from the 34-name table above, HIGH CONFIDENCE — inferred from the id number alone, not independently cross-checked) that also applies the same tint to a second, literal-named item, `"fingernails_r"`.

**A genuine, confirmed hidden-argument case, worth flagging on its own:** the shared per-channel color helper `0x00832230` is called (3 times per RGB tint) with **zero visible stack arguments** in the decompiled listing, and its own decompiled body reads an undeclared, purely-implicit low byte of the `EAX` register as its sole real input (**reworded after adversarial review — the original text quoted the decompiler's own auto-named pseudo-variable for this, a clean-room-style issue, not a factual one; the underlying claim itself was independently re-verified and confirmed correct**). Raw disassembly at all 3 call sites confirms this precisely: each call is immediately preceded by a truncating double-to-int conversion into `EAX` (computing an sRGB-scaled `0`-`255` channel value into `EAX`, hence its low byte `AL`), with no stack push at all. `0x00832230`'s own body applies the low-end branch of the standard sRGB linear-to-encoded threshold test (if the channel, normalized to `0.0`-`1.0`, is `<= 0.03928`, leave it as-is; otherwise call a further function, `0x00ea4300`, with the same value) — consistent with a per-channel gamma-correction step ahead of writing a UI-picked color into the material system. **[CONFIRMED — disassembly, the hidden-AL-register argument at all 3 call sites and the callee's own body; HIGH CONFIDENCE that this is an sRGB gamma-correction step; OPEN — `0x00ea4300`'s own body was not decompiled this pass, so the exact final transform and where its result is written back to is not resolved.]**

**Side effects / subsystem:** character customization (plastic-surgeon "composite"/tattoo/makeup/paint-item slots), shares its core list-management primitives with `pcr_change_hair` (§16.6) — see cross-function note below. **[CONFIRMED — disassembly for the category-name lookup, the shared-list-primitive identification, and the hidden-AL-argument color helper; HIGH CONFIDENCE for individual field/table semantic roles; OPEN for `0x00821740`/`0x008245f0`/`0x00825010`'s own exact internal bodies, and for `0x00ea4300`.]** **[Resolved for `0x00825010`: §19.12.]**

### 16.8 `pcr_get_player_preset` (`0x00830790`) — same wrapper, 11 calls/2 scripts

**Arguments:** none.

**Return:** 3 strings (gender, ethnicity, body-type), each pushed via `lua_pushstring` (`0x00dfe420`) — OR 0 return values if there is no current player.

**Body:** fetches the current player via the shared zero-argument accessor `0x009da4e0`; if null, returns immediately with no pushes. Otherwise pushes 3 strings: a table lookup at `0x01160028` indexed by a byte field at player-object offset `+0xa41`; a second table lookup at `0x01160030` indexed by a byte field at `+0xa40`; and the literal, hardcoded string `"average"` (not data-driven at all). The two lookup tables are the SAME underlying `.rdata` string block, just at two different base offsets 8 bytes apart (`0x01160028`: `male`, `female`, `asian`, `black`, `hispanic`, `white`, ...; `0x01160030`: `asian`, `black`, `hispanic`, `white`, ...) — most plausibly two separate, adjacently-placed tables (a 2-entry gender table and a 4-entry ethnicity table) rather than one logical 6-entry table, though the exact boundary between them was not independently confirmed (no bounds-check instruction was found gating either index). **[CONFIRMED — disassembly for the whole control flow and the literal table/string contents; the "two adjacent tables, not one" reading and the `+0xa40`/`+0xa41` fields' gender/ethnicity roles are now also CONFIRMED (2026-10-02, player-gender initial-state investigation, writers cross-checked directly) — see below.]**

**Producers of `+0xa41`/`+0xa40`, RESOLVED (2026-10-02, player-gender initial-state investigation — previously OPEN):** the character constructor `0x00954340` writes the literal "unspecified" sentinels `+0xa41` := 3, `+0xa40` := 5 (outside both lookup tables above, by design — they are the exact results the engine's own `Gender`/`Race` text parsers, `0x00831fc0`/`0x00832000`, give for an unrecognised or absent string); the character-record reader `0x0096ec80` then copies the character's own `character.xtbl` row gender field into `+0xa41` only (never `+0xa40`); the preset-apply routine `0x00836d90` (reached from a save load `0x00b97510`, the co-op-guest record load `0x00bcaef0`, the fresh-game default-preset step `0x008373d0`, the Lua-bound `pcr_apply_preset` `0x00837640`, and the horde-mode look `0x006e5180`) writes both bytes from a `player_presets.xtbl` preset record's own `+0x5d`/`+0x5c` fields; and the new Lua entry `pcr_set_identity` (`0x00830fa0`, below) writes `+0xa41` only. For the player object specifically, `character.xtbl`'s own `StyleTest_PC` row carries no `Gender`, so `0x0096ec80` leaves `+0xa41` at the "unspecified" 3 it already had — **a freshly created player object genuinely holds `+0xa41` = 3, `+0xa40` = 5 until game-start step `0x00708330` applies exactly one of: a loaded save's own character-record bytes (file offset `+0x203c`/`+0x203d`), the `player_presets.xtbl` row marked `Default` (shipped data: `male_white` = 0/3) on a fresh game, or the co-op session's delivered guest record** — full mechanism and real-save-sample cross-check (16/16 samples agree with the worn body item) in `spec-save-format.md` §10.4. No Lua script ever sees the raw 3/5 sentinel pair in a real run.

**Arguments:** 1 mandatory string, compared case-insensitively against `"male"`.

### 16.11 `pause_menu_control_scheme_init` (`0x007e1110`) — 311-entry UI-wrapper table, wrapper `0x007e18e0`, 11 calls/3 scripts

**Arguments:** 1 mandatory boolean (arg1) + 1 optional number (arg2, control-scheme id, default `-1`).

**Return:** 0, 2, or 3 numbers, pushed via `lua_pushnumber` (`0x00dfe3a0`) — genuinely variable, and the return count is computed to always match the real number of pushes (checked explicitly, no mismatch).

**Body:** if arg1 (boolean) is false, returns immediately with **zero** pushes. Otherwise: stores arg2 (the scheme id) into a global, `0x0229a558`; pushes the literal number `0.0`; then, only if the scheme id is exactly `0` or exactly `1`/`2`, fetches a second value — a stored preset id from one of two globals (`0x01411b08` for scheme `0`, via `0x005bc180`; `0x01411b10` for scheme `1`/`2`, via `0x005bc190`) — and pushes it as a second number; for any other scheme id, this second push is skipped entirely. Finally, always (as long as arg1 was true), pushes one more literal number, decoded precisely from its raw IEEE-754 double bit pattern (`0x4039000000000000`) as **`25.0`**.

**Side effects / subsystem:** records the currently-being-edited control scheme id as global UI state, and reports back up to 3 seed values for whatever UI slider/selector is initializing (most plausibly: a tab/category marker `0.0`, a previously-saved preset id when the scheme is a recognized one, and a fixed range-max constant `25.0`, e.g. a sensitivity-slider ceiling). **[CONFIRMED — disassembly for the full control flow, every push, and the decoded double literal; HIGH CONFIDENCE — inferred for the semantic roles of the 3 pushed values.]**

### 16.12 `pause_menu_update_option` (`0x007e13e0`) — same wrapper, 9 calls/9 scripts

**Arguments:** 2 mandatory numbers (option id, category id) + 1 mandatory boolean + 1 optional number (a float value, default `0.0`).

**Return:** none (`return 0;`).

**Body:** a large, two-level `switch` (outer on category, inner on option id) mapping specific `(category, option)` pairs to one of ~25 individual engine setters — representative examples read directly: category `0`/option `2` → `0x00aef8c0` (also used by the "restore defaults" counterpart, §16.13); category `1`/option `5` or `6` → a value-remap helper (`0x007dfc30`) feeding mouse-sensitivity globals `0x013c898c`/`0x013c8988`; category `4` (options `1`-`4`) → a shared audio-bus volume setter `0x00462910` called with a fixed bus-index literal per option; category `6`/options `3`-`4` → `0x005bc440`/`0x005bc3e0` fed a remapped `value*1.2+0.05`. Before the switch, both numeric args and the boolean and float are formatted through a shared display-label resolver, `0x007dfff0` (used only for its side effect of producing/logging a human-readable settings label — its own return value is discarded at this call site).

**A genuine, confirmed hidden-argument case in the call to `0x007dfff0`:** the decompiled call site shows only 2 explicit arguments (option id, float value), but raw disassembly confirms a 3rd, purely-implicit register argument — `EAX` is loaded with the category id (the SAME value driving this function's own outer switch) immediately before the call — matching `0x007dfff0`'s own independently-decompiled body, which reads that same undeclared `EAX` register for its OWN outer switch (**reworded after adversarial review to avoid quoting the decompiler's own auto-named pseudo-variable — the underlying claim was independently re-verified and confirmed correct**). A 4th value (a byte, loaded into `CL` from the boolean argument's stack slot) is also loaded into a register immediately before the call but was not found to be read anywhere in `0x007dfff0`'s own visible logic — flagged OPEN rather than asserted either way. **[CONFIRMED — disassembly, the hidden-EAX category argument and its match against the callee's own EAX read; OPEN — the loaded-but-seemingly-unread CL/boolean value.]**

**Side effects / subsystem:** applies one live options-menu setting change immediately as the user adjusts it in the UI (audio volumes, mouse-sensitivity curves, gamma/brightness, control-inversion flags, vsync flags, vibration, subtitles, southpaw control scheme, radio-on-by-default, static-minimap, pause-on-focus-loss, crouch-toggle, airplane controls, veh-camera-snap — full case enumeration not reproduced here, matching this document's own house style of summarizing large switch dispatchers rather than exhaustively listing every case). Subsystem: pause-menu options.

### 16.16 Cross-function observations

- **Shared "current player" accessor `0x009da4e0`** (**corrected citation after adversarial review — the real citations are §3's front matter, first mention, and §11's front matter, where the address's own body is independently decompiled and confirmed; not §4.13, which never mentions this address**, a zero-argument, one-line accessor resolving the current player object, backing the `"#PLAYER#"` name-resolver sentinel) is used identically (zero args) by `pcr_change_hair` (via its shared helper `0x00836b10`), `pcr_change_composite`, and `pcr_get_player_preset` in this tranche — but is called with **one explicit argument** inside `game_award_respect` (§16.2), a genuine, disassembly-confirmed exception to its established shape, flagged there for a future cross-check rather than resolved here.
- **`pcr_change_hair` and `pcr_change_composite` are two front ends onto the same underlying "per-character customization item list" mechanism** — a fixed 63-slot-per-character list (`0x026533ac`/`0x026533b0`), a parallel per-category-definition table (`0x0265430c`/`0x02654304`), per-item RGB tint storage (`0x026534b0`), a per-character dirty flag (`0x02653384`), and per-category flags/style-count (`0x02654320`/`0x02654328`), all hung off the current player's edit-session sub-object at `+0x2088`. `pcr_change_hair` reaches this list only through the shared helper `0x00836b10`; `pcr_change_composite` uses that same helper AND walks the list directly for its non-hair categories. Neither `pcr_get_player_preset`'s own `+0xa40`/`+0xa41` fields, nor `pcr_change_hair`'s category-mapping table `0x01300cf4`, were found written by anything decompiled this pass — their producers remain OPEN.
- **`pause_menu_update_option` and `pause_menu_restore_defaults` are a confirmed live-edit/restore-defaults pair** sharing an identical category numbering and calling, field-for-field, the same ~15 individual setter functions — cross-checked directly, not assumed from the names alone (per this project's own standing caution against naming a function's role from its callers' shared need without checking the body — here the body-level match was actually verified).
- **Two genuinely new hidden-argument decompiler artifacts identified this pass**, beyond the ones already on record in this document's front matter/§10: (1) `0x00832230`'s hidden `AL`-register byte argument (an sRGB gamma-correction helper, inside `pcr_change_composite`); (2) `0x007dfff0`'s hidden `EAX`-register category argument (inside `pause_menu_update_option`, where the decompiled call site shows only 2 of the callee's real inputs). Both confirmed by raw disassembly, not inferred from the pseudocode's argument count alone.
- **One real, unresolved discrepancy** (`0x009e2440` called with 1 explicit argument in `game_award_respect` against an independently-decompiled 3-parameter signature elsewhere) is left OPEN rather than guessed at, consistent with `WALLS.md`'s standing caution against asserting a bitfield/argument's meaning from position alone without independent confirmation.
- **`0x00dfe420` (`lua_pushstring`) and `0x009da4e0` (current-player accessor)** — both already CONFIRMED/documented elsewhere in this document (§2's method note, confirmed §8's intro, for `0x00dfe420`; **§3's front matter/§11's front matter for `0x009da4e0` specifically — corrected after adversarial review, not §4.13, which never mentions this address**) — are reused, not re-derived, throughout this tranche, per the task's own instruction.

### 17.1 `vehicle_set_script_hard_goto` (`0x00a631d0`) — 13 calls / 7 scripts

**Arguments:** 1 mandatory string (vehicle name or `"#PLAYER#"`) + 1 boolean read with no nil/absence gate (default `false` via `lua_toboolean`'s own nil-handling, same un-gated shape §7.14/§7.20/§7.26/§7.29 already document).

**Return:** none.

**Body:** the name resolves through the dedicated object-to-vehicle-instance resolver `0x00a281e0` (the SAME resolver `vehicle_suppress_npc_exit` uses, `spec-lua-api-behaviour.md` §4.5). If resolved, a setter is invoked — **confirmed via raw disassembly, not just decompiled pseudocode:** the resolved vehicle instance is never passed as a plain stack argument; the compiler computes `vehicle_instance + 0xc68` — the SAME per-vehicle sub-record §4.5 already documents (there holding the NPC-exit-suppression bits at the sub-record's own `+0x4`) — and loads that computed address into ECX as the implicit `this` for a `__thiscall` to `0x00b237e0`, with only the boolean pushed as the one visible stack argument. Inside `0x00b237e0`, the double-gate record-and-replicate idiom (`0x008ae480` then `0x008837a0`, §7's "variant 1") is checked using an identity pair read from the sub-record's own `+0x4e0`/`+0x4e4` (i.e. absolute vehicle offsets `+0x1148`/`+0x114c`): both-false → opens a network record, opcode `0x46`, debug tags `"vehicle_ai"` + `"vai_force_flagsscript_hard_goto"`; otherwise → sets bit `0x4` of the byte at the sub-record's own `+0x5` to the boolean's value (the standard branchless conditional-set idiom, not an unconditional flip) (absolute vehicle `+0xc6d`).

**Side effects / subsystem:** per-vehicle AI-behaviour flag (script-forced pathing override), network-replicated. ~~This is the FIRST confirmed use of the double-gate/opcode-`0x46` idiom on a VEHICLE object rather than a character — a genuine domain extension of a pattern §7 only observed on characters.~~ (Not the first vehicle use: §9.8/§9.13/§13.8/§13.28/§15.19 already use this idiom on vehicles.) **[CONFIRMED — disassembly for the hidden-`this` computation, the exact sub-record address, and the gate/bit; the sub-record's own `+0x4e0`/`+0x4e4` identity-pair offset is a THIRD distinct offset pair for this shared helper family, alongside the already-documented `+8`/`+0xc` and `+0x610`/`+0x614` pairs (§7.33).]**

### 18.1 `cash_add` (`0x00a42ef0`) — 10 calls / 3 scripts

**Arguments:** 1 mandatory number (a cash amount, read via `lua_tonumber`/`0x00dfe160`+round, unconditional — no countdown check at all, unlike most mandatory-arg idioms in this document). 1 optional string, standard nil-gated idiom, default the literal `"#PLAYER1#"` — **a further confirmed instance of the already-documented second player sentinel** (`spec-lua-api-behaviour.md`'s own citations at the vehicle-reference-resolver family and `inv_item_remove`'s default) — this sentinel is evidently not unique to those two call sites.

**Return:** none (`return 0;`).

**Body:** the target resolves through the generic resolver (`0x00a280c0`). On success, the raw cash amount is scaled ×100 and saturated to ±2,000,000,000 (a dedicated clamp helper, `0x009601d0`, `__thiscall`, stores the result through its own hidden `this`) before being handed to a delegate, `0x0094d920` (`__thiscall`, this = resolved target), together with a literal flag `13`. That delegate branches on the already-established single-gate `0x008addb0`: the true (local-apply) branch does a reward-style UI computation (a helper chain including `0x0091f5e0`, `0x0071b7b0`, and two calls to `0x00710cb0` with a small mode code `2`/`3` plus a float pointer, then a commit call `0x0094a800`); the false branch builds and sends a genuine network-replicated record — opcode `0x46`, tags `"human"` + `"cash_adjust"` (both new literal debug tags, not previously cited), a truncated network id for the target, a time-quantized cash-delta field, and the literal `13`, committed via the already-established genuine multi-target sibling `0x0086f110`.

**Flagged, not resolved:** `0x00710cb0` is called here with **two** explicit arguments (a small int code + a float pointer) — a different shape from `game_award_respect`'s own already-documented characterization of `0x00710cb0` ("using that arg's value as the target/opcode id", one argument). Either `0x00710cb0` is context/argument-count-sensitive at different call sites (matching the exact pattern `game_award_respect`'s own entry already flags for `0x009da4e0`/`0x009e2440`), or this is a distinct overload. Not independently raw-disassembly-confirmed, since `0x0094d920` is a depth-1 callee outside this pass's raw-disassembly budget (which covered the 30 targets themselves only) — **OPEN**.

**Side effects/subsystem:** grants (or, given the signed clamp, potentially removes) cash to/from a resolved character, either as an immediate local UI-feedback+wallet-apply path or as a network-replicated record, depending on replication-authority context. ### 18.9 `player_release_human_shield` (`0x00a598d0`) — 9 calls / 8 scripts

**Arguments:** 1 mandatory string (character name). 1 optional boolean, standard nil-gated idiom, default `false` (a "release forcibly"-style flag). 1 further optional boolean, same idiom, default `false`.

**Return:** 1 boolean, pushed via `lua_pushboolean` — the actual result of the release attempt.

**Body:** resolves via the generic resolver `0x00a280c0`. On success, delegates to `0x009ad6d0(handle, 1, boolA, boolB)` and pushes its byte return; on failure, pushes `false` directly (still returning 1 value either way).

`0x009ad6d0` (fully decompiled, a genuinely rich state machine): first validates the handle is either currently the shielded party OR its cached shielder-partner matches the SAME position pair as the current global human-shield holder (`0x009da4e0`'s already-established zero-arg current-holder getter, here re-confirmed reused). If NOT the local authority for this release, it instead builds a genuine network record — opcode `0x41`, sub-tag `0x3a`/58, forwarding all three caller arguments, committed via the genuine multi-target `0x0086f110`. If it IS the local authority: `boolA` true → forcibly ejects the shield partner with a small upward/forward offset derived from the partner's own velocity-like fields (`+0x40`/`+0x44`/`+0x48` plus scaled adjacent fields), via a vtable `+0x44` call; `boolB` true → calls an unrelated, un-decompiled helper `0x009ad200` (plausibly a "delayed release" path; **[Resolved: see §22.26 for 0x009ad200's body]**); otherwise (normal release) → runs two further gates (`0x0091f5e0`/`0x009feeb0`) and, if a partner is found and the shield state is exactly `1`, plays a resolved sound/state cue via `0x00964b00`, waits `500`–`2000` ms (`0x00d9e180`), and sets BOTH parties' shield-state byte at `+0x18d4` to `4` (a "cooldown/just-released" state, distinct from the active-shield state `1` this document doesn't otherwise catalogue for that field).

**Side effects/subsystem:** ends a human-shield hold, either locally (with three distinct sub-behaviors selected by the two booleans) or via network replication when not the authoritative party. Subsystem: player combat/human-shield state. **[CONFIRMED — disassembly for the full authority/branch structure and the state-byte transition; OPEN — `0x009ad200`'s own body (**[Resolved: §22.26]**), and the exact real-world meaning of shield-state value `4`.]**

**Side effects/subsystem:** enables/disables exactly one fixed parking-spot slot (index `1`) — a real, confirmed naming/behavior mismatch, not a per-argument "which slot" or genuine "all slots" operation. **[CONFIRMED — disassembly, raw-disassembly-verified hidden-argument correction at the target level — the single most notable finding in this tranche for the task's own "check raw disassembly when the call-site argument count looks off" instruction.]**

### 19.14 `pcr_set_anim` (0x00832bc0) — wrapper 0x008377d0 ("pcr")

**Arguments:** 2 — arg1 mandatory string (an anim-category name), arg2 mandatory number (an anim id), neither gated.

**A genuine, confirmed hidden-register-argument case, found specifically because the decompiled pseudocode made arg1 LOOK unused — checked via raw disassembly per this document's standing practice for exactly this situation.** The decompiled body shows the `lua_tolstring` call for arg1 rendered as a bare statement with its return value seemingly discarded. Raw disassembly proves otherwise: the very next instruction after that call moves the just-returned string pointer (in EAX) into the callee-saved EDI register, which is never touched again until, several instructions later, `CALL 0x008307f0` is made with **zero visible stack arguments** — i.e., arg1's string genuinely IS forwarded, as a deliberate hidden register argument, to 0x008307f0. Independently confirmed by reading the real 4-entry string table 0x008307f0 scans via `_stricmp` (base `0x01300d44`, read directly): `"melee_combat_style"`, `"taunt_style"`, `"compliment_style"`, `"facial_expression_style"` — real literal strings, not inferred.

**Body:** 0x008307f0 returns the matched table index (0-3) or `-1` if the forwarded string is null/unmatched; `pcr_set_anim` then only does real work for indices `1`/`2`/`3` (`taunt_style`/`compliment_style`/`facial_expression_style`) — **index `0` (`"melee_combat_style"`) takes the exact same no-op path as an unmatched name**, a genuine, disassembly-confirmed asymmetry worth flagging rather than assuming all 4 categories are equally supported by this particular entry point. For index `1`: bounds-checks arg2 against a count global (0x023008a4) and, if the bounds check passes, writes arg2 into the current player's `+0x28b4` byte **unconditionally** — **CORRECTED, 2026-09-30, adversarial review (`addc799ec56a058c3`), raw disassembly re-checked: this write is NOT gated by the "currently active style category" tracker (0x01300d90) as originally claimed; the `CMP` against the tracker sets flags used only by the LATER `JNZ`, and the field write sits between the `CMP` and that `JNZ`, so it always executes once the bounds check passes.** Only the SECONDARY step — caching a resolved value from a parallel data table (0x0230089c) into 0x01300d94 — is actually gated on the tracker already equalling `1`. Index `2` is the structurally identical sibling (`+0x28b5`, count `0x023008a8`, table `0x023008a0`, tracker value `2`) — same correction applies: the `+0x28b5` field write is unconditional once bounds-checked; only its own secondary cache write is tracker-gated. Index `3` is a third variant writing into `+0xd28` and a global `0x01300d98`, offset by a literal `+0xf3` (243) — **this branch's gating IS correctly described as originally written: raw disassembly confirms its `JNZ` immediately follows its `CMP` with no write in between, so the `+0xd28` write itself genuinely is gated on tracker value `3` (and arg2 `< 0xf`)** — the correction above applies only to indices `1`/`2`, not `3`.

**Side effects/subsystem:** character customization (plastic-surgeon preview-animation category selection — voice/taunt/compliment/facial-expression "style" slots). **[CONFIRMED — disassembly for the hidden-EDI argument (a SECOND independent confirmed instance of this exact convention this pass, alongside item 11's 0x008194f0 calls), the real 4-string table contents, and the full branch structure; OPEN — 0x01300d90's own writer(s) elsewhere, not traced.]**

Item 5's own record/event mechanism (0x00e0xxxx family) is a genuinely different, unidentified mechanism, flagged OPEN rather than assumed to be the same idiom. **[Resolved: §26.23.]**

## 20. Ranks 351-450 tranche, part C — 32 gameplay-cluster functions (2026-09-30)

Third part of a fresh four-part tranche, "ranks 351-450." All 4 parts' name lists were computed centrally up front (grepped the live spec's own already-covered names out of the peer TSV, split gameplay into 3 parts and UI-cluster into a 4th) and handed to each agent as an explicit list, eliminating the rank-arithmetic collision problem that affected the 251-350 tranche's own "Part C." Addresses resolved from `tools/scratchpad/lua_gameplay_1014_raw_pairs.txt` (all 32 confirmed present). Every entry below reuses this document's own already-established shared primitives (the standard `lua_CFunction` prologue idiom, the resolver families, the gate/record-and-replicate idioms) by citation, not re-derivation.

### 20.1 `vehicle_set_vulnerable` (0x00a634f0)

**Arguments:** 1 mandatory string (vehicle name). No boolean argument exists at all.

**Return:** none.

**Body:** resolves via the already-established dedicated vehicle resolver 0x00a281e0 (§4.5/§18.20). On success, delegates (thiscall, this = resolved vehicle) to 0x00a7a830(vehicle, **false** — hardcoded literal 0, never taken from a Lua argument). 0x00a7a830 is a double-gate (variant 1) setter, the exact established shape (0x008ae480 then 0x008837a0): both-false → record, opcode 0x46, tags "vehicle" + "m_force_flagsinvulnerable", position pair +8/+0xc, committed via the genuine multi-target 0x0086f110; otherwise → sets/clears ~~bit 0x8~~ **bit `0x01`** of the byte at +0x1d7a to the boolean (always false here) ~~**[OPEN — conflict: §3.7 gives bit `0x01` at `+0x1d7a` for this same setter 0x00a7a830, and §21.30 assigns bit 0x8 at `+0x1d7a` to a different setter; to be re-derived]**~~ **RESOLVED (2026-10-02, ranking tranche 14, §46.1): CONFIRMED by direct disassembly of the merge idiom (`0x00a7a955`-`0x00a7a965`: load, XOR with the argument, AND `0x1`, XOR back — no shift) — this entry's own `0x8` was simply wrong; §3.7's `0x01` was right all along. The reader `vehicle_is_invulnerable` (§46.5/tranche 14 E.10) tests the same bit `0x01`.**

**Side effects/subsystem:** because the boolean is permanently hardcoded false, this Lua entry point can only ever CLEAR the "invulnerable" flag — i.e. it always makes the target vulnerable; it is not a toggle (turn_invulnerable/vehicle_set_invulnerable, already documented, own the "set true" side). **[CONFIRMED — disassembly, including the hardcoded-false confirmation via raw disassembly at the call site.]**

### 20.2 `vehicle_repair` (0x00a64370)

**Arguments:** 1 mandatory string (vehicle name). 1 optional number (a repair fraction), standard nil-gated idiom, default the same fixed float constant already cited at §18.13/helicopters_set_jitter_override (0x01117a4c). 1 further optional number, rounded via lua_tonumber+round, default sentinel -1.

**Return:** none.

**Body:** resolves via 0x00a281e0. Also calls a trivial always-returns-1 stub (0x00d225f0) whose result is discarded — inert at this call site. On success, delegates to 0x00a9f980(vehicle, repairFraction, roundedArg, **true**, **true** — both hardcoded, not tied to any Lua argument).

0x00a9f980 (fully decompiled): only proceeds if the repair fraction is positive. Single-gate (0x008addb0) authority check. If not authoritative (or a separate unresolved zero-arg predicate at 0x007553b0 is false): opens a record — opcode 0x42, sub-header literal 0x12/18, the vehicle's network id (0x0050f790), the repair fraction and rounded arg (each conditionally appended, standard capacity-check boilerplate — not content-conditional), the first hardcoded-true boolean; committed via the genuine multi-target 0x0086f110 (sync id via 0x008ae020, already cross-referenced at §15.15/§15.21/§15.29) when not authoritative, or via the local-only sibling 0x0086f1b0 (sync id via the host-check helper 0x0087ba20) when it IS the authoritative machine and the second hardcoded-true boolean is set.

Regardless of the record, when the vehicle has a live sub-object at +0x1e00 with a capability byte set AND the flag at +0xbd0 is set: walks the SAME sub-component array §13.20 already establishes (base +0x68c, count via the +0x1e00 sub-object's own +0x390, gated on +0xbd0) resetting/repairing each entry (0x00a77e20/0x00a8bdc0/0x00a88f90/0x00a88770/0x00a896a0/0x00a88bf0/0x00a9c3b0/0x00b12440/0x00ae7060), clears damage-state bits at +0x163d/+0x163c, recomputes physics (0x00aa2be0/0x00aa2b70), and — the actual "heal" step — computes a repair amount scaled by the vehicle's own +0x155c field times the repair fraction and applies it as a NEGATED value through a vehicle-specific position-delta apply primitive, 0x00a9f4f0 (a different address from character_damage's own 0x0096fa20, item 32, but the SAME conceptual "negative damage = healing" design). If not authoritative, current HP (+0x1564) is zeroed first (so the negated "repair" delta becomes the new value once applied elsewhere) — the exact mirrored-authority split this document's damage/HP family already establishes.

**Side effects/subsystem:** repairs a resolved vehicle proportional to a fractional argument, propagating to its sub-components, plus a record-and-replicate step. **[CONFIRMED — disassembly for the whole chain; OPEN — 0x00a9f4f0's own full internals (a depth-2 callee outside this pass's raw-disassembly budget) and 0x007553b0's identity.]**

**Body — a 4-stage resolver cascade, each stage reading a DIFFERENT team-id-byte offset off its own kind of handle:**
1. Generic resolver 0x00a280c0: if it succeeds, reads the resolved handle's own team-id byte at **+0x1ca8**.
2. Else, the already-established #FOLLOWER# family (0x00a26010 name match + 0x00a26110 index resolve, §3's own front-matter citation): if the name matches AND resolves to a live follower, reads the SAME +0x1ca8 offset off that handle; if the name matched the #FOLLOWER# pattern but resolution failed, pushes nil directly (does not fall through to the remaining stages).
3. Else (name is not a #FOLLOWER# sentinel at all), the character-kind resolver 0x005e4dd0 (bit 0x4 at +0xb of 0x02cc9900) + liveness: reads team-id byte at **+0xf0** on THAT handle.
4. Else the vehicle-kind resolver 0x0062a190 (bit 0x8 at +0xb) + liveness + vtable +0x70: reads team-id byte at **+0x16e0** — **the exact same field vehicle_set_team (§18.20) writes**, closing a clean write/read loop across the two documents' own tranches.

Every successful path converts the id byte to a name string via 0x0094f3c0 → 0x0094dc60, both operating against table **0x02623a80**.

**A tooling caution worth flagging:** 0x02623a80 is the SAME address WALLS.md's own emulator-harness section already flags as notoriety_force_no_spawn's (§3.6) name→code table, confirmed to be **runtime-populated, not file-backed** (it lands past its section's raw-data size in the PE image). get_team's own reverse (id→name) lookup depends on that same table being populated — meaning a cold/static read of this table (as opposed to decompiling the CODE, which is what this pass did) would silently return empty/wrong results; the code-level behavior above is confirmed by disassembly, but the actual NAME STRINGS get_team would return at runtime cannot be independently verified without a live process, per WALLS.md's own already-documented caution.

**Side effects/subsystem:** none (pure query). **[CONFIRMED — disassembly for the whole 4-stage cascade and all four field offsets; the runtime-table caution above is inherited from WALLS.md's existing, unresolved emulator finding, not re-derived.]**

### 20.24 `get_object_pos` (0x00a4c200)

**Arguments:** 1 mandatory string (object name).

**Return:** ALWAYS exactly 6 numbers (lua_pushnumber ×6): on success, the object's real world position (x, y, z, each cast float→double) followed by 3 MORE numbers; on failure, only those same 3 numbers (3 total, not 6) (i.e. 6 numbers on success; 3 numbers — the fixed 0x0112a1e0 constant ×3 — on failure; "ALWAYS exactly 6" above is superseded by this).

**A confirmed, notable finding:** the trailing 3 numbers are, in EVERY case (success or failure), the exact same fixed constant (0x0112a1e0) repeated three times — never anything object-derived. If a caller expects real orientation/rotation data in those slots, the shipped binary never supplies it; they are permanently dead/placeholder output.

**Body (the position half):** resolves via a rich cascade inside 0x00a455a0: (1) the generic resolver 0x00a280c0 — reads a 44-byte position+orientation transform block directly at the resolved handle's own +0x40..+0x6c. (2) Else, if given a non-null name, the already-established "genuinely new" by-name resolver 0x00734e90 (§10.5/§12.23/§14.31/§17.4's own citation) + liveness: depending on which of several descriptor bits the resolved kind carries (row-offset +0xb any of bits 0-3, or +0xa bit 0x80, or +7 bit 0x2), it either (2a) — when +0xa bit 0x8 is ALSO set — goes through a capability gate (vtable +0x68) and producer (vtable +0x70), then 0x004e43f0→0x009b9160→0x009b9130→**the already-documented shared underlying-table resolver 0x004dcf00** (§18.31's own cross-reference #1) to reach a final object and read ITS +0x40..+0x6c block (falling back to the intermediate object's own +0x40..+0x6c if the 0x009b9160 check fails); or (2b) — when +0xb bit 0x1 is set instead — calls a zero-visible-argument fixed-transform helper (0x008034f0) combined with a further fixed constant block (0x01321400..0x01321420); or (2c) — neither bit — reads the 0x00734e90-resolved object's OWN +0x40..+0x6c block directly.

**Side effects/subsystem:** none (pure query). A rich, multi-path position resolver reusing two already-documented cross-cutting resolvers (0x00734e90 and 0x004dcf00) in the SAME function for the first time this document has observed. **[CONFIRMED — disassembly for the top-level cascade and the always-3-fallback-values finding; HIGH CONFIDENCE — inferred for the semantic roles of the three descriptor-bit sub-branches; OPEN — 0x008034f0's own body.]**

### 20.28 `character_is_jumping` (0x00a41710)

**Arguments:** 1 mandatory string (character name). 1 optional boolean, standard nil-gated idiom, default TRUE (a further instance of the asymmetric-true-default pattern).

**Return:** on success, exactly 2 boolean values (true, then false, both via lua_pushboolean); on any failure, exactly 1 value (false).

**A genuine, disassembly-confirmed compiled-behavior quirk worth flagging distinctly (in the spirit of §18.29's own naming/behavior-mismatch precedent):** the success path pushes `true` and then unconditionally falls through into the SAME shared tail code every failure path also reaches, which pushes a SECOND value, `false` — meaning a Lua caller doing `local a = character_is_jumping(name)` sees the expected `true`, but a caller doing `local a, b = character_is_jumping(name)` gets `a = true, b = false` on success, or `a = false, b = nil` on failure — never `true, true` or a single clean `true`. This is a real compiled quirk, not a documentation error.

### 20.29 `character_ignite` (0x00a41a20)

**Arguments:** 1 mandatory string (character name).

**Return:** none.

**Body:** resolves via the generic/`#PLAYER#` chain 0x00a281a0. On success, delegates to 0x0097cf80(character, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, **1**) — a source-character argument, a damage-source value, and four further flag arguments, ALL hardcoded (0/0/0/0/0/1), none tied to any Lua argument.

0x0097cf80 (fully decompiled, ~0x84d/2,125 bytes — summarized rather than exhaustively enumerated, matching this document's own house style for functions this size): heavily gated by immunity/state checks (bits at +0x1c98/+0x1c9c, an already-on-fire test, a liveness gate, wetness/underwater exclusion via 0x005de950). Single-gate (0x008addb0) authority split: not-authoritative → opens a network record, **opcode 0x41**, sub-header literal 0xc/12 (not 0x3b/59, which is item 21's own record) — appending the character's and (always-zero) source's network ids plus an encoded byte — committed via the genuine multi-target 0x0086f110. Authoritative branch: finds or allocates a slot in a FIXED 12-ENTRY "currently on fire" tracking array (base 0x0262b168 family — a genuinely new, previously-uncited fixed-size cap on simultaneous burning characters), attaches a fire visual/audio effect at the character's own "pelvis" bone (0x00487e80("pelvis")), sets the "on fire" bit (0x100 at +0xe8), applies AI-alert/ragdoll-adjacent side effects (0x009bc0d0/0x009c07a0), and — unless the character is already downed (state byte +0xccd == 4) — triggers the "catch fire" reaction (0x00986920) or, if a linked "hook" partner handle is present, notifies that handle instead (0x009e6510).

**Side effects/subsystem:** sets a resolved character on fire — a rich VFX/gameplay-state routine with a confirmed hard cap of 12 simultaneous tracked fires — or network-replicates the ignite request (opcode 0x41, sub-header 0xc/12) when not authoritative. **A cross-reference confirmed in item 32 below:** character_damage's own delegate (0x0096fa20) ALSO calls this exact same 0x0097cf80 routine as a side effect when a specific source-flag bit is set — i.e. incendiary damage sources trigger the identical ignite path this function exposes directly to Lua. **[CONFIRMED — disassembly for the top-level structure, the fixed-12-slot array, and the cross-reference to item 32; OPEN — most of the deep internal gating predicates' own individual real-world meanings, given the function's size.]**

### 20.30 `character_has_human_shield` (0x00a41450)

**Arguments:** 1 mandatory string (character name).

**Return:** 1 boolean, pushed via lua_pushboolean.

### 20.32 `character_damage` (0x00a41180)

**Arguments:** 1 mandatory string (target character name). 1 mandatory number (damage amount) — **extracted via a DISTINCT sub-idiom from every other numeric argument in this whole batch**: a plain lua_tonumber (0x00dfe160) cast directly to a single-precision float, WITHOUT the trailing round-to-integer helper (0x00ea2596) every other numeric argument in items 1-31 uses — appropriate since this is a genuinely continuous value, not a count/index. 1 optional boolean, standard nil-gated idiom, default TRUE. 1 optional string (attacker/source character name), standard nil-gated idiom, default absent.

**Return:** none.

**Body:** both names resolve via the generic/`#PLAYER#` chain 0x00a281a0 (source only if given). Builds an 11-bit flags word (bit 0x100 always set; bit 0x200 mirroring the boolean argument). If the target resolved, calls the central damage engine, 0x0096fa20(target, source, damageAmount, **0x0117f8b8**, **0x0117f8bc**, 0, &flagsWord) — reusing the SAME "shared global default position-pair" convention mission_end_failure/teleport/mission_end_success/camera_restrict_target_object (§1.5/§4.3/§6.12/§12.23) already establish, since this Lua entry point never exposes an actual hit-position argument.

0x0096fa20 (fully decompiled, ~0x144e/5,198 bytes — the largest single function this pass examined, summarized at the same level this document uses for its other largest functions rather than exhaustively enumerated): liveness-gated (0x00853b10) with an early invulnerability-descriptor-bit exit (+0x33 bit 0x2). A caller-omittable flags-word pointer defaults to a fixed global (0x0262524c) when null. Bit 0x800 of the flags overrides the damage amount to a fixed constant and calls 0x00bd3440 on the source (plausibly an "environmental/scripted damage type" override). Single-gate (0x008addb0) authority split: not-authoritative → opens a network record, **opcode 0x41**, forwarding both network ids, the damage amount (via a dedicated float encoder 0x0091dbc0), the same default position pair, and **11 individual bits unpacked one at a time from the flags word** (bits 0,1,2,3,4,5,8,9,0xb,0xc,0xd) as 11 separate boolean payload fields — committed via the genuine multi-target 0x0086f110.

The (very large) authoritative/local branch applies a long chain of multiplicative modifiers to the damage amount before applying it — difficulty/friendly-fire scaling (checking whether the source is a co-op partner via 0x00950550, and several fixed scale constants selected by target-type bytes at +0x501), a per-hit-point-bracket falloff curve using the SAME max/current-HP field pair (**+0x1cac/+0x1cb8**) §7.31's own get_max_hit_points/set_current_hit_points family already establishes, weapon/armor-type multipliers, and several early-exit "damage suppressed entirely" gates (god-mode-adjacent checks via 0x0096f4f0/0x00d9e4c0, a further descriptor-bit test at +0xec). It then applies the final amount by subtracting from +0x1cb8 (current HP), and — **a confirmed cross-reference to item 29 above** — when the source carries a specific incendiary-type flag bit (0x1c9c bit 0xe) AND the target isn't already flagged immune (+0x3b bit 0x1), it separately calls **the exact same ignite routine item 29 exposes to Lua**, 0x0097cf80(target, source, 0,0,0,0,0). Finally, if current HP has dropped to or below a fixed threshold constant (0x0125e270, plausibly 0.0): triggers a ragdoll/react call (0x009bc0d0(target,1,1,1) — the SAME call item 29's own ignite routine also uses) and a further call, 0x00963530(target) — **very plausibly the actual death-trigger for this specific damage path.**

**Flagged, not resolved:** §7.31's own set_current_hit_points/0x0094cfc0 entry already identifies a DIFFERENT address, 0x0096f8c0, as "very plausibly the death-trigger path" for that HP-setter's own family. This pass's 0x00963530 sighting is a genuinely different address reached via a genuinely different code path (the damage-application engine, not the direct HP setter) — either there are two distinct death-trigger entry points for two distinct callers, or one of them is a wrapper around the other; not independently reconciled this pass — **OPEN**, worth a future cross-check.

**Side effects/subsystem:** the game's central character-damage-application engine — applies a heavily-modified damage amount to a target's current hit points, can trigger the SAME ignite side-effect item 29 exposes directly, and triggers a death-adjacent call chain at zero HP; network-replicates (opcode 0x41, 11-bit flags payload) when not the local authority. **[CONFIRMED — disassembly for the top-level argument extraction (including the distinct no-rounding numeric sub-idiom), the record/opcode structure, the HP-field and ignite cross-references; OPEN — the 0x00963530-vs-0x0096f8c0 death-trigger reconciliation flagged above, and most of the ~30 individual damage-modifier gates' own precise real-world meanings, given the function's size.]**

### 21.1 `on_collision` (0x00a57a10) — hook-registration, `on_*` family

**Arguments:** 2 mandatory strings, both read unconditionally: arg 1 — callback name; arg 2 — target name/`"#PLAYER#"`.
