**`minimap_icon_add_radius_do` — real null-object-read crash.** 1 object name + optional radius/selector. **When the name is nil, unknown, despawned, or dead, the code zeroes the object pointer and then reads a handle out of it anyway (`object+8`) before using it — a direct access violation at address 8.** Its own sibling, the already-specced `minimap_icon_add_do`, correctly returns early on the exact same failure — the clearest same-tranche "one sibling checks, one doesn't" fix template this series has produced yet. **A second, independent crash shape in the same function:** the selector argument indexes a 4-entry function-pointer table with **no range check**; only values 1-3 are safe (0 and 4-7 call address 0, 8-9 call `0xffffffff`, per tranche 10's own table dump) — `minimap_icon_remove_radius_do`'s shared handler has the identical unchecked-selector shape against its own table, though its missing-object path does correctly return early.

**`open_vint_dialog_do`:** resolved in full; corrects tranche 10's reading of its own completion callback (§42.6 above) and adds a second real gap — the help-text table pointer it uses is never null-checked, unlike its sibling `mission_help_table_do`, which does check the same kind of table.

**`object_indicator_init_lua`:** a one-time-callback-plus-per-call-element-caching setup, the same two-phase shape tranche 13's `autil_hud_mayhem_init` already established for this family; three null-read shapes (no callback context, a missing document element, an exhausted callback pool), all shape-only with reachability HYPOTHESIS. **`message_remove`:** fully bounds- and generation-checked, no crash shape — a genuinely safe entry in a tranche full of unsafe siblings.

### 50.3 Pause map (4 functions, existing registrar `0x007dfae0`/§31) — a real uninitialized-stack-read crash, the first of its kind in this series

**`pause_map_drag_map` — real uninitialized-local crash, a new shape for this whole project.** No arguments. Reads the mouse-movement deltas into three local variables, but **that read only actually happens when a specific input-flags bit is set — when it's clear, the three locals are left completely uninitialized and the map pans by whatever garbage was already on the stack.** Whether that bit can be clear while the pause map is open on PC (e.g. with a gamepad as the active input device) is OPEN; a reimplementation should zero the deltas unconditionally before this call regardless.

**`pause_map_stag_takeover_do_reward`** (already specced at §31.6): re-confirmed, with one precision added — **the selected-zone pointer itself is unchecked, not only the field read off it** — calling this with no zone actually selected reads through address `0x44` directly. `pause_map_is_stag_mode`/`pause_map_is_tutorial_mode`: trivial, already-documented flag-byte getters that simply had no entry of their own until now.

### 50.4 PC options and the Killbane choice (2 functions)

**`options_display_pc_set_options`:** the full 12-argument PC graphics-settings applier (resolution, VSync, fullscreen, MSAA, anisotropic, lighting/shadow/scene detail, reflections, post-processing, ambient occlusion) — files a mode-change request and a revert snapshot only when something actually differs from the current mode, then applies each detail setting through its own dedicated setter. **Reflections, post-processing, and the low end of ambient occlusion are stored with no range check at all** (an out-of-range value like `0` just stores `-1`); anisotropic and shadow detail are safely bounded instead. A secondary, lower-confidence crash shape: a negative script-supplied width can dereference a possibly-null thread-local object while looking up the requested display mode for telemetry, and a non-negative width's mode lookup is divided by a denominator whose zero-case safety is OPEN.

**`msn_killbane_selected_option`:** delivers the player's choice from the Killbane UI straight to whichever script function registered itself via tranche 10's `on_m21_player_choice` (the same global hook slot) — closes the loop on that earlier entry's own open question of what consumes the registration.

### 50.5 Characters, crew, melee, and notoriety (7 functions)

**`notoriety_get` — real crash path, outcome depends on the CRT handler.** 1 track-name string. A non-string argument passes a null pointer straight into the C runtime's `__stricmp` with no check — in the stock release CRT this terminates the process outright (whether SR3 installs a handler that survives it is OPEN). Separately, and confirmed regardless of that: **an unknown or misspelled track name returns zero Lua values, not nil or zero** — a script that does arithmetic on the result crashes inside the *script*, not the native.

**`mesh_mover_reset_by_zone` — real null-read crash.** 1 zone-name string. The zone-name hash function reads the first character of the name with **no null check at all** — a nil or non-string argument reads address 0 directly. An unknown (but valid-string) zone name is handled correctly and does nothing.

**`party_dismiss_do`:** takes a Lua table of character names (not individual arguments); **passing anything other than a table — a single name string, for instance — raises a Lua error inside the binding itself** (HIGH CONFIDENCE, standard Lua 5.1 table-indexing behavior, not independently re-derived). Each resolved non-player character is removed from its squad via the same "remove from crew" primitive tranche 16 D.1 already named.

**`melee_get_move_id_from_name`:** returns **65535, not -1 or nil**, for an unrecognized move name — another "non-nil-non-negative sentinel" return shape for a binding layer to get right. `npc_is_in_brute_grab_qte`, `npc_dont_auto_equip_or_unequip_weapons`, `npc_brute_set_no_downed_finisher`: straightforward state queries/setters, no further crash shapes; `npc_dont_auto_equip_or_unequip_weapons`'s own boolean argument notably defaults to **false** on omission (an unconditional read), unlike most of this setter family's usual default-true idiom.

### 50.6 Mission state and world reset (2 functions)

**`mission_maybe_uncomplete_m22`:** un-completes mission 22 only when the player has progressed down exactly one of two mutually-exclusive follow-on missions (an XOR gate), and only does so **on the host** — but **broadcasts its network record from every machine regardless of host status**, the same "host-only effect, unconditional broadcast" pattern as tranche 16's stronghold-upgrade setter. ~~Combined with tranche 16 B.3, a second 'needs a host session' binding — more circumstantial weight for 'single player runs with a host session' (still HYPOTHESIS).~~ **CORRECTED (2026-10-03, same reconciliation as §49.1/§26.28): this is not supporting evidence for a single-player session — §8.27/§26.28 already CONFIRM by exhaustive negative check that single player never has one, so this binding, like the stronghold-upgrade setter, is simply CONFIRMED to be a no-op in single player via this path. Worth flagging to Team B as a real behavior to reproduce (or not), not as a clue about session state.**

**`mesh_mover_reset_by_zone`** is covered above (§50.5) for its crash shape; structurally it resets every free-standing, currently-attached mesh mover in a named *loaded* zone back to its saved transform, with no host gate at all (each machine resets its own copy).

### 50.7 Cross-function observations

This tranche produced the clearest same-function-family sibling-asymmetry examples in the whole series: `minimap_icon_add_do` vs. `minimap_icon_add_radius_do` (one checks, one doesn't, identical failure case), and `mission_help_table_do` vs. `open_vint_dialog_do` (same pattern, a help-text-table pointer). It also introduces two new defect shapes for this project: a "state flag set even though the object it describes failed to be created" ordering bug (`main_menu_restart_video`, §50.1 — worth grepping other `create → store → set-active` sequences for the same mistake), and the series' first genuinely uninitialized-stack-local crash (`pause_map_drag_map`, §50.3, as opposed to the recurring "null pointer plus offset" and "unchecked array index" shapes). Return-value surprises continue to recur as their own hazard class: `notoriety_get` (no value), `melee_get_move_id_from_name` (65535), and `open_vint_dialog_check_done` (§42.6 correction, only ever -2 or -1) all give a binding layer a way to get a "no crash, just silently wrong" integration bug instead of a safe default.

**Crash-shaped findings, summary (all CONFIRMED code paths from the disassembly; reachability marked where not separately settled):** `minimap_icon_add_radius_do` (null-object handle read at address 8, plus an unchecked selector table index shared with `minimap_icon_remove_radius_do`); `main_menu_restart_video` (null video object, crash deferred to the next call); `pause_map_stag_takeover_do_reward` (null selected-zone read at address `0x44`); `pause_map_drag_map` (uninitialized stack locals used as mouse deltas); `mesh_mover_reset_by_zone` (null-name read in the zone-hash function); `notoriety_get` (null name reaching the CRT `__stricmp`, handler-dependent outcome); `open_vint_dialog_do` (unchecked help-text table pointer).

**Review status (2026-10-03):** all 25 names in tranche 18 resolved and written up (§50.1-§50.6); none failed. CONFIRMED unless individually marked HYPOTHESIS/OPEN above. Residual OPEN items: which dialog-close paths pass `-1` to `open_vint_dialog_do`'s completion callback (decides whether its stuck-poll hazard can trigger from a normal choice, not just a missing dialog); whether `options_display_pc_set_options`'s TLS dereference and mode-lookup division are reachable with real display-mode data; the writer of the pause-map input-flags bit (§50.3); whether any shipped script passes a player object to `party_dismiss_do`.

## 51. Ranking tranche 17 — 25 previously-unspecced Lua-bound names (2026-10-03)

**Source.** Job `D:\Project Crreish\TEAM A\ghidra\jobs\ranking\tranche-17.json` (names 351-375 of 554, Team B call-count order; full write-up in `review/exe-notes-2026-10-01/interp_ranking_tranche_17.md`). 12 names in the gameplay registrar `0x00a20840`; 13 under the UI bring-up `0x008430f0` across five table-driven sub-registrars (Saintsbook, save-system, playlist, and two pause-menu tables) — **no function-pointer-before-name registrar this time**, the first tranche in a while without that quirk. A single shared no-op stub (`0x007c9f50`, already documented elsewhere in this spec) backs 32 registered rows across 10 different registrars project-wide, including two of this tranche's own names. Addresses below are CONFIRMED — disassembly unless marked otherwise.

### 51.1 The clearest same-function sibling-asymmetry crash yet: `qte_start_m02_skyqte_01`

**Real null-dereference crash, single-player-only path.** 1 character + 1 callback name + 2 optional names (partner, point). The underlying worker function **checks its optional partner argument on the remote (network-forwarded) branch but not on the local branch** — the exact same "one branch checks, one doesn't" shape this series keeps finding, but this time inside the *same* function rather than between two siblings. A nil, misspelled, despawned, or dead partner argument crashes only when the calling character is locally owned (i.e., only in single player or for the local player in co-op) — the remote/forwarded path is safe. The one shipped call site evidently always passes a live partner, so this is a real latent crash for any new script that omits it.

### 51.2 Saintsbook, save system, and playlist (9 functions)

**`sb_select_hitman_target`/`sb_select_chop_shop_vehicle`:** both fully bounds-checked selectors on their respective diversion-contract managers; **selecting a contract in either manager clears the other's active contract first** — only one Saintsbook diversion can be active at a time. A real, confirmed asymmetry: re-selecting the current chop-shop vehicle **deselects** it, but re-selecting the current hitman target is simply a no-op. `sb_saintsbook_is_available`'s third eligibility term reads a global that nothing in the binary ever writes — permanently dead, confirmed by an exhaustive reference check (the same "write-only or read-only global kills half a condition" pattern this series keeps finding).

**`save_system_delete_game`** — real silent-drop logic defect. 1 save-slot index (bounds-checked, no crash shape). **A delete request made while another storage job is still running, or with no Steam user interface available, is silently dropped — but the save-list UI refresh callback still fires regardless**, so the script sees the entry still present with no error at all to explain why. Separately, the slot's bookkeeping (used-count decrement, flag clears) happens **before** the asynchronous delete job is known to have actually succeeded; whether a failed job gets this repaired is OPEN. `save_system_set_operation` writes to a global nothing reads — another confirmed-dead write.

**`playlist_play_track`** — real null-read crash, plus an index-aliasing shape. 1 track index. **An out-of-range index, a negative index, or any index at all while no songs are loaded makes the song-lookup return null, and the caller reads through that null with no check.** Separately, the index comparison only examines the low 16 bits, so an index of 65536+k silently plays track k instead of failing or wrapping sensibly.

### 51.3 Radio (4 functions) — a real cross-machine set/clear divergence

**`radio_set_sing_along_track`** — real network-divergence logic defect. 2 song-name strings. **The second argument is never actually read by the local-apply logic at all — it exists purely to be sent over the network** — and if that second name fails to resolve, it's sent as the wire sentinel for "no song," which the receiving machines interpret as a **clear** instruction. The result: **every remote machine silently clears the sing-along state that the local machine just set**, with no error anywhere. `radio_clear_sing_along_track` compounds this: **song index 0 can be set by the setter above but can never be cleared from script** (the clear function explicitly rejects index 0), and the clear also leaves a separate "current sing-along index" global stale rather than resetting it. `radio_unblock`/`radio_newsbreak_clear`: straightforward local-only state changes, no further crash shapes.

### 51.4 Players and characters (7 functions)

**`player_get_custom_voice`** — real null-dereference crash. 1 player name. The resolver's result is never checked before being dereferenced — a nil, misspelled, non-player-class, or dead/despawned name reads straight through null.

**`perform_killswitch`** — real null-virtual-call crash, narrow trigger. 1 victim name + 1 killer name. The victim argument is used **only** for a type check (confirming it's Killbane-type) — the actual QTE always targets whatever live object is currently registered under the literal script name `"M21_Killbane"`, not the passed-in victim object itself. **If no live object carries exactly that name when this is called (a second Killbane-type spawn, a renamed instance, or the real one having been removed), the code zeroes the lookup result and immediately makes a virtual call through it** — narrow in practice (the one shipped call site presumably always targets the real Killbane), but a real crash shape for any script that calls this under different naming conditions.

**`player_take_human_shield_do`:** a range-gated grab with two branches that **return success optimistically before anything has actually happened** — whenever the taker or the victim belongs to a remote machine, the function returns `true` immediately upon forwarding the request, with the real outcome decided elsewhere, later, off this call's return value entirely. Its "force" argument **defaults to true**, meaning an out-of-range victim is grabbed anyway unless a script explicitly opts out.

**`players_naked`, `player_names_get_all`, `player_action_is_pressed`:** resolved in full, no further crash shapes (a strip-and-resync routine covering both local and remote co-op players; a dense 1-based name table; a bounds-safe 166-row action-name lookup with two harmless aliased ids and one genuinely unused id).

### 51.5 Pause menu and satellite weapon (5 functions)

**`pause_menu_horde_mode_new`:** resets horde-mode state and **broadcasts an opcode-`0x44` record to the session with no host gate at all** — any machine, host or client, sends it; consequence on a client receiving its own echo is OPEN. `pause_menu_horde_mode_retry`: the same underlying mission-end routine, but preserves three state dwords across the reset that `_new` discards. `pause_menu_is_using_southpaw_control_scheme`/`…_vehicle_…`: simple bounds-safe input-binding-table queries, no crash shape.

**`satellite_weapon_mode_set`:** enable/disable on a per-machine controller singleton for a selectable player mask (local, remote co-op, or both); a remote player's request is simply forwarded to that player's own owning machine. No crash shape found; whether re-enabling an already-active controller is separately guarded is OPEN.

### 51.6 Cross-function observations

This tranche's defining pattern is the "one branch of the same function checks, the other doesn't" shape (§51.1's `qte_start_m02_skyqte_01`) rather than the more common "one sibling function checks, the other doesn't" shape earlier tranches found repeatedly — both are the same underlying lesson (an unchecked optional argument reachable down exactly one code path) but this is the first time it's been the *same* function's own two branches rather than two different functions. Write-only/read-only dead globals continue to recur as their own hazard class (§51.2, twice in one tranche) — cheap to grep for project-wide given how often this series keeps finding them. Two diversion-manager selectors (`sb_select_hitman_target`/`sb_select_chop_shop_vehicle`) clearing each other, and two QTE-starting natives (this tranche's `qte_start_m02_skyqte_01` and §50.4's `perform_killswitch`-adjacent Killbane QTE) sharing hook slot `0x18` on their starter's hook table, both continue patterns already established elsewhere in this spec.

**Crash-shaped findings, summary (all CONFIRMED code paths from the disassembly; reachability marked where not separately settled):** `qte_start_m02_skyqte_01` (null partner read on the locally-owned path only — the clearest same-function sibling-asymmetry case in the series); `player_get_custom_voice` (unchecked resolver result, null dereference); `playlist_play_track` (unchecked null song-lookup result, plus a 16-bit index-aliasing shape); `perform_killswitch` (null virtual call when no live object is named exactly `"M21_Killbane"`, narrow trigger).

**Review status (2026-10-03):** all 25 names in tranche 17 resolved and written up (§51.1-§51.5); none failed. CONFIRMED unless individually marked HYPOTHESIS/OPEN above. Residual OPEN items: what the two diversion managers' cross-clearing helper functions do to each other's active-contract state beyond "clear it"; whether a client receiving `pause_menu_horde_mode_new`'s unguarded broadcast misbehaves; who creates the radio-preview emitter object `playlist_play_track` relies on; the exact meaning of the southpaw control-scheme binding slots.

## 52. Ranking tranche 15 — 25 previously-unspecced Lua-bound names (2026-10-03)

**Source.** Job `D:\Project Crreish\TEAM A\ghidra\jobs\ranking\tranche-15.json` (names 301-325 of 554, Team B call-count order; full write-up in `review/exe-notes-2026-10-01/interp_ranking_tranche_15.md`). 14 names in the gameplay registrar `0x00a20840`; 9 in the **new** 20-row vehicle-customization UI registrar `0x00820aa0` (the `vcust_*` family, continuing the family tranche 06 started); 2 in the already-specced store-vehicle registrar `0x008152a0`. No function-pointer-before-name registrar this tranche. Addresses below are CONFIRMED — disassembly unless marked otherwise.

### 52.1 Vehicle customization (`vcust_*`, 9 functions) — a whole family that mostly skips its own precondition check

**The single biggest structural finding this tranche: only 2 of the 9 `vcust_*` names in this tranche actually check that a live "customization vehicle" exists before using it — the other 7 dereference the null result of a failed resolve outright.** A binding layer should simply treat every name in this family as "requires a live customization vehicle" and refuse up front, since the retail code mostly doesn't.

**`vcust_change_top_level_menu`** — **real null-pointer-chain crash, a new "poisons its own next call" shape.** 1 relative-or-absolute-mode number + 1 optional step count. **An out-of-range absolute selection stores null into the "current top-level node" global unconditionally — and the very next relative (±1) call dereferences that same global with no check at all.** So two calls in sequence, the first harmless on its own, crash the second. The global is also null before the customization screen is even set up, so any premature ±1 call hits the same crash from a different cause.

**`vcust_select_paint_slot`, `vcust_adjust_camera_angle`, `vcust_preview_rim_sizing`, `vcust_purchase_component`, `vcust_purchase_paint`, `vcust_show_nos_hydraulic_warning`** — all **real null-dereference crashes** when the customization vehicle fails to resolve (confirmed per-function, each at its own specific offset into the vehicle/customization-record chain). `vcust_adjust_camera_angle` additionally reads the current menu node global with no null check of its own, a second independent crash in the same function. Several of these also take **completely unchecked numeric indices** into fixed-size tables (`vcust_select_paint_slot`'s slot index, `vcust_preview_rim_sizing`'s combined size+style index, `vcust_set_underglow`'s palette-colour index) — out-of-range values read unrelated memory and hand it to downstream code as if it were a valid record.

**The purchase sub-family is internally inconsistent in four different ways** (full comparison table in the interp note): `vcust_set_underglow` applies its colour change **before** charging, trusts a script-supplied price with no floor, and has no purchase callback or telemetry at all, unlike its three siblings; `vcust_purchase_paint` has **no price validation whatsoever — a negative price credits the player's cash, and a price of exactly zero still fires the stat/callback/telemetry side effects** as if a real purchase happened; `vcust_purchase_component` is the only one of the four with a real memory-safety bug (below); `vcust_purchase_performance_upgrade` is the **only** member of the family that validates its result before charging anything. None of the four checks whether the player can actually afford the purchase, and none null-checks the local player before charging.

**`vcust_purchase_component` — real out-of-bounds read-and-write, most severe finding in this tranche.** No arguments; operates on a globally-tracked "currently selected item" index. **That index is file-initialized to -1 and is reset back to -1 on every exit from this function** — so calling it twice in a row, or calling it at all before a fresh selection, computes an "item" pointer 60 bytes before the real item array. If the garbage bytes there happen to decode as an unowned item with a positive price, **the function charges that garbage price to the player and then writes a bit into the dword immediately preceding the array** — a real heap-corruption shape, not just a crash, since what sits there in practice (heap metadata, an adjacent allocation) is unexamined and genuinely OPEN.

### 52.2 Vehicles (10 functions, gameplay registrar)

**`vehicle_detonate_random_parked_car` — not random, and a misspelled argument silently widens its blast radius to the entire world.** Optional reference-object name + angle/distance window. **There is no random-number generator call anywhere in this function — it deterministically detonates the first qualifying parked vehicle in world-list order**, and critically, **a reference-object name that fails to resolve takes exactly the same code path as passing no reference at all**, meaning a typo doesn't fail safely — it just blows up the first parked car anywhere in the game world instead of one near the intended location. Separately, calling it with only a reference name and the default (all-zero) angle/distance window effectively detonates nothing, since the default window only admits a vehicle at exactly zero distance and zero angle.

**`vehicle_component_is_shattered`/`vehicle_component_shatter_glass`** — **real crash path, handler-dependent.** 1 vehicle + 1 component name. A nil or non-string component name passes a null pointer straight into the C runtime's `_stricmp` once per named component on the vehicle — fatal under the stock invalid-parameter handler (whether SR3 installs its own survivable handler is OPEN, the same open question this exact hazard keeps raising across several tranches now). **`vehicle_component_shatter_glass` is not glass-specific at all — it applies the "shattered" bit and effect to any named component on the vehicle**, regardless of what that component actually is.

**`vehicle_flee`:** resolved in full — drives AI mode 2 (flee) on the vehicle's AI controller with several real vetoes (a player-driven vehicle never flees; an AI mode/distance veto). One of the three vetoes is **confirmed permanently dead by an exhaustive reference check** — the global it tests has exactly one reference in the whole binary (this read), so that veto branch can never actually fire, the same "write-only or read-only dead global" pattern recurring across this whole series.

**`vehicle_get_max_speed`** returns **miles per hour**, not the stored metres-per-second value directly (a confirmed unit-conversion fact worth getting right in any reimplementation), and **-1** for an unresolved vehicle rather than nil or 0. `vehicle_in_air`, `vehicle_is_flipped`, `vehicle_allow_ownership_transfer`, `vehicle_evacuate`: resolved in full, no further crash shapes beyond `vehicle_evacuate` discarding its own occupant-liveness check result (dead occupants are evacuated/destroyed exactly like live ones — consequence HYPOTHESIS: benign). `vault_heli_hack_for_m01`: a narrow, mission-1-specific component-index cache setter.

### 52.3 Characters, triggers, and tutorials (4 functions)

**`turn_to_check_done`** — a real "name doesn't mean what it says" shape: it returns true for an unresolved character, for a character that never started turning, **and** for a character whose turn just finished — **and the act of querying a finished turn consumes the completion record**, so a second consecutive call reports "done" again through the "no record exists" path rather than because anything is actually still true. `tutorial_lock` — **a real silent-no-op for roughly 10% of all tutorials**: it only accepts tutorial indices up to 188, but the project's own 210-entry tutorial table (already documented elsewhere in this spec) has entries up to 209 — the 21 entries from 189-209 can never be locked through this native at all. `trigger_allow_dead_guys`, `tutorial_stop_current`: resolved in full; the latter correctly handles all list-unlinking cases and replicates to the session host only under specific descriptor conditions, with a confirmed client-side gap (a co-op client stops its own prompt locally but tells the host nothing, so the host's copy of that prompt keeps running).

### 52.4 Cross-function observations

The "select-or-null" idiom — a flag comparison compiled into a conditional move that produces a **null base pointer** instead of a branch when a precondition fails — recurs across at least nine different functions in this tranche's call graph (vehicle component-set validity, customization-record validity), and is the direct mechanical cause of most of §52.1's crash shapes: the fix template is uniformly "test the flag and return early," not "fix the null-pointer-arithmetic downstream." This is a materially different (and more subtle) root cause than the plain "unchecked resolver result" pattern this series has catalogued dozens of times before — same symptom, different cause, worth distinguishing in any automated hazard-scanning tool built from this spec.

**Crash-shaped findings, summary (all CONFIRMED code paths from the disassembly; reachability marked where not separately settled):** `vcust_purchase_component` (out-of-bounds read **and** write from a stale -1 selection index — the most severe finding this tranche); `vcust_change_top_level_menu` (null-pointer chain that poisons its own next call); `vcust_select_paint_slot`/`vcust_adjust_camera_angle`/`vcust_preview_rim_sizing`/`vcust_purchase_paint`/`vcust_show_nos_hydraulic_warning` (null customization-vehicle dereferences); `vehicle_component_is_shattered`/`vehicle_component_shatter_glass` (null name reaching the CRT `_stricmp`); `vehicle_detonate_random_parked_car` (not random, and a failed reference-name resolve silently widens the blast target to the whole world).

**Review status (2026-10-03):** all 25 names in tranche 15 resolved and written up (§52.1-§52.3); none failed. CONFIRMED unless individually marked HYPOTHESIS/OPEN above. Residual OPEN items: the exact contents of the 60 bytes read before `vcust_purchase_component`'s item array (decides whether the out-of-bounds charge/write is observable in practice with real heap layout); which writer sets vehicle `+0x1d84` (max speed); whether SR3 installs a survivable CRT invalid-parameter handler (shared with several prior tranches' identical open question); the meaning of `vehicle_flee`'s special path and of several vcust record-byte flags.

## 53. Ranking tranche 20 — 25 previously-unspecced Lua-bound names (2026-10-03)

**Source.** Job `D:\Project Crreish\TEAM A\ghidra\jobs\ranking\tranche-20.json` (names 426-450 of 554, Team B call-count order; full write-up in `review/exe-notes-2026-10-01/interp_ranking_tranche_20.md`). 14 names in the gameplay registrar `0x00a20840`; 11 under four UI registrars — the already-specced garage table `0x005fc500`, the 113-row UI helper table `0x00845aa0`, the already-specced pause-map table `0x007dfae0`, and a **new** 8-row gang-customization registrar `0x0083a900`. No function-pointer-before-name registrar this tranche. Also resolved tranche 16 §49's own OPEN item (`0x005f87c0` is `garage_can_customize`) and corrected §27.9's description of the garage entry-pointer array (above). Addresses below are CONFIRMED — disassembly unless marked otherwise.

### 53.1 Gang customization (1 function, new registrar `0x0083a900`) — the most severe memory-safety finding in the series so far

**`gang_customization_select_vehicle` — real arbitrary-address write, script-controlled.** 2 numbers: a visible-catalogue position and a **gang-vehicle slot**. **The slot argument indexes a 3-slot global array with absolutely no bound check, and the write path is reachable directly from Lua** — slot 3 overwrites the very catalogue-category pointer the same function is still reading from on that call; slot 4 hits another live pointer the slot-loader depends on; any other value writes an arbitrary item pointer to `array_base + 4×slot`, anywhere in the address space, with a negative slot writing before the array entirely. **Three sibling functions in the same registrar index the identical unbounded array** — `gang_customization_revert_vehicle` also **writes** through it unchecked, while `…_confirm_vehicle` and `…_show_vehicle` read through it unchecked (an out-of-range read there feeds whatever garbage it finds into the vehicle-spawn path as if it were a real item pointer). **A binding layer must reject any slot outside 0-2 for every `gang_customization_*_vehicle` name** — this is the single clearest "accept exactly this tiny range, nothing else" fix this whole series has produced.

A second, independent real bug in the same function's preview-release path: when the previously-previewed vehicle handle is stale (no longer resolves to a live object), the code correctly zeroes its working pointer but **then keeps using that null pointer anyway** — it still calls the object-hide and object-destroy primitives with it, and specifically **writes a flag bit through `null + 0x16c0`**. The all-zero-handle case (nothing was ever previewed) correctly skips this; only the "used to resolve, now doesn't" case hits the null write.

### 53.2 Helicopter (6 functions, gameplay registrar) — "true" that doesn't mean "it happened"

**`helicopter_land` and `helicopter_enter_dropoff`** both return their success boolean **after only the cheap preconditions pass** — the actual landing or drop-off request can still be silently dropped (the target is farther than 200 units away for `helicopter_land`; fewer than 2 live occupants for `helicopter_enter_dropoff` unless explicitly overridden) or merely forwarded to a remote owning machine with the real outcome decided later, off this call's return value. The same "optimistic true" shape this series has now found in several different native families. `helicopter_enter_dropoff`'s `"#PLAYER#"` sentinel for its drop-off-target argument resolves to **whichever player is closest to the drop-off point, not necessarily the local player** — a real behavioral trap on co-op where it can silently mean the remote player.

The four boolean flag setters (`helicopter_set_large_dspiral`, `helicopter_set_dont_move_in_combat`, `helicopter_set_dont_explode_in_air`) and the bank-angle clearer (`helicopter_clear_max_bank_angle`) accept **any resolved vehicle, not just a helicopter** — none of them actually checks the vehicle's AI mode before writing its flag bit, unlike `helicopter_land`/`helicopter_enter_dropoff`, which do check. `helicopter_clear_max_bank_angle` only clears the "override enabled" bit and **leaves the previously-set bank angle value in storage untouched** — a later re-enable without supplying a fresh angle silently reuses the old one.

### 53.3 Guardian angel and script groups (5 functions)

**`guardian_angel_start_zone_pinning`** — a real logic trap: an unknown or misspelled zone-set name **releases whatever is currently pinned and then pins nothing new** (the release runs unconditionally before the name lookup) — a typo doesn't fail safely, it silently un-pins. Separately, a zone set with more than 8 zones pins nothing at all, yet the function still records that set as "the current pin" internally — a state/reality mismatch. The release mechanism also has a scope mismatch worth flagging: it wholesale-empties two entire zone-priority classes (not just this call's own contribution to them), while two other classes the pin path can also fill are never touched by the release at all.

**`group_create_do`/`group_create_hidden_do`** are confirmed to be the same underlying creation routine differing only in one passed literal, and **creation happens exactly once** — calling `group_create_hidden_do` on a group `group_create_do` already created does nothing at all, so a script relying on that sequence to retroactively hide an already-visible group is simply wrong. `guardian_angel_release_attack_groups`/`guardian_angel_clear_zone_pinning`: resolved in full, no further crash shapes beyond the same unchecked base-object dereference pattern `guardian_angel_start_zone_pinning` shares with its siblings (shape-only, reachability OPEN).

### 53.4 Garage (7 functions, existing registrar `0x005fc500`) — an off-by-one and a double-release, on the same 168-slot array `garage_preview_vehicle`'s own correction (§27.9) already flagged as unbounded

**`garage_clear_new` — real off-by-one bound, confirmed structurally.** 1 list index. **The bound check accepts `index == count`, not just indices strictly below it** — that one-past-the-end slot can be a null pointer (zero-fill array), a stale pointer to an already-recycled record, or, once the array reaches its 168-entry capacity, the count field itself being read and written through as if it were an entry pointer. Its own sibling `garage_back_to_customize` bounds the identical array correctly (`< count`) — the direct fix template, the same "one sibling checks, one doesn't" shape this series keeps finding, now inside the garage family specifically.

**`garage_remove_vehicle` — real double-release logic defect.** No arguments. Correctly unlinks and recycles the currently-selected garage entry back to its object pool on a normal call — but **never clears the "selected entry" global or removes the stale pointer from the 168-slot array afterward.** A second call before a fresh selection is made finds the same now-stale pointer, decrements the live-entry count a second time (which can go negative), and **hands the same record back to its free pool a second time — even if that pool has since reissued it to something else entirely**, a real use-after-free/double-free shape on an object pool, not just a flat crash.

**`garage_can_customize`** resolves tranche 16's own open question (§49): it is confirmed to be `0x005f87c0`, gated on exactly the same 12-mission denylist tranche 16's sibling store-access check already uses, plus a garage-type and entry-flag check of its own. `garage_vehicle_load_pending`, `garage_get_garage_type`, `garage_can_delete`, `garage_back_to_customize`: resolved in full, no further crash shapes.

### 53.5 World/object queries and UI string helpers (5 functions)

**`get_char_in_string` — real null-read crash.** 1 string + 1 0-based index. The length computation is an inline `strlen`-equivalent loop over the first argument with **no null check at all** — a nil or non-string argument with a non-negative index reads straight through address 0 (a negative index happens to return early before the unchecked loop runs, by coincidence of the check ordering, not by design).

**`get_localized_string_for_tag`** returns the engine's own internal encoded wide-text byte form (a leading tag byte, then 3 bytes per character, decoded by the UI's own text setters) — **not plain UTF-8 or ASCII text** — a reimplementation that changes this representation must update every consumer that decodes it, not just this one function. `get_closest_object` returns the **empty string, never nil,** when nothing qualifies (no reference resolves, the candidate table is empty or not actually a table, or nothing in it resolves) — a return-shape trap consistent with this series' recurring "no value/empty value instead of nil" hazard class. `get_world_income_dollars`, `get_stag_active`: resolved in full, no crash shape.

### 53.6 Cross-function observations

This tranche is explicit, by its own design, about **not** repeating the single-player-host-session inference mistake two prior tranches made and had to be corrected for: several functions here gate on the same session/host double-gate or single-gate shapes, and the note draws no conclusion about single-player session existence from any of them, citing §8.27/§26.28 directly. Two new flag-byte families are documented for helicopters (a double-gate, string-tagged pair on vehicle `+0x1d7e`, and a single-gate opcode-`0x42` family on the flight record at `+0x101`/`+0x102`), extending the already-large catalogue of such families elsewhere in this spec. The garage entry-pointer array (corrected at §27.9) and the gang-customization 3-slot array (§53.1) are this tranche's two clearest "small fixed-size array, indexed straight from an unchecked script argument" cases — exactly the shape a targeted hardening pass should grep for first.

**Crash-shaped findings, summary (all CONFIRMED code paths from the disassembly; reachability marked where not separately settled):** `gang_customization_select_vehicle`/`_revert_vehicle` (unchecked slot index into a 3-slot array → arbitrary-address write, the most severe finding in the series so far); `gang_customization_select_vehicle`'s preview-release path (null-pointer write through `null+0x16c0` after a stale-handle lookup failure); `garage_clear_new` (off-by-one array bound, reads/writes one slot past the end); `garage_remove_vehicle` (double-release of a recycled object-pool record on a repeated call); `get_char_in_string` (unchecked null argument reaching an inline `strlen`); `garage_preview_vehicle` (completely unbounded index into the garage entry-pointer array, corrected at §27.9).

**Review status (2026-10-03):** all 25 names in tranche 20 resolved and written up (§53.1-§53.5); none failed. CONFIRMED unless individually marked HYPOTHESIS/OPEN above. Residual OPEN items: what reads the helicopter "large dspiral" and "don't move in combat" flag bits; whether the gang-customization catalogue's fixed 256-entry per-item tables can ever actually be exceeded by real shipped data; what clears the two zone-pinning priority classes the guardian-angel release path never touches; the exact meaning of several garage entry flag bits.

## 54. Ranking tranche 19 — 25 previously-unspecced Lua-bound names (2026-10-03)

**Source.** Job `D:\Project Crreish\TEAM A\ghidra\jobs\ranking\tranche-19.json` (names 401-425 of 554, Team B call-count order; full write-up in `review/exe-notes-2026-10-01/interp_ranking_tranche_19.md`). 17 names in the gameplay registrar `0x00a20840`; 8 in the already-specced 18-row main-menu table `0x007c9fc0`. No function-pointer-before-name registrar among the 25, though one does appear for a non-tranche neighbor (`game_proto_select`, §54.4). Addresses below are CONFIRMED — disassembly unless marked otherwise. This note's own agent was explicitly briefed on, and correctly avoided, the single-player-host-session inference mistake two earlier tranches made — every session/host-gated function below is described as simply taking its no-session path in single player, per §8.27/§26.28, with no inference drawn.

### 54.1 Main menu (8 functions, already-specced registrar) — 6 of 18 rows are inert on PC

**Three names are the shared no-op stub; two more, plus three further names elsewhere in the binary, are hardcoded to always return `true`** (`main_menu_check_online_privilege`/`game_user_has_online_privilege` and `main_menu_check_chat_priv`/`game_user_has_voice_privilege`/`vcust_using_lightset` — five Lua names, two handlers, both constant). **This pass also settles why: the shared `0x008703f0` helper both of them funnel through is not a platform privilege check at all — it is a plain "1 ≤ argument ≤ 8" range test with no platform call and no state.** This directly corrects tranche 16 §49.4's `screen_capture_preview_should_upload` entry (fixed above): that function's own "privilege denied" cancel path is dead code on PC, since the range test can never actually fail for the constant argument it's called with. `main_menu_check_open_nat` adds a sixth inert row — its own gating call is a linker-folded "return 0" body, so it never does anything either, regardless of what its name promises.

**`main_menu_matchmaking` — real null-dialog-pool crash shape.** An optional boolean. Runs save/storage preconditions, then starts matchmaking into the fixed `"sr3_city"` map with the boolean. **Each precondition-failure warning dialog is popped from the shared 4-slot dialog pool and used immediately with no null check** — if all four pool slots are already in use when this runs, the result is a write near address 0 (narrow trigger: four other dialogs already open exactly when the main menu starts matchmaking). Three localized strings this function computes are confirmed dead — they're built and stored but never actually displayed by anything.

**`main_menu_continue`:** resolved in full — raises a continue/save-enumeration request handled by the main-menu's own per-frame update, with an input-lock Lua hook bracketing the work. No crash shape; the "no usable save" and success paths are both handled.

### 54.2 Line of sight and lights (4 functions)

**`los_check_do` — real stuck-poll hazard.** 2 object names. A cached, request-pooled line-of-sight query between two objects: returns -1 ("ask again"), then 1 or 0 once resolved. **The -1 "pending" result is returned even when the underlying request pool is exhausted or either object fails the request creator's own kind check — meaning a script polling "until not -1" can loop forever**, the same stuck-poll shape this series has now found in several different query families. Separately, an unresolvable object name returns 0 — identical to "no line of sight" — so a script cannot distinguish a typo from a real negative answer.

**`light_group_attach_to_camera`/`light_group_detach_from_camera`:** a reference-counted 16-slot table (attach increments, detach decrements, removal only at zero) with two confirmed real gaps: a 17th attach is **silently dropped** with no error, and a light group that gets despawned while still attached **can never be detached** through this binding (its slot sits occupied until the whole table is reset elsewhere) — the attach/detach pair isn't a reliable toggle once a group can disappear out from under it. `level_light_enable_all_do`: resolved in full (three lighting modes on a world-object list's light channel), no further crash shape beyond the usual unchecked world-manager pointer pattern.

### 54.3 World queries, inventory, and downed characters (8 functions)

**`is_syn_tower_destroyed` — real wrong-arity return.** No arguments. It's confirmed to be nothing more than the already-documented `city_zone_swap_is_active` with a hardcoded zone name — but **its own wrapper pushes an extra `false` on the "destroyed" path that the underlying function never pushes**, so it returns 2 values when true and 1 when false, unlike every other caller of that same primitive.

**`hud_x_of_y_update` — real script-controlled out-of-bounds write, worse than an already-documented sibling.** 2 numbers (slot index, new count). **This function applies zero bound or sign checking to its slot index at all** — its own sibling `hud_x_of_y_add` correctly rejects indices outside 0-3, but this one writes two dwords and a byte at a computed address for *any* 32-bit index, landing inside an adjacent vtable-bearing HUD object table for small out-of-range values or at a flatly unmapped address for a large or negative one. This is confirmed strictly worse than the already-specced `hud_x_of_y_remove`'s own unbounded-index issue (§41.4), since that one only reads.

**`human_being_revived_by`** — a **real session-dependent return-value difference**, the first in this series where the *return value itself* (not just a side effect) changes between single player and co-op: it returns the reviving player's real script name on a co-op host, a `"#NETID#<id>"` placeholder string on a co-op client, and **the literal `"#NETID#0"` in single player** (since single player has no session at all, per §8.27/§26.28 — this is simply that no-session path, not a new finding about sessions). It also returns nil indistinguishably for "never revived" and "revived by a non-player NPC." `human_downed_set_mars_kb_interactable` has **no repeat-call guard**: calling it twice on the same still-downed character creates a second on-screen indicator and overwrites the stored id of the first one, leaking it. `inv_item_dual_wield` sets its flag **locally only** with no way to clear it through the binding, and on a non-owning machine only the re-equip step (not the flag itself) is forwarded to the owner — a real potential visual desync in co-op. `inv_item_get_weapon_slot`, `inv_item_get_anim_group`, `human_being_revived`, `is_a_vehicle`: resolved in full, each with its own confirmed "unknown input" sentinel value that a binding layer must preserve exactly (255, `"Default"`, a flag bit, false respectively).

### 54.4 HUD and homie missions (4 functions, plus a crash-shaped non-tranche neighbor)

**`hud_pop_screen`:** only actually pops the named screen when it's on top of the HUD stack, but **broadcasts the "pop" notification to the session regardless of whether the local pop happened** — a peer can be told a screen was popped that this machine actually kept open. `hud_get_proto_selection`, `homie_mission_unlock`: resolved in full (a sticky poll result; an activity-record override that, paired with its `lock` sibling, has no way to restore the record's original default state through either binding).

**A real crash-shaped defect found one hop outside this tranche while tracing `hud_get_proto_selection`'s only writer: `game_proto_select` (`0x00840fa0`).** Two numbers. **An argument of 0, nil, or any non-number value computes a negative index and writes a byte into the caller's own saved register spill area on the stack** — specifically the saved EBX for the nil/zero case, and any of the four saved general-purpose registers for arguments down to -15. Those are registers the Lua VM's own C-call dispatcher depends on immediately after this function returns. The write itself is CONFIRMED; whether it manifests as an outright crash or a more subtly corrupted VM state is HYPOTHESIS, but either way this is a real stack-corruption shape reachable directly from a script-supplied number, flagged for the backlog even though the name itself isn't one of this tranche's 25.

### 54.5 Cross-function observations

This tranche adds a second confirmed member to the "dead no-op disguised as a real check" family §49/§54.1 both document (`main_menu_check_open_nat`'s folded-zero gate, alongside `0x008703f0`'s always-true range test) — worth a dedicated project-wide sweep for other linker-folded "return 0"/"return 1" bodies hiding behind a plausible-sounding Lua name. The sentinel-value catalogue for "unknown input" answers keeps growing (255, `"Default"`, nil, `"#NETID#0"`, -1-forever) — a reimplementation guide should probably collect all of these into one table rather than leaving them scattered across 50+ spec sections.

**Crash-shaped findings, summary (all CONFIRMED code paths from the disassembly; reachability marked where not separately settled):** `hud_x_of_y_update` (fully unbounded slot index → out-of-bounds write into adjacent vtable objects or unmapped memory); `game_proto_select` (non-tranche neighbor; an invalid argument writes into the caller's own saved-register stack spill); `main_menu_matchmaking` (null dialog-pool-exhaustion write, narrow trigger); `los_check_do` (stuck-poll hazard when the request pool is exhausted or either object fails its kind check).

**Review status (2026-10-03):** all 25 names in tranche 19 resolved and written up (§54.1-§54.4); none failed. CONFIRMED unless individually marked HYPOTHESIS/OPEN above. Residual OPEN items: whether every object the generic resolver can return actually carries the kind bit `los_check_do`'s request creator requires (decides real-world reachability of its stuck-poll hang); the writer of the camera-position global the light-group attach pass reads; which two characters the "downed-interactable" template ids identify; whether activity-lock records are ever synchronized between co-op machines.

## 55. Ranking tranche 22 — 25 previously-unspecced Lua-bound names (2026-10-03)

**Source.** Job `D:\Project Crreish\TEAM A\ghidra\jobs\ranking\tranche-22.json` (names 476-500 of 554, Team B call-count order; full write-up in `review/exe-notes-2026-10-01/interp_ranking_tranche_22.md`). 11 `game_*` names in the UI helper registrar `0x00845aa0`; 14 names in the gameplay registrar `0x00a20840`. Every name is 1 call site in 1 script. No pointer-before-name registrar in this tranche. Addresses below are CONFIRMED — disassembly unless marked otherwise. This note's own agent was briefed on, and correctly avoided, the single-player-host-session inference mistake tranches 16/18 made; every session/host-gated function below is described as simply taking its no-session path in single player, per §8.27/§26.28, with no inference drawn.

### 55.1 Game-state and UI queries (8 functions, UI helper registrar)

**`game_is_german_build`, `game_is_demo`, `game_is_debug_reloading_level`** all resolve to the already-catalogued constant-false stub `0x00a3c670` (tranche 12's alias list already counted them; this note adds their body entries). **`game_event_tracking_interface_exit`** resolves to the shared no-op stub `0x007c9f50`; its sibling `game_event_tracking_interface_enter` is bound to a real, undumped function, so the pair is asymmetric — whatever "enter" does, "exit" does not undo it.

**`game_is_going_to_main_menu`** reads the game-state stack's *projected* top (the top after still-queued push/pop requests are applied, re-derived only when a "changed" byte is set) — projected state 2 → true; otherwise the *current* top is read, with 5 or 6 → false and anything else → true. So the binding answers false only while state 5 or 6 is on top and no switch to state 2 is queued; which concrete states 2/5/6 name (front end / loading screen, HYPOTHESIS) is OPEN. **Latent defect:** the projection routine replays the queued push/pop requests into a 16-dword stack buffer with no bound and no de-dup, unlike the real state pump it mirrors (which refuses pushes past 15 entries and pushes of an already-present state) — a long enough queue overflows that buffer. Reachability OPEN.

**`game_get_game_play_mode`/`game_get_pending_game_play_mode`** read a *separate* "game-play mode" global (unrelated to the game-state stack above, with its own four-entry name table: `"Activity"`/`"Diversion"`/`"Normal"`/`"Mission"`, file-default current = `"Normal"`) and push the **untranslated English identifier directly**, never a localized string; the pending mode pushes the literal `"None"` when no change is queued. The name-table index itself has no bound check (safe here — only internal code ever writes the index).

**`game_get_coop_ping`** reads the first non-local session member's machine record `+0xb200` (meaning/units OPEN) as an **unsigned** 32-bit value; with no session (single player, §8.27/§26.28) or no other machine it returns **0**.

**`game_format_int_to_string`** — **real precision and rounding defects.** The input number is round-tripped through a **single-precision float** before formatting, so integers above 2^24 (16,777,216) can print off by one or more (relevant near the $20,000,000 cash cap, tranche 20 §53.2); rounding is **floor**, not truncation (−1.5 prints "−2", unlike `get_world_income_dollars`'s truncation); out-of-range and NaN inputs print the literal **"-2,147,483,648"**. Formatting itself groups digits with a comma every three places, unconditionally (no locale). A call with no argument reads stale stack content, not a clean 0 (§55.5 M.1).

### 55.2 `game_cancel_mission` — three distinct crash paths

**Real crash-shaped function — three distinct, independently reachable crash paths, none null-checked.** Reads the active mission's in-progress type (already documented at §27.25); **type 4 (diversion)** cancels immediately with no confirmation dialog — localizes and shows a "diversion canceled" message, but the writes that clear the diversion singleton are unconditional, so if its own abort call happens to clear that singleton first (OPEN whether it does), the message-writing step then writes through a stale pointer at offsets `0x8`/`0x9`/`0xc`. **Every other type** opens a "cancel?" confirmation dialog instead (mission/activity/stronghold text selected by type, with a "zombie activity" variant), and this is where the three confirmed crash paths live:

1. **Null mission pointer.** Reached whenever the in-progress type is read as **−1** ("nothing in progress") or comes from a *pending* record while the active mission pointer is still null (the phase-6/7 case) — the dialog-opening code then dereferences that null mission pointer at offset `0xa0` unconditionally.
2. **Dialog pool exhausted.** The shared 4-slot dialog pool (§27.11) returns null when all four slots are already open; the binding stores into the result at offset `0x118` with no null check regardless. Trigger: call `game_cancel_mission` repeatedly before the player answers — each call opens a new dialog.
3. **Unhandled mission type.** Any in-progress type other than 0 (mission)/1 (activity)/3 (stronghold)/4 (diversion) falls to a default branch that still writes to offset `0x118` and reads offset `0x12c` with the dialog register never set; whether such types (e.g. 2) occur in shipped content is OPEN.

Each call also takes a game-pause reference before the dialog exists, with no confirmed release path on either confirm/cancel (OPEN — the result callback itself was not dumped). **Fix template:** test the mission pointer and the dialog pointer before use, and treat an unrecognized type like −1 (do nothing).

### 55.3 `game_audio_set_rtpc` (UI helper registrar)

Sets a Wwise RTPC (by name, resolved through the Wwise name hash, or by numeric id) to a float value on one specific playing-instance id — the same instance id `game_audio_stop` (§11.7) consumes, resolved through the same two lookups. Nothing happens unless both the instance id and the RTPC id are non-zero (the string `"none"` resolves to 0, making it a safe no-op). No crash shape — an unknown instance id fails cleanly. The RTPC is applied per-instance, not globally.

### 55.4 Forced combat actions (4 functions, gameplay registrar)

All four resolve a character name through the generic character resolver and drive the tranche 03 combat-action-entry (CAE) record. **`force_fire_do`/`force_fire_target_do`** resolve a target (navpoint-like, or object-kind depending on which of the two) and **commit CAE action 0 (`fire`) immediately** — unlike the throw bindings, they do not reset the staged action block first, so stale staged fields from an earlier suggestion can be committed alongside the new target, and there is no "busy" test, so a running action is simply overridden. **`force_throw_do`** only *stages* CAE action 4 (`throw grenade`, same pattern as `ai_suggest_action`) and requires the character to have a throwable item equipped/held; it is null-safe throughout.

**`force_throw_char_do` — real derived-pointer-before-null-test crash.** Computes `character + 0x40` as a position pointer for the target resolver **before** the character is null-checked. When the character name fails to resolve (unknown name, or a character that is already dead — the resolver rejects dead objects) that pointer is literally **address `0x40`**; if the target argument is `"#PLAYER#"` or `"#CLOSEST_PLAYER#"`, the special-name resolver measures every player's squared distance to that "position," reading address `0x40`. Any other target name is harmless. **Fix:** check the character for null before resolving the target — the order its own sibling `force_throw_do` already uses.

### 55.5 Other gameplay-registrar functions

**`follower_is_unconscious`** — **naming trap, opposite polarity from its sibling.** Tests the same "downed" state field `human_is_downed` (§7.13) reads, but through the character resolver that *rejects* dead objects — so a dead or misspelled-name follower reads as **unconscious (true)**, the opposite of `human_is_downed`'s **false** for an unresolved name. HYPOTHESIS: deliberate, so follower scripts treat a missing follower as needing attention.

**`flashpoint_start_mission`** starts a flashpoint by id both locally (sets two state globals, searches the world's flashpoint list by id — the *last* matching entry wins, id 0 matches anything with a non-zero marker field — hides its map marker, and suspends every other currently-active flashpoint) and remotely (an opcode-`0x43`/sub-code-`0x2a` broadcast whose receive handler runs the identical local-start routine on the peer). An id matching nothing still flips the "running" globals and still suspends every other flashpoint. In single player the broadcast simply does nothing (§8.27/§26.28). No crash shape.

**`flashlights_enable`/`flashlights_disable`** set one global byte (`0x0262e690`, confirmed to be the global itself, not a setter-function address, per the WALLS.md setter-vs-global rule) that the player-character flashlight update checks every frame; a world/mission reset routine clears the byte back to "enabled" independently. The switch is global (all characters) and purely local (no network record sent).

**`fade_get_percent`** — **naming trap.** Despite its name, it is a hard **0.0/1.0 step**, never an intermediate percentage: 0.0 only while the screen-fade state (§26.24) is fully-faded-in, 1.0 in every other state (fading in, fading out, fully faded out). A script polling it during a fade sees 1.0 until the very last frame.

**`dlc3_m03_punch_load`/`_unload`** load/unload a UI document (`"clones_m3"`, HYPOTHESIS the DLC3 mission-3 punch meter) by a bitmask argument (bit 0 = local, bit 1 = opcode-`0x43`/sub-code-`0x2f` broadcast to a matching receive handler). **Logic defect:** `_load` overwrites its stored document-id global without checking it was already set, so a second load — two script calls, or a local call racing the peer's own broadcast under the default mask — leaks the first document, which can then never be unloaded through this path.

**`dlc2_m02_clapboards_set`/`_get`/`_reset` — the tranche's headline finding: a real script-controlled arbitrary read/write.** `_reset` sets a count (clamped to at most 10, no lower clamp) and zeroes that many bytes of a 10-byte flag array. `_set`/`_get` take a **1-based** clapboard number, convert it to a zero-based index, and compare that index against the count — **as a signed value, with only the upper bound checked**. Any argument **≤ 0** produces a negative index: `_set` writes the byte **1** below the array, `_get` reads a byte below it. The most negative possible argument (−2^31) wraps the address computation to `0x827043b0`, so the full reachable range is every address in `0x00000000`-`0x027043af` and `0x827043b0`-`0xffffffff` — effectively the whole image. This is only blocked before the first `_reset` call (file-default count is −1, so every index fails the upper bound too). `_get` also returns **no value at all** (nil, not false) when out of range — a return-shape trap on top of the memory-safety issue. **Fix:** require `1 ≤ argument ≤ count` on both.

### 55.6 Cross-function observations

**M.1 — missing-Lua-argument semantics, settled.** Dumping the Lua stack-index resolver directly: a positive index maps to `base + 16·(index−1)` and returns the shared nil object once past the top of the stack, but an index counted from the top (as every argument read in this project's "count from the bottom" convention effectively is once the argument is missing) has **no bound check at all** — the first missing argument (index 0) reads whatever is at the stale top of the stack, and a **second** missing argument (index 1) re-reads the **first real argument's own value**. This settles `interp_lgdz.md`'s open missing-argument hypothesis (its two known cases were right; the argument-aliasing case is new) and affects every binding project-wide that reads an argument slot without first checking `lua_gettop`. Nil-gated reads (e.g. §55.4's `force_fire_*` arg 3) are unaffected, since they check the count first.

**Two unrelated "mode" systems.** The game-state stack `game_is_going_to_main_menu` reads (§55.1) and the game-play mode `game_get_game_play_mode` reads (§55.1) are separate globals with unrelated numbering — cancelling a diversion (§55.2) requests play-mode 2 ("Normal"), which is not game-state 2.

**Fire commits, throw stages** (§55.4) — the same immediate-vs-staged distinction `ai_suggest_action` already establishes (tranche 03), confirmed here for a second pair of binding families.

**Four more constant/no-op bindings** fully resolved in body (§55.1): three alias the constant-false stub `0x00a3c670`, one the shared no-op stub `0x007c9f50` — both already catalogued by tranche 12's alias sweep, but without body entries until now.

**Crash-shaped findings, summary (CONFIRMED structure unless marked OPEN):** `dlc2_m02_clapboards_set`/`_get` (signed index, no lower bound → arbitrary one-byte write/read, §55.5); `game_cancel_mission` (null mission pointer with nothing in progress or in phase 6/7; write to address `0x118` with the dialog pool exhausted; write to `0x118`/read of `0x12c` for an unhandled mission type, §55.2); `force_throw_char_do` (derived pointer computed before a null test, reachable with `"#PLAYER#"`/`"#CLOSEST_PLAYER#"`, §55.4); `game_is_going_to_main_menu`'s state-projection buffer overflow (reachability OPEN, §55.1).

**Review status (2026-10-03):** all 25 names in tranche 22 resolved and written up (§55.1-§55.5); none failed. CONFIRMED unless individually marked HYPOTHESIS/OPEN above. Residual OPEN items: the meaning of game states 2/5/6 and the four play-mode enter/leave callbacks; what the diversion singleton's own abort call does to the pointer `game_cancel_mission`'s diversion path then writes through unconditionally; which mission types other than 0/1/3/4 occur in shipped content, and what the cancel-confirmation dialog's result callback does on "yes"; the flashpoint record's marker/suspend fields; who re-enables flashlights automatically.

## 56. Ranking tranche 21 — 25 previously-unspecced Lua-bound names (2026-10-03)

**Source.** Job `D:\Project Crreish\TEAM A\ghidra\jobs\ranking\tranche-21.json` (names 451-475 of 554, Team B call-count order; full write-up in `review/exe-notes-2026-10-01/interp_ranking_tranche_21.md`). All 25 names live under the UI bring-up: 5 in the gang-customization registrar `0x0083a900` (tranche 20); 7 in the `game_` helper table `0x00845aa0`; 4 in the pause-options registrar `0x007e18e0` (tranche 10/17); 5 in the machinima registrar `0x00bc68a0` (tranche 12); 3 in the lobby registrar `0x007abbb0` (tranche 12); 1 (`game_proto_select`) in a **pointer-before-name one-name registrar** `0x00841020` — the same quirk tranches 13/16/18/19 describe (a `lua`-mode dump lands on `lua_setfield`; a `range` dump of the registrar's own bytes shows the real handler `0x00840fa0` pushed before the name). Addresses below are CONFIRMED — disassembly unless marked otherwise. No session inferences drawn; every session/host-gated function below takes its no-session path in single player per §8.27/§26.28.

### 56.1 Gang customization — 5 functions (registrar `0x0083a900`)

**The tranche's headline finding: every one of its five gang-customization bindings takes an unchecked index or an unchecked baseline into the sign/vehicle state** — combined with tranche 20's two names, all six index-taking rows of this registrar read so far are unchecked.

**`gang_customization_select_gang_sign` — two crash shapes.** Mode 0 previews a sign by list position with **no bound check at all** against the sign count — a script-controlled double arbitrary read (the position indexes a position-to-record map, then the record itself). **Mode 1 is a deterministic, non-data-gated null-pointer dereference**: it reads a pointer that, across an exhaustive write-census of its own global and every neighboring dword, is confirmed to be **written only as zero**, then calls through its vtable. Every mode-1 call crashes, full stop — the clearest crash in the tranche (whether the shipped script ever actually passes mode 1 is OPEN; Team B's own call-site data can settle it).

**`gang_customization_confirm_gang_sign` — unbounded index, persisted to the save.** Same unchecked list position as `select_gang_sign` mode 0, but here the out-of-range **record pointer itself is stored**, later dereferenced by the sign-list rebuild with no check, and **written into the save file as a truncated byte index** that the loader trusts unconditionally on the next load — so a single out-of-range call can corrupt a save slot that only manifests on the next session.

**`gang_customization_revert_gang_sign`** restores the sign recorded when the sign list was last built; if that list was never built, the restored pointer is null, deferring the same crash/corruption shape to the next list build and the next save (reachability HYPOTHESIS).

**`gang_customization_confirm_vehicle`/`gang_customization_revert_vehicle`** reconfirm tranche 20 §53's unbounded 3-slot array read/write, and add a **second, new crash**: if `revert_vehicle` runs before the vehicle "baseline" slot is ever set (zero-fill by default), it writes **null** into the slot and hands that null to the preview-vehicle spawner, which reaches a callee that reads the item's count/array fields at offset `0x24` with **no null check on its first argument** (its sibling call site from `…_show_vehicle` can reach the same null-item path). A third, lower-severity shape reconfirms tranche 20's unchecked UI-element-as-`this` call.

### 56.2 Video-recording options — 4 functions (registrar `0x007e18e0`)

Three of the four are the shared no-op stub `0x007c9f50`; the fourth is the constant-false stub `0x00a3c670`. Combined with tranche 12 B.1's two siblings in the same registrar, **all six `game_record_*` names are inert on PC** — three always report false, three do nothing — HYPOTHESIS: console video-capture features compiled out of the PC build. A reimplementation can bind the whole family to constants with no behavioral loss.

### 56.3 `game_` helper functions — 5 functions

**`game_use_imperial_units`** follows the **Windows user locale's measurement-system setting**, read once at boot via `GetUserDefaultLCID`/`GetLocaleInfoW` — there is no in-game option and no Lua setter; a reimplementation running under a different locale diverges here. **`game_steam_open_url`** opens an arbitrary script-supplied URL in the Steam overlay with no validation. **`game_steam_open_dlc_page_overlay`** opens the store DLC listing for the game's own Steam app id (55230, hardcoded). **`game_request_game_terminate`** is a **once-only exit latch** (never cleared — a second call does nothing) that queues a push of game mode 10 onto the pending-transition queue, silently dropped if that queue happens to be full.

**`game_pause_map_filter`** — **real wrong-arity-by-input-type defect.** Setting the filter (string argument present, non-nil, string-convertible) returns **0 values**; anything that falls through to the getter path (no argument, or a non-string-convertible type) returns **1 value** — so a caller passing the wrong argument type gets a return value it did not ask for. Separately, the setter does not respect a mission-imposed filter lock (ids ≥ 0x80): a script can silently override a locked filter with any of the eight public ones, with the lock only ever visible again through the getter (`"PFT_FILTER_LOCKED"`).

### 56.4 `game_proto_select` — reconfirms a non-tranche finding (one-name registrar `0x00841020`)

Re-read in full; **confirms tranche 19's finding stands**: an argument of 0, nil, or any non-number value writes a byte into the caller's own saved-register stack spill area, corrupting state the Lua C-call dispatcher depends on immediately after return. New refinement: with only two argument writes into a 3-byte local, the "nothing free" fallback branch is unreachable for valid 1-3 arguments, and the selection is deterministically "the lowest of 0/1/2 not named by either argument."

### 56.5 Machinima clips and recording — 5 functions (registrar `0x00bc68a0`)

**A shared path-builder defect underlies four real crash/data-loss shapes.** The file-path builder used by every machinima binding below **returns without writing its output buffer on any of its three failure exits** (process-token open, folder lookup, folder creation), and **no caller checks this** — each then passes an uninitialized stack buffer to `FindFirstFileW`/`CopyFileW`/`DeleteFileW` as a file path (environment-gated reachability). Separately, the UI-encoded-name decoder these bindings also share **writes nothing for a plain (non-UI-encoded) string**, producing the same uninitialized-buffer shape from ordinary script input, not just from a failing environment — this is the same defect tranche 12 already found in `game_machinima_playback_enter`, now confirmed to also hit `copy_clip`/`overwrite_clip`/`delete_clip`.

**`game_machinima_delete_clip` — the most severe instance: it can delete the wrong file.** With a plain (non-encoded) name, the decode buffer is never written, and **a file whose name is whatever garbage was already on the stack gets deleted** — confined to the clip folder in practice, but a stale buffer holding an earlier real clip name would delete that clip. The decoded name is also never sanitized against `..\`/path separators before the delete call. `game_machinima_copy_clip`/`_overwrite_clip` share the uninitialized-source-name shape and additionally **discard the `CopyFileW` result**, so the script cannot detect a failed copy. `game_machinima_record` **always resets first** (stopping/discarding any in-progress recording) before deciding whether to actually start, so calling it while already recording silently restarts and discards the previous take; a refusal to record is also silent, leaving the reset's side effects (radio unmuted, buffers freed) in place regardless.

### 56.6 Lobby and co-op — 5 functions

**`game_lobby_update_ready_state` — the binding's meaning changes by network role.** On a co-op client it only reports the local ready state; on the host (or with no session — the single-player path) setting ready **true** starts a countdown-script coroutine and setting it **false** cancels a pending start — genuinely different behavior behind one Lua call, with a paired callback (`"game_lobby_update_ready"`) whose own argument count also differs by role (one boolean on a client, two on a host).

**`game_lobby_horde_continue_from_wave`** reconfirms tranche 12's known inconsistency from the other side: it returns **0** for an invalid selected-map index (not a sentinel meaning "no progress"), the same value a naive `~= -1` check would misread as "continue from wave 0" alongside the already-documented **−1** ("nothing to continue") and **N ≥ 2** ("continue from wave N") cases. `game_kick_coop_player` performs an **immediate, host-only kick with no confirmation and no Lua callback** (unlike its sibling `game_coop_kick_player`, tranche 12), and shares that sibling's 256-character stack buffer formatted through the project's 1024-character-limit wide-sprintf wrapper — a data-gated overflow shape, reachable only with an unusually long remote persona name. `game_lobby_finished_loading` and `game_is_waiting_for_partner` resolve in full with no crash shape; the latter defaults to **true** ("waiting") whenever its backing session-ping object is entirely absent.

### 56.7 Cross-function observations

**The missing-Lua-argument aliasing finding (§55.6/M.1) is reconfirmed project-wide**, not newly found in this tranche — none of this tranche's unconditional-read arguments happened to be called with too few arguments in the dumps, but the same resolver semantics apply to every binding here that reads unconditionally.

**Same verb, two naming conventions, one project.** The machinima file family mixes UI-encoded names (`delete_clip`, the source of copy/overwrite) with plain registry tags (`clip_exists`, the destination of copy/overwrite) — passing the same Lua string to each means something different, and a reimplementation must preserve both conventions and the decoder's "write nothing for plain input" quirk that makes that distinction load-bearing.

**Growing sentinel-value catalogue (tranche 19 J.3's running list):** `game_lobby_horde_continue_from_wave` (−1/0/N≥2), `game_pause_map_filter` (`"PFT_FILTER_LOCKED"`, nil for an unlisted id, 0-or-1 return values by input type).

**Environment-derived behavior:** `game_use_imperial_units` (Windows locale) and the machinima clip folder (Windows Documents folder, redirectable) are both real divergence points for any reimplementation not running under the identical Windows environment.

**Crash-shaped findings, summary (CONFIRMED structure unless marked OPEN):** `gang_customization_select_gang_sign` mode 1 (deterministic null-vtable-call, not data-gated — the clearest crash of the tranche); `gang_customization_select_gang_sign` mode 0 and `…_confirm_gang_sign` (unbounded sign-list index — read and persisted-write respectively); `gang_customization_revert_vehicle` (null baseline reaching a null-unsafe callee, reachability HYPOTHESIS); `game_proto_select` (reconfirmed saved-register corruption, tranche 19); the machinima path-builder's unwritten-buffer-on-failure shape, shared by all five machinima bindings; `game_machinima_delete_clip`'s wrong-file deletion from uninitialized stack content.

**Review status (2026-10-03):** all 25 names in tranche 21 resolved and written up (§56.1-§56.6); none failed. CONFIRMED unless individually marked HYPOTHESIS/OPEN above. Residual OPEN items: whether the shipped script ever calls `select_gang_sign` with mode 1; what object the mode-1 pointer was meant to hold; the declared size of the sign position-to-record map; whether `revert_vehicle` can run before `show_vehicle`/`confirm_vehicle` in shipped UI flow; what the two `game_proto_select` arguments mean semantically; who fills the machinima tag registry and whether a discarded recording take is ever saved first; whether `game_lobby_update_ready_state`'s two tracked bytes are really synchronized between co-op machines; the identity of `game_is_waiting_for_partner`'s backing object.

## 57. Ranking tranche 23 — 25 previously-unspecced Lua-bound names (2026-10-03)

**Source.** Job `D:\Project Crreish\TEAM A\ghidra\jobs\ranking\tranche-23.json` (names 501-525 of 554, Team B call-count order; full write-up in `review/exe-notes-2026-10-01/interp_ranking_tranche_23.md`). 14 names in the gameplay registrar `0x0a20840`; 2 in the dialog registrar `0x007c5630`; 4 under a crib-purchase table `0x005f1fc0` **new to this series**; 5 more spread one-each across crib-garage/completion/main-menu/UI-helper/cinema-editor tables; 1 (`cell_playlist_save_list`) in the playlist registrar. Every name is 1 call site in 1 script; no pointer-before-name registrar this tranche. Addresses below are CONFIRMED — disassembly unless marked otherwise. No session inferences drawn; functions gated on session/host state below simply take their no-session path in single player per §8.27/§26.28. This tranche also corrects §23.19 and §25.23 in place (see those sections).

### 57.1 Dialog boxes — 2 functions (dialog registrar `0x007c5630`)

**`dialog_box_create_internal` — the tranche's most severe memory-safety finding: an unbounded copy into a fixed 64-byte field.** This 15-argument dialog builder copies its callback-name argument into a 64-byte slot field with **no length limit**: a name of 64+ characters overruns the field itself, and one of 68+ characters corrupts the **next dialog slot's** own ring-link fields (or, for the last of the four dialog slots, the first body-text pool block's own pointer and links) — a script-controlled heap-adjacent corruption reachable from ordinary Lua string arguments. The same function also reads its title/body/callback-name arguments **unconditionally with no null check**, crashing on a nil argument in any of the three, and reads the current Lua-thread coroutine context with no null check (crash only if called with no active script thread, which should not occur in normal use).

**`dialog_pause_unpause`** hides a script-openable pause display (or cancels a still-pending deferred show) by testing one byte written only by the matching opener; its hide path, like that opener's show path, writes into a Lua-hook-firing record with **no null check and no "hook exists" test** — the dialog manager's own close path (§57.1 above) shows the correctly-guarded form of the same write.

### 57.2 Cutscenes — 2 functions (gameplay registrar)
